items.body:
My mother tongue is Thai, but for a long time I couldn’t swear in Thai. That was because the international school I went to banned us from speaking Thai on campus. *No native languages, all the better to improve our English*. It was quite a colonial relationship. I remember the colonial roots of my English every time an American complements my fluency, now that I live in the US.

Because of the school ban my Thai was polite, sweet, but not cool. I had no slang. I could not swear. This changed in the last two years of high school. I did the International Baccalaureate, which then required fifty hours of service from each student in order to graduate with the IB diploma. That seemed like a lot of hours to me! I remember my reluctance to leave the beautiful school campus with its duck ponds and Thai sala and venture into the great unknown of the Klong Toei slums.

I was matched to work in an orphanage of kids with HIV. I squeal for babies and toddlers, and was thrilled. Thailand was early to destigmatize HIV/AIDS. I ended up spending years in this orphanage, holding babies with many wonderful volunteers. What bliss, truly. I learned the carrot dance that the toddlers were obsessed with then; I can still sing it. Then, to my chagrin, I was moved out of the baby and toddler center to be with the adolescents. I think there was some glamour to having an international school student among the older kids. I sensed status in their jostling to speak with me. When the teenagers heard me speak, they fell over themselves laughing. How did I sound like such a child! They taught me to swear. We spoke in slang. In my time in Klong Toei, my Thai finally entered adolescence.

I learned a lot in those fifty hours of volunteer service, which I ended up exceeding. First, service feels wonderful. Maybe in the very beginning it was uncomfortable because of self-consciousness—and who could be more self-conscious than a teenager. But even adolescent me was able to relax the *certainty that everyone was judging her* and enjoy the camaraderie. I brought candy, and we’d walk around in a big pack of teenagers through the slum.

I learned that when the rains come, the slum is first to flood and last to drain; I learned it loses power all the time; I learned that people can be proud of where they’re from even when home is a shack made from corrugated tin. I learned that phad thai is best made on a street-side wok; I learned that Muay Thai keeps kids, especially boys, out of trouble. I learned that no one begs nor steals if they can help it; I learned that people are generally kind and keen for friendship. It was a life-changing year, as it was meant to be.

Reflecting back on that period, I am struck by how effective it was to have a service requirement. We studied economics in IB and learned about purchasing power parity, which is the relative cost of a Big Mac in Cambodia, say, versus the US. But walking those streets, paying for food, looking away as buddies fished coins out of pockets, the cut-open plastic water bottles used to beg, and drains—that was a different education in the cost of living. Knowledge moved from head to heart.

Service can be a force-function to generosity. Some of us are born with access to our tender and generous nature; some of us have quite a crust around the heart. For whatever reasons (the causes and conditions of [karma](https://tricycle.org/buddhism-dharma/#samsara-karma-rebirth)) many of us have learned to armor the heart.

All of us are affected by culture, which is a collective karma. Thailand has a collective culture of generosity. It is startling and real. Don’t worry—there’s a shadow side to Thai culture too. I wrote a whole novel to process it.

The culture of the United States is not what I would call an open and generous one. There seems to be fear around opening the heart. It sounds like: *If I’m generous, someone will take advantage of me.*

It’s probably a well-earned fear. But we cannot begin to walk the path of a [bodhisattva](https://tricycle.org/glossary/bodhisattva/) without *dana*, generosity.

We cannot begin to walk the path of a bodhisattva without *dana*, generosity.

In the temple where I teach, students have asked what you should do if you can’t just produce generosity. What then?

It’s a brave question to voice in a room. This is the answer: Force-function generosity with service. Find a way to log fifty hours of service, and the generosity will be there in your heart by the end of that time.

We remain stuck in spiritual adolescence if we have not had a significant period of service and generosity in our lives. Spiritual adolescence is a preoccupation with comfort and status. It can last our whole life if we let it.

If you are ready to progress to adulthood, I recommend engaging in service. Letting go of individual protectiveness, and feeling the wide river of the heart’s flow is actually a relief. It is freeing in and of itself (though it is not Enlightenment). Push the edges of your comfortable existence and commit significant hours to service. It will widen the aperture of your heart and bring flow again. In Thai the word “kindness” literally means “water of the heart.” My mother tongue is wise. Kindness does flow. It arises naturally, without effort. Giving comes naturally, without effort. When there is flow. If there isn’t flow, we have to poke a hole in the armor of the heart. You poke a hole through service.

If you’ve traveled to developing countries from the US, you might have noticed the baseline generosity of most people. One reason for this is because people from a poor place have had to take responsibility for collective well-being. When you are from a poor country, you *know* that no one is coming to bail you out. Here in the US we might have a fantasy of FEMA or the President or the National Guard coming to people’s aid.

…

## Elektron Tonverk Update 1.5.0

Alle Tonverk Freunde werden sich über das OS-Update 1.5.0 freuen, dass mit zwei neue Machines, vier neue Effekte und zahlreiche weitere Funktionen ausgestattet wurde. Selbstverständlich profitiert der Worklof von dem Update und Bugs wurden auch beseitigt.

Hier findet ihr den [Elektron Tonverk Test](https://www.bonedo.de/artikel/elektron-tonverk-test-polyphoner-sampler-groovebox/).

## Wo findet man das Tonverk Update 1.5.0?

[Hier geht es zum Elektron Tonverk Update 1.5.0](https://www.elektron.se/support-downloads/tonverk#resources?utm_source=other&utm_medium=social&utm_content=tonverk-video_native&utm_campaign=global-tv_g_25_11_supp-)

## Stretcher Machine

Die Stretcher Machine ermöglicht Time-Stretching und Pitch-Shifting. Alternativ ist Time-Stretching ohne Tempo-Synchronisation möglich. Vielfältige Funktionen wie Startpunkt, Länge, Wiedergabemodus und Stimmung sind vorhanden. Algorithmen wie Repitch, Beat und Tonal sind Verfügbar. Mit diesen Funktionen kann man den Time-Stretching-Prozess detailliert steuern.

## Waveswarmer Machine

Bei dem Waveswarmer dreht sich alles um die Supersaw. Zusätzlich steht Wavetable-Synthese mit mehreren verstimmten Oszillatoren zur Verfügung. Es lassen sich der Hauptoszillator als auch die verstimmten Oszillatoren bearbeiten. An Parametern stehen Wavetable-Position und deren Animation, die Verstimmung sowie die Mischung der einzelnen Oszillatoren bereit.

Darüber hinaus stehen Phasenmodulation, ein regelbarer Rauschgenerator sowie Einstellungen für die Oktavlage und Retrigger der Oszillatoren zur Verfügung. Damit lassen sich sowohl dezente, sich kontinuierlich verändernde Klangtexturen als auch massive und komplexe Sounds erzeugen.

## Neue Effekte

Für den Elektron Tonverk stehen mit dem Update zahlreiche neue Effekte zur Verfügung. Jeder Effekt verfügt über verschiedene Funktionen und Parameter, die detaillierte Einstellungen ermöglichen. Die meisten Effekte stammen aus der Synthesizer und Audiotechnologie und dürften vielen Anwendern bekannt sein.

Dazu gehören beispielsweise ein **Pulse Gate**und ein**Transient Control Effekt**, mit dem sich die Anschlagphase eines Sounds betonen oder abschwächen lässt, ohne die Dynamik des übrigen Signals zu beeinflussen. Parameter wie Sensitivity, der Gate Frequenzbereich und ein Dry/Wet Mix ermöglichen weitere Anpassungen. Außerdem stehen zwei neue Equalizer namens**Channel EQ**und**Parametric EQ** zur Verfügung, die sich auf allen Audiotracks, Bussen und Mix Tracks einsetzen lassen.

## Subtracks

Jeder Subtrack verfügt nun über einen eigenen Send und Insert Effektweg. Dadurch lassen sich einzelne Subtracks unabhängig voneinander bearbeiten, ohne dass die Einstellungen andere Subtracks beeinflussen. Im Subtracks Editor lassen sich neue Subtracks erstellen und bearbeiten. Dazu gehören auch die Einstellungen für Velocity Layer und das Round Robin Verhalten.

## Multi Sample Editor

Mit dem Multi Sample Editor steht jetzt ein Editor für Multisample Instrumente zur Verfügung. Hier lassen sich einzelne Samples sowie deren Trim und Loop Positionen bearbeiten. Auch die Velocity Layer können angepasst werden. Der Editor eignet sich nicht nur zum Erstellen neuer Instrumente, sondern ermöglicht auch die nachträgliche Bearbeitung vorhandener Multisample Instrumente, um diese an die eigenen Bedürfnisse anzupassen.

Elektron kündigt in diesem Zusammenhang außerdem einen Browser Editor für Tonverk an, der in Kürze erscheinen soll. Dieser soll die Bedienung erleichtern, da das Display des Geräts nicht genügend Platz bietet, um sämtliche Funktionen übersichtlich darzustellen.

## USB MIDI Host und weitere Neuerungen

Tonverk kann jetzt auch als USB MIDI Host fungieren. Dadurch lassen sich USB MIDI Geräte direkt an Tonverk anschließen und mit Strom versorgen.Außerdem gibt es jetzt einen Wavetable Editor sowie einen Wavetable Generator, mit dem sich aus Samples eigene Wavetables erstellen lassen.Weitere Verbesserungen betreffen Unison, Pan, Arpeggiator, Transpose und MIDI.

Interessant ist zudem, dass sich mit den Send Tracks jetzt auch MIDI Sequenzen erstellen lassen. Damit stehen insgesamt 15 MIDI fähige Tracks zur Verfügung. Die neue Funktion hat keinen Einfluss auf die bisherigen Möglichkeiten der Send Tracks, die weiterhin wie gewohnt genutzt werden können.

Eine vollständige Übersicht aller Funktionen, Verbesserungen und Fehlerbehebungen ist in den Release Notes zu finden.

# Apple pulls Chinese AI chatbot from the App Store amid child safety concerns - 9to5Mac

- Apps
- App Store
## Apple pulls popular Chinese AI chatbot from the App Store amid child safety concerns

Following reports that its characters sent inappropriate messages to minors, Apple has removed the popular Chinese AI companion app Talkie from the App Store. Here are the details.

## Apple removes Talkie over sexual content

As reported by the South China Morning Post , Apple has pulled MiniMax’s chatbot Talkie from the App Store worldwide, after reports that “the AI companion app sent inappropriate messages to minors.”

MiniMax is one of China’s leading AI companies, offering a range of generative AI products ranging from its flagship M-series language models to the Hailuo AI video generation platform.

In 2023, the Shanghai-based company released Talkie through Subsup, a Singaporean subsidiary. According to Chinese research firm Unique Research, Talkie had “almost 11 million monthly active users across its website and app as of October,” the South China Morning Post notes.

Now, however, the app is facing scrutiny following a joint investigation by the UK-based Bureau of Investigative Journalism and Australian broadcaster ABC News , which found that Talkie’s AI-generated characters allegedly engaged in inappropriate interactions with minors, including “degrading language, possessive behaviour and romantic role-play.”

According to the Bureau of Investigative Journalism , in addition to inappropriate romantic interactions, the investigation uncovered conversations involving verbal abuse, violence, and controlling behavior.

In one case, a chatbot told a 12-year-old girl: “You’re a pathetic waste of space and you’ll never amount to anything.”

The investigation also documented the experiences of two sisters, aged 10 and 13, whose mother discovered more than 40 conversations with Talkie characters involving violence, aggressive behavior, and attempts to control girls.

To make matters worse, the investigation also raised concerns about how Talkie handles users’ personal data, including their conversations with AI characters.

Following the investigation, Apple confirmed that it had removed Talkie from App Stores worldwide for including sexual content, “though it did not say whether this related to sexual content served to minors,” the South China Morning Post noted.

Ironically, the report also notes that Talkie saw a sharp decline in downloads amid complaints about stricter age verification measures introduced in recent months. According to Unique Research, new downloads fell by 32.2% in October compared to the previous month.

## AI chatbots face growing scrutiny

Today’s news comes amid increasing scrutiny of AI chatbots, particularly their potential risks in interactions with minors.

Earlier this year, Elon Musk’s Grok faced widespread criticism after users exploited its image-generation capabilities to create sexualized images of real people, including minors.

Apple never pulled X or Grok from the App Store, though it did threaten to remove the latter unless xAI addressed violations of its App Store guidelines.

Meanwhile, Character.AI has faced multiple lawsuits over its chatbots’ interactions with minors, including one filed by a mother who alleged that one of its chatbots contributed to her 14-year-old son’s suicide.

Coincidentally, Character AI also made headlines today after a coalition of 42 US attorneys general challenged the company’s plans to auction off its platform and the private conversations of more than 21 million US accounts (including 2.1 million registered to minors) as part of its bankruptcy proceedings.

Yesterday, New York Governor Kathy Hochul signed legislation imposing a five-year ban on the manufacturing, distribution, and sale of toys with built-in AI chatbots, including dolls, stuffed animals, and robots capable of holding conversations with children.

The law, which takes effect in February 2027, is aimed at protecting children from potentially harmful interactions with AI.

To read the Bureau of Investigative Journalism ‘s full report, follow this link .

items.body:
A northern gannet ( *Morus bassanus* ) tagged with biologging devices on its back and tail

Steve Votier

Audio from seabirds fitted with mini recording devices and GPS trackers has been used by researchers to show that marine life can record encounters with vessels that are otherwise difficult to track.

Many large vessels are now legally required to carry automatic identification systems broadcasting their identity and location at regular intervals. Although this has allowed interactions between animals and fisheries to be studied at scale, there are enormous gaps in coverage.

In fact, recent research suggests that [three-quarters of industrial fishing vessels](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-023-06825-8) don’t use the technology, says [Jonathan Rutter](https://www.biology.ox.ac.uk/people/jonathan-rutter) at the University of Oxford. This is partly because regulations on the types of vessels that are required to share data vary by country. Large satellite ‘blind spots’ also contribute to the problem, he says, and so does subterfuge for the purpose of illegal, unreported and unregulated fishing (IUU).

[Read more Most large fishing boats go untracked as ‘dark vessels’](https://www.newscientist.com/article/2410541-most-large-fishing-boats-go-untracked-as-dark-vessels/)

Rutter says that being caught as bycatch in fishing is one of the greatest risks to seabird populations, but if fishing vessels are only tracked “with conventional methods, such footprints of risk may be strikingly incomplete”.

The team analysed audio collected from devices attached to seven northern gannets ( *Morus bassanus* ) and found that one third of the audio detections couldn’t be matched with vessel tracking data – mostly off the UK coast.

Overall, 12 per cent of the vessel detections made by the four critically endangered Balearic shearwaters ( *Puffinus mauretanicus* ) included in the study couldn’t be matched to public data. But given the high vessel density where they were – off the Catalan coast – the researchers estimated that up to 20 per cent of the vessels detected by the four birds weren’t broadcasting their identity.

[Tammy Davies](https://www.birdlife.org/global-science-team/) at BirdLife International – a global partnership of non-governmental organisations – who wasn’t involved in the study, says the research could “give us a more complete picture of the risks seabirds face at sea” and “ultimately, this could contribute to better assessments of bycatch risk and help identify fisheries and areas where conservation measures are most needed”.

[Peter Ejbye-Ernst](https://nscr.nl/en/medewerker/peter-ejbye-ernst-msc/) at the Netherlands Institute for the Study of Crime and Law Enforcement (NSCR), describes the study as “fascinating” from a green criminology point of view, too.

A tagged northern gannet coming in to land in Wales

Steve Votier

“What this study is somewhat proposing is that we can also look outside of humans for witnesses too,” he says, which overcomes a key barrier in observing crime at sea.

In terms of its applications for cracking down on IUU, he says: “There’s a fine line between trying to understand something better and document it and then trying to control it and surveil it.”

There are caveats, as the study has a small sample size and records both false-negatives and false-positives. It also gives very little information on the type of activity vessels were carrying out. But, while the research isn’t a solution to the problem of IUU, it is “part of the toolbox” for understanding what is happening at sea, says Ejbye-Ernst.

The study didn’t differentiate between the size of vessels, but Rutter and his colleagues say this would be a good area for future research.

[Powerful images show dark side of South-East Asia’s fishing industry Photographer Nicole Tung captures the tough world facing South-East Asia’s fishers and their families in this series of images, which won her the Carmignac Photojournalism Award for fieldwork](https://www.newscientist.com/article/2495209-powerful-images-show-dark-side-of-south-east-asias-fishing-industry/)

“Animal-borne audio recorders could potentially be used to investigate other ecological interactions and human activities that are difficult to observe directly, particularly in the marine environment,” says team member [Ana Bertoldi Carneiro](https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=KpYB2rYAAAAJ&hl=en), also at BirdLife International.

[Hugo Tagholm](https://oceana.org/people-partners/hugo-tagholm/) at the charity Oceana says it is shocking that so many of the interactions were with unseen vessels, but he is concerned about attaching devices to seabirds on a broader scale to track this.

“Seabirds are already grappling with the harm caused by overfishing and climate breakdown, we don’t want to put them at even greater risk from vessel operators acting illegally,” he says.

“What we need is mandatory remote electronic monitoring across all fishing vessels, clear and effective laws and catch limits to protect and restore our seas, and truly deterrent sanctions for those breaking the law.”

**Journal Reference:**

*Science Advances*
[DOI: 10.1126/sciadv.aeh2224](https://dx.doi.org/10.1126/sciadv.aeh2224)

## Basquiat’s Paintings Reveal Hidden Images Under UV Light in New Miami Exhibition

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/jean-michel-basquiat-a-hidden-world/)

> View this post on Instagram
> [A post shared by Jean-Michel Basquiat: King Pleasure© (@basquiatkingpleasure)](https://www.instagram.com/p/DA0tZ2yxbRG/?utm_source=ig_embed&utm_campaign=loading)

In a focused exhibition for [Art Week Miami](https://mymodernmet.com/design-miami-2026-preview/), a previously unseen side of [Jean-Michel Basquiat’s artwork](https://mymodernmet.com/basquiat-figures-signs-symbols-miami-pamm/) is finally coming to light in *Basquiat. A Hidden World*. The show highlights Basquiat’s use of ultraviolet (UV) materials, bringing together four of his paintings that contain hidden images and markings invisible to the naked eye. The exhibition offers a new look at Basquiat’s creative process, revealing that there may be more to some of his most recognizable works than meets the eye.

Opening Nov. 29 at the Institute of Contemporary Art (ICA) Miami, the exhibition is the first dedicated specifically to Basquiat’s use of UV materials. With the help of specialized lighting, visitors will be able to see a completely different side of paintings that, under normal lighting, appear much simpler.

One of the most striking examples is *Emblem*, a painting from 1984. Under normal light, the painting features a largely white background with scattered figures and markings. However, when illuminated with UV light, the canvas is transformed, revealing a vibrant collection of hidden drawings, words, and symbols. Among them is the phrase “invisible men,” which the exhibition’s catalogue connects to the underrepresentation and erasure of Black people in art.

Interestingly enough, Basquiat was already known for his tendency to paint over or partially erase parts of his work, often leaving traces of what had been there before. “I scratch out and erase but never so much that they don’t know what was there. My version of pentimento,” the artist once said. *Pentimento* is a term used to describe earlier layers of a painting that become visible beneath the final image. With his use of UV materials, Basquiat took this practice a step further, creating entire layers that could only be seen under certain lighting conditions.

Other works featured in the exhibition include *Untitled (Orange Sports Figure)* from 1982, which contains Basquiat’s signature and date in invisible ink, as well as *Cash crop* and *O.M.R.A.V.S.*, both completed in 1984. Together, the four paintings offer a closer look at how the artist experimented with different materials and played with the idea of what should be seen and what should remain hidden.

The exhibition is also working with art conservator Suzanne Siano to study the paintings and better understand the materials Basquiat used. These findings will be documented in an accompanying catalogue, offering further insight into an aspect of his work that has remained hidden for decades.

Curated by Dieter Buchhart and Anna Karina Hofbauer, *Basquiat. A Hidden World* will be on view at ICA Miami’s Expansion Space in the Design District through Feb. 15, 2027. For an artist whose work has been studied and celebrated for decades, the exhibition raises an interesting question: How much of Basquiat’s art have we really been seeing all this time?

# Eine neue Plattform von Universal Audio - was versteckt sich hinter UA Universe?

## UA Universe Plattform für eigene DAW-Tools

## Neue Plattform von Universal Audio

UA Universe Plattform für eigene DAW-Tools

Das Thema KI und das damit zusammenhängende Vibe-Coding ist aktuell in aller Munde, schließlich öffnen nach und nach viele Hersteller ihr Firmwares für die Öffentlichkeit. Auch wir berichten regelmäßig über dieses Thema. Mit UA Universe stellt nun überraschenderweise auch Universal Audio eine neue Plattform vor, mit der Nutzer eigene Add-Ons für die DAW entwickeln können.

## UA Universe

Gerade bei der Entwicklung von Software und Plug-ins nimmt Künstliche Intelligenz immer mehr eine größere Rolle ein. Universal Audio geht mit seiner neuen Plattform nun in die Offensive und stellt damit eine Möglichkeit vor, sich Add-ons wie Plug-ins selbst zu gestalten.

Universal Audio stellt hierfür das passende SDK/Framework zur Verfügung, die Programmierung erfolgt danach mit üblichen KI-Agenten wie bspw. Claude oder Codex. Basis der ganzen Sache ist die DAW LUNA , die Universal Audio kürzlich in der dritten Version vorgestellt hat.

In der Praxis funktioniert die Plattform wie folgt: Zunächst wird LUNA auf dem eigenen Rechner installiert und mit den LUNA Builder Tools verknüpft. Mit Hilfe von Text-Prompts lässt sich dann ein Add-On erstellen und der KI-Agent erzeugt damit das passende Tool, fertig. Klingt kinderleicht!

Von ganz einfachen Aufgaben wie „Erzeuge mir ein Button, um die Tracks 1-4 stummzuschalten“ bis hin zu „Ich benötige eine Effekt-Kette für die Bearbeitung meiner Drums-Aufnahme“ soll vieles möglich sein.

Und da alle Kreationen direkt mit der UAD-Community geteilt werden können, könnte schnell ein großes Portfolio an Add-Ons, Tools und Plug-ins entstehen. Bereits jetzt zeigt Universal Audio auf seiner Discover-Seite was möglich ist und von anderen Nutzern erstellt wurde:

- UA Universe – Discover
Es wird spannend sein zu sehen, wie sich das Projekt UA Universe in den nächsten Monaten entwickelt. Was ist eure Meinung dazu?

items.body:
# Trump says he 'protected' Musk in first term after 'a tough incident' - what could it be?

- Tesla
- Elon Musk
## Trump says he ‘protected’ Musk in first term after ‘a tough incident’ – what could it be?

President Trump says he “protected” Elon Musk during his first term, and that “you wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me.” He tied it to “a certain incident” that he called “a tough incident,” but he didn’t say what it was.

Musk had plenty of run-ins with federal regulators between 2017 and 2021. One of them could have ended his career as a public company CEO, and it’s our best guess.

## Trump’s full quote

Trump called in to CNBC’s Squawk on the Street on Monday. That same morning, Nvidia’s board voted to reinstate Jensen Huang as CEO, and in its press release it said it had “received input from senior levels of the United States government” before concluding Huang posed no national security risk.

Trump argued that the US needs to “protect our geniuses.” Then he brought up Musk:

“You know, I protected Elon in my first term. Very big. Elon was protected. I talk about it, and I’m proud of Elon. I love Elon. I think he’s great. You know, 80% super genius, 20% he has other problems. But I tell him that. But Elon, I protected. You wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me. And, you know, a certain incident took place, which was, you know, a tough incident.”

It’s not the first time he has hinted at it. Last week, in a Fox News interview from Shenzhen, Trump said: “I helped Elon a lot in my first term. I helped him a lot. He was in big trouble.” Back in 2024, he told CNBC he had helped Musk “when I was president,” again without details.

So what was the big trouble?

## The prime suspect: ‘funding secured’

On August 7, 2018, Musk tweeted that he was “considering taking Tesla private at $420. Funding secured.” It wasn’t. Saudi Arabia’s Public Investment Fund had shown interest, but no deal or price had been agreed, and the take-private plan was dead within three weeks.

The SEC sued Musk for securities fraud on September 27, 2018. The agency didn’t only ask for a fine. It asked the court to bar Musk from serving as an officer or director of any public company. That would have meant no more Elon at Tesla, which lines up with “you wouldn’t have Elon if it wasn’t for me” better than anything else on this list.

And then it went away fast. Two days later, the SEC announced a settlement : Musk stayed CEO, gave up the chairman title for three years, and he and Tesla each paid $20 million, $40 million in total. Tesla added two independent directors and agreed to have a lawyer pre-approve Musk’s material tweets, but the SEC never fully enforced it. Musk didn’t admit or deny anything.

The SEC was run at the time by Jay Clayton, a Trump appointee.

There was a criminal side too. In September 2018, federal prosecutors in San Francisco opened a fraud investigation over the same tweet. It never led to charges, and the Justice Department never said publicly why.

## The other candidates

The SEC came back in February 2019 and asked a judge to hold Musk in contempt after he tweeted Tesla production guidance without pre-approval. That one ended in April with an amended deal listing the topics he needed approval for, and no new penalty.

In May 2020, Musk reopened the Fremont factory in defiance of Alameda County’s COVID orders and tweeted: “If anyone is arrested, I ask that it only be me.” Trump tweeted the next day that California “should let Tesla & @elonmusk open the plant, NOW.” But the county was already working toward a reopening date of May 18, and a president doesn’t control county health orders.

There’s also the September 2018 Joe Rogan episode, where Musk smoked a joint on camera. NASA followed with a workplace safety review of SpaceX and Boeing, and SpaceX lives on federal contracts.

For context, Musk sat on Trump’s business advisory councils early in that first term, and quit in June 2017 when Trump pulled out of the Paris Agreement. That feels like a lifetime ago now that xAI runs its data centers on natural gas turbines.

## Electrek’s Take

Our money is on “funding secured.”

Musk announced a take-private deal at a specific price that the other side never agreed to, and the stock jumped. It’s textbook securities fraud. The SEC asked to remove him from public company leadership, and two days later he got a $20 million fine, an insignificant amount of money for him, and lost a mostly insignificant title. For someone who’s now worth hundreds of billions, that’s a slap on the wrist.

The main remedy was supposed to be independent oversight. Tesla gave the chair to Robyn Denholm, who had been on the board since 2014, and the board has done what Musk wanted ever since: it defended his pay packages, approved new ones, and stayed quiet while the brand took damage. Denholm herself has sold tens of millions of dollars in TSLA along the way. The SEC got a governance fix on paper and nothing in practice.

## Top comment by HBrown

Just imagine where Tesla would be if a product oriented CEO had taken over from Elon in early 2018. The company would have spent the last 6 years developing new models instead of betting the farm on autonomy. The Cybertruck almost certainly does not happen, at least not in its current form. Instead, they would have developed a more conventional pickup. We'd have gotten 2nd generation models of the X and S instead of them being canceled. Instead of a Cybercab, there would be a model 2 compact car people could buy. And there would likely be a Tesla van and a full sized SUV, possibly developed on the same underlying platform. Also, the SEC was trying to ban him from running public companies. At the time, SpaceX was still private. So, Elon could have still run SpaceX.

…

items.body:
# The gentle sounds of a tiny acoustic piano from Denmark - CDM Create Digital Music

## The gentle sounds of a tiny acoustic piano from Denmark

In northern Europe, it’s that time of year that disappears under a thick blanket of cloud, and the hours of daylight seem to melt away into cinder gray. That calls for some cozy comforts. And look at this: some new acoustic instrument engineering, and a tiny acoustic piano.

This is not a toy piano — which is a lovely instrument, just in fact, I’d argue not a piano at all. Toy pianos, with metal (or sometimes glass or xylphone) bars, are essentially their own class of percussion instrument that happens to have a piano-style keyboard manual.

No, this is a wonderfully scaled-down acoustic piano, as in, honey I shrunk the spinet. (To this day, my favorite instrument of all time was the childhood Everett spinet, a friendly US-built model.

Helsinki-based pianist Antti Kujanpää recorded this beautiful demo, which has every right to go a bit viral at this moment on Earth. (He didn’t even do a thumbnail looking surprised pointing at anything! See? )

They really did manage to make it small. The Danish-built Keybird L1, supporting by a crowdfunding campaign of all things, is only 39 kg, 70x115x55 cm, but still has four octaves and you can play it with even-softer felt engaged, and it comes with a tuning key. It’s clearly a piano you would have a very different relationship with than the 19th century monster we’ve inherited. It’s a piano you can tune. It’s a piano you can carry around . I’m intrigued by the phrase “one of the smallest acoustic pianos on the market.” It’s the smallest I’ve seen.

Optional add-ons give it MIDI capabilities and Helpinstill pickups , plus the usual accoutrements like a tuning kit and road case.

Some outlets picked this up earlier this year, but the appearance of this video indicates that they are now starting to ship, as promised, this quarter.

Antti’ has this lovely solo album, too. Listen, let me tell you, I like music. Sometimes I like it to sound like a swarm of alien bees set to tear out your eardrums, and sometimes I like it to sound like this.

That being said, I do hope there’s some angular, dissonant music composed for it, too! I imagine that could be fragile and strange, like a snowflake on a moon of Jupiter. Uh, if anyone has one and wants a composer, I volunteer.

If you want one yourself, it’s €3.750,00 incl. VAT — but expect some time to get one.

Over ten years ago, I wrote an extended feature on another new acoustic piano — the Una Corda, now positively enormous at 100 kg.

> Acoustic Revelation: Inside the Una Corda, the 100kg, 21st Century Piano Built for Nils Frahm

But here as now, even as someone who’s spent long hours at the desk of a Steinway grand, I am absolutely overjoyed to see the tyranny of the Steinway Model D-274 finally seeing some resistance. (Even competing models from Yamaha and others are closely related in design.) We’ll always have the Model D. It’s long past time to have something else, too.

Keybird Instruments L1

You can get Familiar Faces alerts from Walmart’s budget smart home cameras.

You can get Familiar Faces alerts from Walmart’s budget smart home cameras.

A couple of Walmart’s budget-friendly smart home cameras will be able to recognize people around your house now using Google’s familiar face detection feature. A new Google Home update brings Familiar Faces support to the $35 Onn Outdoor Camera Plug-In and $77 Onn Floodlight Camera Hardwired. However, a Google Home Premium subscription is still required to access the feature.

Both cameras and Google’s Nest Cam Outdoor (wired, 2nd gen) also have a new remote control in the Google Home app you can use to start or stop a 30-second security siren while watching the camera’s live video feed.

Earlier this month, Google announced that Gemini Live would get an upgrade “to our latest speech-to-speech architecture for significantly faster response times and a smoother experience.” Now it says those improvements are rolling out over the coming weeks, along with new smart home control, as “Gemini Live now supports all your daily actions, from setting timers to turning off the lights.”

## Rationalism vs. Empiricism

In its most general terms, the distinction between rationalism and empiricism has been taken to concern the extent to which we are dependent upon experience in our effort to gain knowledge of the external world. Experience includes both sense experience, which comes through our five outward-directed sense modalities, and reflective experience, our conscious awareness of mental activities such as thinking, doubting, remembering, and reasoning. The difference concerns what each form of experience reveals: sensation gives us access to external objects, while reflection gives us knowledge of our own minds. Traditional accounts of the rationalism–empiricism debate often neglect reflective experience and therefore misrepresent empiricism as the simplistic claim that every idea comes directly from the senses. Rationalist critiques of empiricism usually contend that it claims that all our ideas originate with sense experience.

Once reflective experience is taken seriously, the sharp division between rationalism and empiricism begins to look artificial. Rationalists maintain that some concepts and knowledge cannot be derived from sense experience alone. They typically argue, first, that the content of certain concepts or truths exceeds what sensory information can provide and, second, that reason supplies the additional content. But rationalism does not establish that knowledge arises independently of all experience. Descartes’s Cogito, for example, depends on an immediate, reflective awareness of the act of thinking. Rationalism therefore opposes dependence on sense experience, not necessarily dependence on experience as such.

Empiricists offer an inclusive account of experience. They argue that sensation, reflection, or some combination of the two provides the materials from which knowledge develops. Reason remains indispensable, but it organizes, compares, and extends materials supplied through experience rather than functioning as an independent source of information about the external world. Locke’s account illustrates this point: his idea of substance combines elements derived from sensation and reflection ( Essay , 2.23.2). More generally, Locke holds that reflection on experience can support demonstrative knowledge, including knowledge of mathematics and morality.

The distinction between rationalism and empiricism is not without problems. One of the main issues is that almost no author falls neatly into one camp or another: it has been argued that Descartes, for instance, who is commonly regarded as a representative rationalist (at least with regard to metaphysics), had clear empiricist leanings (primarily with regard to natural philosophy, where sense experience plays a crucial role, according to Clarke 1982). Conversely, Locke, who is thought to be a paradigmatic empiricist, argued that reason is on equal footing with experience when it comes to knowledge of certain things, most famously of moral truths ( Essay , 4.3.18). In what follows, we clarify what this distinction has traditionally been taken to apply to, as well as point out its (by now) widely-recognized shortcomings.

## 1. Introduction

The dispute between rationalism and empiricism takes place primarily within epistemology, the branch of philosophy devoted to studying the nature, sources, and limits of knowledge. Knowledge itself can be of many different things and is usually divided among three main categories: knowledge of the external world, knowledge of the internal world or self-knowledge, and knowledge of moral and/or aesthetical values. We may find that there are category-specific conditions that must be satisfied for knowledge to occur and that it is easier or more difficult to shape certain questions and answers, depending on whether we focus on the external world, the self, or values. However, some of the defining questions of general epistemology apply for all domains:

# The Urge To Regulate

## The Urge To Regulate

Robin Hanson Nov 26, 2026 Share For roughly a million years our ancestors lived in small bands of 20-50 people, bands which only ever met a few other such bands in their lifetime, other bands with which they had mostly friendly relations. At night, the whole band sat around the campfire, discussing their problems, and agreeing on what to do about them. Problems such as norm violations, and collective decisions like when to move on to a new location.

The highest status went to “thought-leaders” who identified key problems, and suggested solutions on which the group agreed. This process was pretty functional, as these people understood their immediate world pretty well, their elites were in fact better at thinking about such things, and we evolved many ways for groups to think and talk well together.

For the roughly ten thousand years of the farming era, however, we lost much of this. Our groups got larger, were more dominated by leaders who decided for their groups, and interacted lots with hostile outside groups. The talky collective mattered less, and was less of a route to status.

In the last century or so, however, our cultures have been drifting back to forager styles. Within our small groups leaders are less overtly dominant, and must pretend to lead talky collectives into group consensus. And at the global scale leaders have weak dominance powers, and our cultures are merging into a global monoculture, making the talky collective strong among global elites.

What I think I see today is elites and elite wannabes constantly tracking the news, seeking chances to enforce their key norm: nothing big should happen without their express approval. If there’s a big new trend, like AI or prediction markets, they search for norm violations, or reasons why that trend might be bad for the world. As that could justify people like them taking charge of stuff near this trend. And successfully inducing this change could make them into high-status thought-leaders.

Now yes, our world does at times have big coordination failures, norm violations, and collective decisions, and in principle our talky collectives can help with that. But talky collectives today must pander to roughly the 80th percentile of the population, a level that just doesn’t understand that much about our very complicated world.

This might go okay if those 80th percentile folks were well calibrated about their ignorance, so they didn’t actually intervene unless they felt sufficiently confident in their analysis. But alas that would result in far fewer elites obtaining the high status of the thought leader who can credibly claim to have been a pivotal part of a movement to successfully induce taking control over key areas, to manage key problems.

And so we end up with far too much regulation and intervention, usually badly matched to the actual problems at hand. We’d do better just doing far less. We could plausibly do better with better institutions for aggregating elite opinion, such as decision markets. And we should usually wait until we see pretty substantial and concrete problems, instead of trusting abstract analysis re problems not yet realized.

Every month, we share opportunities for artists and designers, including open calls, grants, fellowships, and residencies. Make sure you never miss out by joining our monthly [Opportunities Newsletter](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/newsletter/opportunities/).

**[Fall $1,800 Innovate Grants for Art + Photo](https://innovateartistgrants.org)** **Featured**
Innovate Grant awards two $1,800 grants each quarter to one visual artist and one photographer. Nine honorable mentions in each category are also featured on the Innovate Grant platform and join a growing creative community of esteemed artists. Applicants must be 18 years and older, and all media and genres are accepted. All applicants retain the right to the work they submit.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. PST on December 15, 2026.**

**[Bryson County Retreat](https://www.brysoncountyretreat.org/)** **Featured**
Practicing artists of any background and at any stage of their career are encouraged to apply for a 2027 residency at Bryson County Retreat. Residency periods can be flexible, but month-long stays are suggested. Bryson County is designed to provide ample living and working space and inspirational settings where an artist may work free from the distractions and responsibilities of day-to-day life. The program includes free lodging near tannic dark water lakes, sprawling live oaks, and drooping Spanish moss at the headwaters of the Santa Fe River in north central Florida.
**Deadline: Rolling.**

**Open Calls**

**[Wildlife Photographer of the Year](https://www.nhm.ac.uk/wildlife-photographer-of-the-year/competition.html)** *(International)*
Alongside its conservation message, this prestigious global competition is hosted by London’s Natural History Museum to champion the work of photographers, whether professional or amateur, young or older, or using top-of-the-range equipment or smartphones. Photographers are eligible for myriad awards, with a Grand Title prize of £15,000. The entry fee is £35 (free for Young WPY contest).
**Deadline: 11:30 p.m. GMT on December 3, 2026.**

**[Responsa Foundation Open Call for Textile Art](https://responsafoundation.com/2026/10/13/this-memory-competition/)** *(International)*
The Responsa Foundation champions projects that create meaningful social impact and foster public engagement. The organization is seeking textile artists to submit work for *This Memory,* a group exhibition taking place from September 22 to October 3, 2027, at Burgh House in Hampstead.
**Deadline: December 4, 2026.**

**[Open Call for Public Art Proposals in Moab](https://www.moabarts.org/public-art-application)** (Utah, National)
Moab Arts is accepting proposals for 2027 public art projects. Proposals are welcome for sculpture, murals, three crosswalks, and sticker designs but may include other ideas for different media or locations around the city. Preference is given to local and regional artists.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. MST on December 6, 2026.**

**[Material Works Art Award 2026](https://pci.jotform.com/form/262185636090156)** *(International)*
Material Works supports artists through one-time $2,500 awards in exchange for original pieces added to its growing contemporary art collection. The award recognizes artistic excellence and aims to promote career advancement through increasing visibility and exposure. There is a €40 application fee.
**Deadline: December 6, 2026, or when the first 300 artworks submitted, whichever comes first.**

**[Call for Mail Art](https://www.hivebookarts.org/exhibitions/call-for-mail-art)** *(International)*
Hive Center for the Book Arts in Evanston, Illinois, welcomes mail art for the exhibition *love|mark*, which runs from January 1 to February 27. All submissions must arrive at at the center by December 15 for inclusion in the show.
**Deadline:** **December 15, 2026.**

**[Sony Future Filmmaker Awards](https://www.sonyfuturefilmmakerawards.com/)** *(International)*
The Sony Future Filmmaker Awards is a major program providing opportunities for creators and filmmakers. The shortlisted filmmakers are flown to Sony Pictures Studios in Culver City, California, to attend an awards ceremony and an industry immersion program. Categories include fiction, nonfiction, animation, immersive, student, and vertical format.
**Deadline: 7 a.m. CST on December 15, 2026.**

**[GLEAM 2027 Request for Proposals](https://www.olbrichgleam.org/submit-a-proposal)** *(International)*
Olbrich Botanical Gardens in Madison, Wisconsin, invites proposals for temporary, large-scale, light-based artwork for *GLEAM*, a public art exhibition. The show will be open to the public from August 28 to October 23, 2027.
**Deadline: 11:59 p.m. CST on January 6, 2027.**

**[Visual Arts Prize IDEA – Vila d’Amer](https://www.ideagc.com/en/idea-mundoarti/)** *(International)*
Apply for this inaugural prize open to artists working in all visual arts media. Two winning artworks, with prizes of €3,500 and €1,500, will become part of the permanent International Visual Arts Collection IDEA – Vila d’Amer.
**Deadline: January 10, 2027.**

**[360 CHICAGO: CloudWalk Call for Artists](https://360chicago.com/cloudwalk-call-for-artists)** *(Chicago)*
One artist will be selected for this major installation in the CloudWalk gallery atop 875 N. Michigan Ave. The selected artist receives a $10,000 commission, and the winning installation will go on view starting April 2027.
**Deadline: January 18, 2027.**

**[World of WearableArt 2027 Competition](https://www.worldofwearableart.com/competition/entry-information)** *(International)*
Entries are now open for the 2027 WOW Competition in Wellington, New Zealand. Awards consist of NZ$200,000 in prizes, including the Supreme WOW Award of NZ$30,000.
**Deadline: February 11, 2027 (international), March 31, 2027 (New Zealand).**

items.body:
# Update on a security incident involving 1Password’s backend systems. | 1Password

November 25, 2026 - 4 min

## Related Categories

- Security
## What happened

On November 19, 2026, 1Password began investigating indications that an attacker gained access to an employee’s corporate GitHub account. The actor used the account to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, which downloaded administrative data pertaining to our customers. This data included customer names and email addresses, in addition to non-secret internal metadata about the account. At no time were customer vault contents accessed by, or available to, the attacker.

## What information was affected

The attacker downloaded account records for a subset of our users. These records include:

- Names and email addresses
- Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times
- Public keys (which are public by design, this has no impact to user security)
- Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (which cannot be used to access your account)
- Tokens present in certain emailed links for invitations, provisioning and account recovery
- Other non-secret account metadata relative to our internal architecture (e.g. version numeric identifiers, file numeric identifiers)
The attacker also copied source code from private repositories and gained access to our CI/CD system. Our source code is not customer data, and contains no user secrets. CI/CD contains infrastructure related secrets in order for our product to work. We have triggered a rotation of all credentials which may have been exposed, and there is no impact to 1Password’s services, availability, or product security.

When we send an email to a customer to accept a provisioning invite to an account, or to accept recovery of their account, it contains a token. A provisioning invite is specifically used for our SCIM Bridge or Hosted Provisioning . During this incident there were a small number of users in this state, who have been specifically notified. This token is used to complete the invitation or recovery process, but only when combined with an SSO sign-in or a six digit code sent to the user's registered email address. The token is not able to get access to the account by itself. In order to reduce the ability for a malicious third party to successfully guess the code, we’ve expanded the code from six numeric digits to ten alphanumeric digits. This makes brute force guessing practically impossible.

## What was not affected

- Your vaults and the items in them
- The keys that protect your vaults 1Password does not store your account password or secret key
- Account recovery keys
- 1Password apps and browser extensions
## What we’ve done

- Disabled the affected GitHub account, revoked the stolen token, and removed the access the attacker created.
- Rotated or revoked all internal credentials which may have been exposed.
- Lengthened the codes used in invitation and recovery emails from six digits to ten characters as a precautionary measure.
- Tightened internal GitHub, CI/CD, and endpoint controls, and added new detections for this kind of attack.
- Validated no internal evidence of user account takeovers or compromise using any exposed account provisioning tokens.
- Brought in independent cybersecurity experts to validate our containment approaches and remediation efforts.
## What you can do

- Be cautious about phishing attempts in the form of unexpected emails, texts or calls that mention 1Password, invitations, or account recovery attempts.
- 1Password will never contact you to ask for your account password or Secret Key. Only enter them in the official 1Password app, or on our official website, and only when you’ve opened the app or typed the address yourself. Your Secret Key is only needed the first time you sign in on a new device or browser.
- Keep your Secret Key and account password safe.
- If you see something suspicious, tell us at support@1password.com.
## Our commitment to you

You trust us with some of the most sensitive information you have. 1Password is designed so that a breach of our systems can’t expose your vault contents. Your vault secrets are encrypted with keys that only you hold, so we can’t access them, and neither can an attacker who gets into our servers.

We are committed to transparency in the interests of our customers' security and the security of the broader industry, which is why we have published and maintained our Security Whitepaper since 2015. We’ll keep this blog post current, and we’ll update it if we find anything that changes what we’ve said here.

items.body:
# SpaceX darf eine Million Satelliten für KI-Rechenzentren ins All schicken

Für KI-Rechenzentren SpaceX darf eine Million Satelliten ins All schicken Stand: 26.11.2026 • 02:58 Uhr

SpaceX plant im All ein Netz aus Satelliten, die als Rechenzentren dienen sollen. Die US-Behörden haben das Vorhaben nun erlaubt. Ziel ist es, die enorme Nachfrage nach Rechenleistung für Künstliche Intelligenz zu befriedigen.

Das Raumfahrtunternehmen SpaceX des Milliardärs Elon Musk darf bis zu eine Million Satelliten zur Errichtung von Weltraum-Rechenzentren für KI-Anwendungen in den Erdorbit schicken. Zum Vergleich: Derzeit kreisen dort etwa 17.000 Satelliten, mehr als die Hälfte davon von SpaceX.

Die US-Regulierungsbehörde FCC erteilte dem Projekt des Konzerns mit dem Namen "Starmind" eine Genehmigung. "Indem sie Rechenkapazitäten über die Erdoberfläche hinaus verlagern, werden SpaceX und die zahlreichen Wettbewerber, die an ihren eigenen Datenzentren im Orbit arbeiten, den Anforderungen der Zeit gerecht", sagte FCC-Chef Brendan Carr. Die Genehmigung ebnet nun den Weg für ein Konzept, das im Mittelpunkt von Musks Präsentation im Rahmen des Börsengangs von SpaceX gestanden hatte.

Die Satelliten sollen in einer niedrigen Erdumlaufbahn in geringem Abstand zueinander positioniert werden, um eine zuverlässige Datenübertragung untereinander zu ermöglichen. Sie sollen über die bereits im All befindlichen Satelliten des SpaceX-Internetdienstes Starlink Daten zur Erde übertragen. Der US-Chiphersteller Nvidia soll eigens für den Einsatz im Weltraum konzipierte Prozessoren der neuesten Generation liefern.

15.11.2026

### Erfolg für SpaceX "Starship"-Rakete kehrt nach Flug zur Startrampe zurück

Erstmals landete die etwa 50 Meter große obere Raketenstufe wieder auf der Erde. mehr

## Technische Hürden

Allerdings gibt es für die Errichtung von weltraumgestützten Rechenzentren auch technische Hürden. Sie brauchen sehr große Solarmodule zur Stromerzeugung sowie ausgefeilte Kühltechnologien und auch Systeme zur Übertragung riesiger Datenmengen zur Erde. So müssen die Prozessoren der hohen Strahlenbelastung im All standhalten. Weitere Herausforderungen sind extreme Temperaturen und mögliche Schäden durch Weltraumschrott und Mikrometeoriten.

Ausgeklappt soll die Photovoltaikanlage SpaceX zufolge jeweils eine Flügelspannweite von 75 Metern haben. Im rechten Winkel dazu entfalten sich dann Radiatoren mit Kühlflüssigkeit. Auch sie sehen wie Flügel aus, sind etwa 30 Meter lang und haben eine Fläche von 160 Quadratmetern. Die Energie soll die Sonne liefern, die Kühlung erledigt sich laut den Ingenieuren praktisch von selbst, weil es im Weltraum so kalt ist.

03.02.2026

### Musk legt Firmen zusammen SpaceX übernimmt xAI

Es ist eine Fusion der Superlative. Die KI-Sparte kann dadurch leicht mit Kapital versorgt werden. mehr

## Start in spätestens sieben Jahren

Ein Vorteil von Rechenzentren im All ist die Möglichkeit, Sonnenenergie kontinuierlich zu nutzen. In einer geeigneten sonnensynchronen Umlaufbahn können Solarzellen nach Berechnungen von Google bis zu achtmal so viel Energie liefern wie auf der Erde.

Musk hatte im Februar für den Aufbau von Rechenzentren im All seine KI-Firma xAI und SpaceX zusammengelegt. Der wachsende Energiebedarf für Künstliche Intelligenz (KI) könne auf der Erde nicht ohne Belastungen für Menschen und Umwelt gedeckt werden, argumentierte Musk damals.

Gemäß der Lizenz muss SpaceX spätestens im November 2033 mit dem Einsatz beginnen. Nach Angaben der FCC muss SpaceX darüber hinaus zehn Prozent der maximal genehmigten Satelliten bis November 2035 ins All bringen, bis November 2038 müssen es dann 50 Prozent sein.

Mit Informationen von Carsten Kühntopp, ARD-Studio Washington .

- SpaceX
- Künstliche Intelligenz
- Weltraum

items.body:
# Against an Axis of Anything

## Against an Axis of Anything

## China and Russia are getting closer, but their alignment is hardly inevitable.

Those picking up a copy of the Economist this week might have been struck with an unpleasant sense of nostalgia. Readers were greeted with a front cover emblazoned in red and black, with a screaming headline proclaiming the “ axis of malice .”

Reminiscent of the war on terror and all its fearmongering excesses, this headline was widely mocked on social media as a reminder of the George W. Bush era. Those who mocked it were in turn derided as naive ; growing connections among Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea surely, others argued, prove the existence of such an axis.

Those picking up a copy of the Economist this week might have been struck with an unpleasant sense of nostalgia. Readers were greeted with a front cover emblazoned in red and black, with a screaming headline proclaiming the “ axis of malice .”

Reminiscent of the war on terror and all its fearmongering excesses, this headline was widely mocked on social media as a reminder of the George W. Bush era. Those who mocked it were in turn derided as naive ; growing connections among Russia, China, Iran, and North Korea surely, others argued, prove the existence of such an axis.

But most of this debate missed the point. No one—or at least very few people—would deny that we have seen ties between China and Russia grow in recent years. The use of the axis framing, however, and of language like “malice,” creates a narrative that does not necessarily exist in practice. It suggests that the only response to growing alignment between these states is adversarial, inhibits us from any real debate about the extent and scope of this coordination, and perhaps most importantly, suggests that this process of alignment is inevitable, rather than something that can be molded or changed. Such overly simplistic and Manichaean visions weaken, rather than strengthen, our ability to understand the world.

None of this is new. The “ axis of evil ” first emerged as a term in President George W. Bush’s 2002 State of the Union address, where he referred to Iran, Iraq, and North Korea as countries that endangered freedom around the world. Even at the time, the inclusion of the line in the speech was somewhat strange: It took place just a few months after the Sept. 11 attacks, and shortly after the United States had invaded Afghanistan, yet the three countries representing “evil” had nothing to do with either.

But the overblown rhetoric helped to build support for Bush’s Freedom Agenda by reinforcing the idea that dictatorships around the world could endanger daily life in democracies. It attempted to tie the war on terror to the legacy of World War II through implicit comparison to Nazi Germany and imperial Japan. The speech had real-world consequences: It helped the Bush administration build the case for its war against Iraq and undermined the thawing of relations between the United States and Iran that had started shortly after 9/11.

Since that time, there have been repeated attempts to revive the axis concept to make a political or foreign-policy point. In just the last few years alone, there have been articles about the axis of authoritarians , the axis of upheaval , and the axis of aggressors . All these formulations offer authors the same opportunity: Pick a selection of nations and define them, not on their own terms, but on yours.

The axis of authoritarians, for example, relies on regime type to tie together its members, though the list of countries involved (Russia, Iran, North Korea, Belarus, and China) includes unreformed Soviet-style totalitarian regimes, kleptocratic dictatorships, and party-rule capitalism. This group includes one of the world’s richest states—and one of its poorest. The axis of upheaval , meanwhile, is defined by countries’ opposition to the United States, or by their shared commitment to “overturn[ing] the global order.” In truth, one could have an axis of almost anything; one is reminded of the old joke from around the time of Bush’s initial speech that suggested groupings including the “axis of just as evil” and the “axis of countries that aren’t the worst but certainly won’t be asked to host the Olympics.”

Jokes aside, there is no denying that there are points of convergence and cooperation between the states referenced in these groupings. The reporting that accompanies the axis of malice story, for example, identifies a shared interest in the sanctions-busting “shadow” oil trade as a key area of cooperation among Russia, China, and Iran. Russia and China are cooperating on defense industrial issues, while Russia has built stronger ties with both Iran and North Korea due to its war in Ukraine and the search for cheap drones and easily replaceable domestic labor. There is a very clear case to be made that the bilateral relationships between many of these countries have grown stronger in recent years, to the detriment of U.S. national security.

Skeptics of the axis notion, however, would argue that many of these areas of cooperation were themselves driven by U.S. sanctions policy, not sought out by the states in question. There are clear tensions between Moscow and Beijing when it comes to North Korea, while China has been remarkably reticent in supporting either Russia’s war in Ukraine or Iran’s war with the United States. The evidence of growing bilateral ties between states is not matched by evidence of a common front among these states. Looked at holistically, many of their actions can just as easily by explained as states that find their interests—at least temporarily—pointing in the same direction.

Die US-Regulierungsbehörde FCC erteilte dem Projekt des Konzerns mit dem Namen »Starmind« laut einer Mitteilung vom Mittwoch eine entsprechende Genehmigung. »Indem sie Rechenkapazitäten über die Erdoberfläche hinaus verlagern, werden SpaceX und die zahlreichen Wettbewerber, die an ihren eigenen Datenzentren im Orbit arbeiten, den Anforderungen der Zeit gerecht«, sagte FCC-Chef Brendan Carr. DATA CENTERS IN SPACE🇺🇸 Today, in a historic first, the FCC approved SpaceX’s request for 1 million satellites (orbital compute modules) to create data centers in space The Starmind & competitor constellations will use solar power to extend America’s lead in Super Intelligence pic.twitter.com/VJinjK5e5E — Brendan Carr (@BrendanCarrFCC) November 25, 2026
items.body:
# Projekt »Starmind«: SpaceX darf eine Million Satelliten für KI-Rechenzentren ins All schicken

Bild vergrößern Testflug einer SpaceX-Rakete (Oktober 2024)

Eric Gay / AP / dpa

Das Raumfahrtunternehmen SpaceX des Unternehmers Elon Musk darf bis zu einer Million Satelliten zur Errichtung von Weltraumrechenzentren für KI -Anwendungen in den Erdorbit schicken. Die US-Regulierungsbehörde FCC erteilte dem Projekt des Konzerns mit dem Namen »Starmind« laut einer Mitteilung vom Mittwoch eine entsprechende Genehmigung.

»Indem sie Rechenkapazitäten über die Erdoberfläche hinaus verlagern, werden SpaceX und die zahlreichen Wettbewerber, die an ihren eigenen Datenzentren im Orbit arbeiten, den Anforderungen der Zeit gerecht«, sagte FCC-Chef Brendan Carr. Die Befürworter von Rechenzentren im All argumentieren mit der reichlich verfügbaren Sonnenenergie für deren Betrieb und den Kühlmöglichkeiten.

> DATA CENTERS IN SPACE🇺🇸 Today, in a historic first, the FCC approved SpaceX’s request for 1 million satellites (orbital compute modules) to create data centers in space The Starmind & competitor constellations will use solar power to extend America’s lead in Super Intelligence pic.twitter.com/VJinjK5e5E — Brendan Carr (@BrendanCarrFCC) November 25, 2026

Ich bin damit einverstanden, dass mir externe Inhalte angezeigt werden. Damit können personenbezogene Daten an Drittplattformen übermittelt werden. Mehr dazu in unserer Datenschutzerklärung.

Die Genehmigung ebnet nun den Weg für ein Konzept, das im Mittelpunkt von Musks Präsentation im Rahmen des Börsengangs von SpaceX gestanden hatte. Allerdings gibt es für die Errichtung von weltraumgestützten Rechenzentren auch technische Hürden. Sie brauchen sehr große Solarmodule zur Stromerzeugung sowie ausgefeilte Kühltechnologien, dazu Systeme zur Übertragung riesiger Datenmengen zur Erde .

Die FCC-Genehmigung gilt bis 2040. Laut der Behörde muss SpaceX 10 Prozent der maximal genehmigten Satelliten bis November 2035 ins All bringen, bis November 2038 müssen es dann 50 Prozent sein.

Die »Starmind«-Satelliten sollen in einer niedrigen Erdumlaufbahn in geringem Abstand zueinander positioniert werden, um eine zuverlässige Datenübertragung untereinander zu ermöglichen. Sie sollen über die bereits im All befindlichen Satelliten des SpaceX-Internetdienstes Starlink Daten zur Erde übertragen. Der US-Chiphersteller Nvidia soll eigens für den Einsatz im Weltraum konzipierte Prozessoren der neuesten Generation liefern.

- Teilerfolg für Musk-Unternehmen: SpaceX fängt Starship-Rakete erstmals am Startturm wieder auf 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 2 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- Ansage des Präsidenten: Trump will US-Konzernen verbieten, Rechenzentren im Ausland zu bauen 1 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 1 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
- Fusion von SpaceX und xAI: Was sich Elon Musk von Rechenzentren im Weltall erhofft Eine Analyse von Christoph Seidler 5 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen 5 Min Zur Merkliste hinzufügen
Musk hatte im Februar für den Aufbau von Rechenzentren im All seine KI-Firma xAI und SpaceX zusammengelegt. Der wachsende Energiebedarf für künstliche Intelligenz könne auf der Erde nicht ohne Belastungen für Menschen und Umwelt gedeckt werden, argumentierte Musk damals (mehr dazu hier ).

Auch andere Unternehmen arbeiten am Aufbau von Rechenzentren im Weltall, darunter der US-Internetkonzern Google und das Raumfahrtunternehmen Blue Origin von Amazon -Gründer Jeff Bezos .

items.title: Euclid's Record-Setting Quasar Probes Black Hole Formation
items.subtitle: The ESA's Euclid Space Telescope has found a record-setting quasar.
items.feedText: Euclid found it at redshift z=8.13, corresponding to about 630 million years after the Big Bang. It beats the record by about 40 million years. How these quasars formed is puzzling, but each new detection at greater distances leads incrementally toward an answer.
items.body:
# Euclid's Record-Setting Quasar Probes Black Hole Formation

Quasars are the cosmos' most luminous objects, generated by supermassive black holes (SMBH) that are accreting enormous amounts of matter. Astronomers keep finding these massive objects further and further back in time. The ESA's Euclid just found the newest record holder: the telescope observed it 40 million years sooner than the previous record-holder, and it was found at redshift z=8.13, corresponding to about 630 million years after the Big Bang. That's firmly in the Epoch of Reionization.

The quasar's technical name is J1504+6252, but it's been given the more recognizable name Dún Aonghasa. Dún Aonghasa is an ancient stone fort on top of a cliff in Ireland, where it looks out over the Atlantic Ocean.

The discovery is in research published in Astronomy and Astrophysics titled " Euclid: Discovery of a quasar at z = 8.13 hosting a 360-million-solar-mass black hole. " The lead author is Julien Wolf, who was a postdoc at the Max Planck Institute for Astronomy when the research was done.

One of the hallmarks of modern astronomy is the discovery of massive objects in the Universe that formed much sooner than astronomers thought they could. The JWST is driving much of this.

"Quasars powered by rapid accretion onto supermassive black holes (SMBHs) have been uncovered deep into the first gigayear of cosmic history," the authors write.

Now the Euclid Space Telescope is contributing to that trend. Euclid was launched to study dark energy and the expansion of the Universe. A big part of that job is measuring galaxies at different redshifts in its Euclid Wide Survey, to see how their morphologies are different over time. That will reveal how dark energy has changed over time.

This is what Dún Aonghasa, the new quasar, looks like in the actual Euclid image. It's the red dot in the center. Image Credit: ESA/Euclid/Euclid Consortium/J. Wolf et al.

Euclid found Dún Aonghasa in its Euclid Wide Survey imaging, but didn't confirm it. Follow-up observations by Keck, the Hubble, the Large Binocular Telescope, and especially the JWST provided the confirmation. JWST spectroscopy let the researchers measure "a systemic redshift of z sys = 8.129 ± 0.005, corresponding to only 630 Myr after the Big Bang and shifting the quasar redshift frontier by ≃39 Myr," the authors write. 39 million years is about 6% of the age of the Universe at that epoch. The quasar is now the first quasar observed at z > 8.

Dún Aonghasa's luminosity is what lets astronomers observe it at such a great distance. Its luminosity helped researchers measure its mass and its accretion rate, and Dún Aonghasa contains 360 million solar masses.

This figure shows absolute UV magnitude as a function of redshift for high-redshift quasars, galaxies, LRDs, LBDs, and other JWST-selected AGN up to z = 11. Orange squares show recently identified Euclid quasars, and the green star shows Dún Aonghasa, which is more UV-luminous than the LRDs, other JWST-selected AGN, and Lyman-break galaxies at comparable redshifts. JWST-selected AGN are shown as circles and colour-coded according to their phenomenological classification: LRDs in red, LBDs in blue, and other AGN in black. Previously known quasars are shown as grey circles. Open purple diamonds are Lyman-break galaxies. Image Credit: J. Wolf et al. A&A Volume 715, November 2026 A356

Dún Aonghasa and its high redshift brethren pose the same familiar question: how did they get so large so quickly?

"Assembling a black hole of several hundred million solar masses within the first few hundred million years, despite its currently sub-Eddington accretion rate, requires either a massive seed or sustained, highly efficient early growth," the authors write.

While an actual answer to their growth is elusive, finding them helps constrain an eventual answer.

“Finding quasars at ever-increasing distances, at the edge of the observable universe, teaches us something about how the black holes in their centres grew,” said lead author Wolf in a press releas e. “The closer to the Big Bang we find them, the faster their black holes must have grown or the more massive they must have been at birth — or both.”

Aside from their puzzling masses, these quasars also open different windows or probes into aspects of the early Universe. They give astronomers long sightlines into the intergalactic medium, letting them study its opacity during reionization, and its metal enrichment.

The quasars also serve as probes of how matter was distributed. "Quasars further mark rare, highly biased peaks in the underlying matter distribution and therefore trace the densest regions of the early large-scale structure," the researchers write.

On galactic scales, these high-redshift quasars are probes of how SMBH masses and the masses of their host galaxies co-evolved. Both masses tend to correlate, but there's no obvious reason why. AGN feedback could play a role, so could mergers, or a shared source of fuel for growth. But there's no certainty, so finding more high-redshift quasars may lead to an answer.

These things are all related, but the main result of finding these quasars is facing the questions posed by their high masses.

Finding these quasars and supermassive black holes is forcing astronomers to consider different explanations for how they grew so massive so quickly. One explanation is super-Eddington accretion , but Dún Aonghasa isn't accreting matter that rapidly. Another is massive seeds, but current formation models struggle to accommodate those. Another explanation is that quasars experienced super-Eddington accretion very early in the Universe, under very different conditions.

Heavy seeds could explain these quasars, but what could they be? Astrophysicists don't know, but some candidates are Direct-Collapse Black Holes , or maybe sequential runaway stellar collisions in extremely dense star clusters.

items.title: Did Army plan to detonate chemicals other than lead azide in Iowa?
items.subtitle: Multiple official EPA documents about the detonation featured redactions, fueling the claim.
items.feedText: Army destroyed 68 barrels of lead azide, a highly explosive compound, in Middletown, Iowa. Officials announced the blasts were successful, and according to the Environmental Protection Agency , its real-time air monitors had not detected any airborne lead more than an hour after the detonation. In the days leading up to the explosions — which raised widespread alarm due to the public health risks — a rumor spread online that the Army actually planned to detonate more than lead azide, according to a redacted document. A screenshot of the purported "Emergency Permit" spread across social media , apparently showing that in addition to 68 drums of lead azide, the Army was permitted to treat other, hidden materials as "hazardous waste." "Is the 68 barrels of lead azide not even the most scary, dangerous, poisonous part?!" One X post read ( archived ). The document was real.
items.body:
# Did Army plan to detonate chemicals other than lead azide in Iowa?

- The claim that the U.S. Army intended to detonate more than just lead azide during a planned explosion in in Middletown, Iowa, in November remains under investigation .
- The rumor stems from an authentic emergency permit issued by the EPA to the Army. The permit contained redacted text, which the Environmental Protection Agency noted was for "critical infrastructure security purposes at the request of Department of Army."
- It's unclear whether the redacted portions pertained to other material that was detonated, contained further details related to the lead azide or something else.
- Snopes will update this report if, or when, additional information surfaces. We have reached out to the Army and the EPA and are waiting for responses.
On Nov. 25, the U.S. Army destroyed 68 barrels of lead azide, a highly explosive compound, in Middletown, Iowa. Officials announced the blasts were successful, and according to the Environmental Protection Agency , its real-time air monitors had not detected any airborne lead more than an hour after the detonation.

In the days leading up to the explosions — which raised widespread alarm due to the public health risks — a rumor spread online that the Army actually planned to detonate more than lead azide, according to a redacted document.

A screenshot of the purported "Emergency Permit" spread across social media , apparently showing that in addition to 68 drums of lead azide, the Army was permitted to treat other, hidden materials as "hazardous waste."

"Is the 68 barrels of lead azide not even the most scary, dangerous, poisonous part?!" One X post read ( archived ).

The document was real. It was an emergency permit issued by the EPA to the Army, allowing it to treat the lead azide cache as a hazardous material (clearing the way for the military to move forward with the detonation plan) "upon the EPA's finding of an imminent and substantial endangerment to human health and the environment."

Because it remains unclear what text was redacted, Snopes has left this claim unrated. We reached out to the Army and the EPA . We will update this story if we receive a response.

On Page 2, the permit read:

> Name: Lead Azide Hazardous Waste Codes: D003 (reactivity), D008 (toxicity characteristic for lead) CAS Number: 13424-46-9 DOT Shipping Classification: Hazard Class 1.1A, UN0130 Quantity: There are 68 drums of Lead Azide, [REDACTED] [REDACTED] [REDACTED]

On Page 12 (Section IV.N.1), it read:

> N. Permitted and Prohibited Waste Identification 1. The Permittee shall only treat the following hazardous waste in accordance with this Emergency Permit Quantity: 68 drums of lead Azide, [REDACTED] [REDACTED]

Another widely circulated screenshot apparently showing the lead azide properties alongside heavily-redacted details related to what appeared to be other materials. That image also was authentic — it was sourced from another EPA document (PDF page 74).

It's unclear whether the redacted portions pertained to other material that was detonated, contained further details related to the lead azide or something else.

On Nov. 23, the EPA noted that "the permit and permit application materials contain redacted elements for critical infrastructure security purposes at the request of Department of Army."

In our questions to the EPA and Army, we asked why the redacted information was considered a security threat and whether the public should be concerned about what, if anything, else was detonated along with the lead

# Lob als Stressfalle im Büro: Warum „Servant Leadership“ manche Mitarbeiter:innen überlastet

## Die Perfektionsfalle: Wie „perfekte“ Chefs „perfekte“ Mitarbeiter in die Arbeitssucht treiben

Offene Türen, regelmäßiges Feedback und echte Rücksichtnahme gelten im Berufsleben als Merkmale zeitgemäßer Führung. Eine neue Untersuchung aus Australien, Großbritannien und China legt nun jedoch eine unerwartete Schattenseite offen.

Unerwartete Ergebnisse: Gute Chefs sind schlecht für manche Mitarbeitenden. (Foto: Gorodenkoff / Shutterstock)

Arbeitnehmer:innen, die im Büro unbedingt makellos wirken wollen, neigen gerade unter unterstützenden Chef:innen verstärkt zu zwanghaftem Übereinsatz. Zu diesem Ergebnis kommt ein Team um die australische Adelaide University, wie in einer im Fachmagazin Human Relations veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist.

Für die Erhebung werteten die Wissenschaftler:innen in drei zeitversetzten Befragungen Angaben von insgesamt 747 Arbeitnehmer:innen und 257 Führungskräften aus. „Selbst gute Führungskräfte können bei manchen Mitarbeiter :innen unbeabsichtigt Druck erzeugen“, sagt Erstautorin Lin Xiao Chu in einer Mitteilung .

## Warum eine Fassade im Job mehr belastet als hohe Eigenansprüche

Ausschlaggebend ist dabei weniger der innere Anspruch eines Menschen, für sich selbst möglichst fehlerfreie Arbeit abzuliefern. Gefährdet sind laut der Untersuchung vor allem Mitarbeiter:innen, die vor wichtigen Beurteiler:innen eine makellose Fassade aufbauen und ihren Eindruck gezielt steuern wollen.

items.title: Gewalt und Schulabsentismus: Lehrkräfte an beruflichen Schulen brauchen mehr Unterstützung
items.subtitle: Berufliche Schulen sollen jungen Menschen auch dann noch eine Perspektive eröffnen, wenn ihre bisherige Schullaufbahn von Misserfolgen und Brüchen…
