items.body:
BERLIN. **Berufliche Schulen sollen jungen Menschen auch dann noch eine Perspektive eröffnen, wenn ihre bisherige Schullaufbahn von Misserfolgen und Brüchen geprägt war. Doch ausgerechnet in den Bildungsgängen, die Jugendliche ohne Ausbildungsplatz auf das Berufsleben vorbereiten, sind Lehrkräfte besonders mit Gewalt und hohen Fehlzeiten konfrontiert. Das geht aus einer bundesweiten Befragung von knapp 2.000 Lehrkräften durch den Bundesverband der Lehrkräfte für Berufsbildung (BvLB) hervor. Der Verband sieht die Ursachen vielfach in der Bildungsbiografie der Jugendlichen – und fordert Konsequenzen für die personelle Ausstattung der Schulen. Eine große Mehrheit der befragten Lehrkräfte wünscht sich auch ein konsequenteres Vorgehen gegen Schulabsentismus.**

Lust auf Schule? (Symbolfoto.) Foto: Shutterstock

Fast drei Viertel der befragten Lehrkräfte an beruflichen Schulen (73 Prozent) fühlen sich auf den Umgang mit Gewalt nicht ausreichend vorbereitet. Allerdings verteilen sich die Probleme höchst unterschiedlich auf die einzelnen Bildungsgänge. Während 61 Prozent der Befragten die Berufsvorbereitung als besonders von Gewalt betroffen nennen, sind es beim beruflichen Gymnasium lediglich vier Prozent. Zu den häufigsten Erscheinungsformen zählen nach Angaben der Lehrkräfte psychische Gewalt wie Beleidigungen und Mobbing, aber auch körperliche Auseinandersetzungen unter Schülerinnen und Schülern.

Das geht aus einer nun veröffentlichten Befragung des Bundesverbands der Lehrkräfte für Berufsbildung hervor, an der sich zwischen dem 12. April und dem 27. August dieses Jahres 1.969 Lehrkräfte an beruflichen Schulen aus 14 Bundesländern beteiligt haben. Die Ergebnisse sind zwar nicht repräsentativ, vermitteln aber ein breites Stimmungsbild aus der schulischen Praxis.

## „Lehrkräfte an beruflichen Schulen leisten täglich weit mehr als Unterricht – im Übergangsbereich ganz besonders“

Auch beim Schulabsentismus zeigen sich erhebliche Unterschiede zwischen den Bildungsgängen. 56 Prozent der Befragten nennen Berufsfachschulen als besonders von Fehlzeiten betroffen, 49 Prozent die Berufsvorbereitung. Schulabsentismus ist allerdings auch in der dualen Berufsausbildung ein Thema: 29 Prozent der befragten Lehrkräfte nennen die Berufsschule im dualen System als besonders betroffen. Damit berührt das Problem unmittelbar auch die Bemühungen um die Fachkräftesicherung. Regelmäßige Fehlzeiten gefährden den erfolgreichen Abschluss einer bereits begonnenen Ausbildung.

Die besondere Konzentration der Probleme im Übergangsbereich hat nach Einschätzung des BvLB wesentlich mit den Voraussetzungen zu tun, unter denen die Jugendlichen an die beruflichen Schulen kommen. In den entsprechenden Bildungsgängen werden junge Menschen ohne Ausbildungsplatz auf eine Berufsausbildung vorbereitet oder zu einem Hauptschulabschluss beziehungsweise einem mittleren Schulabschluss geführt. Für viele von ihnen ist dies die Möglichkeit, Versäumtes aus ihrer bisherigen Schullaufbahn nachzuholen und überhaupt erst die Voraussetzungen für eine Berufsausbildung zu erwerben.

Woher die Probleme kommen, die den Lehrkräften dabei begegnen, beschreiben die Befragten ebenfalls. Als wesentliche Einflussfaktoren nennen sie Schulmüdigkeit, negative Schulerfahrungen, familiäre Probleme und Überforderung. Die Ursachen für die Schwierigkeiten im Übergangsbereich liegen demnach vielfach in einer Zeit, in der die Jugendlichen noch gar keine berufliche Schule besuchten – und zum Teil außerhalb des Einflussbereichs von Schule überhaupt.

Für die Lehrkräfte bedeutet das, dass sie neben der fachlichen Qualifizierung der Jugendlichen auch daran arbeiten müssen, deren Bereitschaft zum Schulbesuch wiederherzustellen. Sie beraten, vermitteln in Konflikten und versuchen, Schülerinnen und Schülern mit geeigneten Unterstützungsangeboten die Rückkehr in einen geregelten Schulalltag zu ermöglichen. Gleichzeitig sollen sie fachliche Defizite aufarbeiten und die Jugendlichen auf die Anforderungen einer Ausbildung vorbereiten.

Wie groß der Förderbedarf aus Sicht der Lehrkräfte ist, zeigen weitere Ergebnisse der Befragung. 46 Prozent wünschen sich mehr Lernberatung, 30 Prozent eine stärkere Sprachförderung und 29 Prozent zusätzliche Förderstunden. Der BvLB verweist in diesem Zusammenhang auf die Bedeutung grundlegender Kompetenzen im Lesen, Schreiben und Rechnen sowie auf die sprachlichen Voraussetzungen für eine erfolgreiche Berufsausbildung. Der Übergangsbereich übernimmt damit auch Aufgaben, die eigentlich bereits in den allgemeinbildenden Schulen hätten erfüllt werden sollen.

Besonders groß ist der Bedarf an Unterstützung durch andere Professionen: 81 Prozent der befragten Lehrkräfte wünschen sich mehr Unterstützung durch Schulsozialarbeit oder Schulpsychologie. „Lehrkräfte an beruflichen Schulen leisten täglich weit mehr als Unterricht – im Übergangsbereich ganz besonders. Unsere Befragung zeigt aber auch: Diese vielfältigen Aufgaben sind ohne zusätzliche Unterstützung auf Dauer nicht zu bewältigen. Bund und Länder sind jetzt gemeinsam gefordert“, erklärt Christian Löffler, Leiter der Fachkommission für Schul- und Bildungspolitik im BvLB.

Der Verband fordert deshalb, multiprofessionelle Teams dauerhaft an den beruflichen Schulen zu etablieren. Schulsozialarbeit, Schulpsychologie und weitere pädagogische Fachkräfte müssten entsprechend dem tatsächlichen Bedarf zur Verfügung stehen. Unterstützungsstrukturen, die sich im Rahmen des Startchancen-Programms bewährten, müssten in die Regelfinanzierung übernommen werden – ausdrücklich auch an beruflichen Schulen.

Dass sich die Lehrkräfte nicht allein zusätzliche pädagogische Unterstützung wünschen, sondern auch eine verbindlichere Durchsetzung der Schulpflicht, zeigt ein weiteres Ergebnis der Befragung: 86 Prozent sprechen sich für Konsequenzen bei hohen Fehlzeiten aus. Fast die Hälfte (48 Prozent) wünscht sich mehr Unterstützung durch das Ordnungsamt.

items.title: How to make Thanksgiving even better
items.subtitle:
Photo by Jimmy Conover on Unsplash

Just to be clear, I like Thanksgiving.
items.feedText: In fact, I like holidays in general. My favorites are Christmas and New Year’s, but I also love the 4th of July, Valentine’s Day, and Halloween. I like Labor Day and Memorial Day, despite the fact that most people don’t seem to get off work these days. I enjoy Mother’s Day and Father’s Day, even though my parents are no longer with us. St. Patrick’s Day and Cinco de Mayo are fun, even though I don’t drink much alcohol. Passover and Purim are underrated Jewish religious holidays, and Hanukkah is an excellent alte…
items.body:
Photo by [Jimmy Conover](https://unsplash.com/@jimmy_conover?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText) on [Unsplash](https://unsplash.com/photos/brown-and-white-wooden-house-fyEin27bHZ8?utm_source=unsplash&utm_medium=referral&utm_content=creditCopyText)

Just to be clear, I *like* Thanksgiving. In fact, I like holidays in general. My favorites are Christmas and New Year’s, but I also love the 4th of July, Valentine’s Day, and Halloween. I like Labor Day and Memorial Day, despite the fact that most people don’t seem to get off work these days. I enjoy Mother’s Day and Father’s Day, even though my parents are no longer with us. St. Patrick’s Day and Cinco de Mayo are fun, even though I don’t drink much alcohol. Passover and Purim are underrated Jewish religious holidays, and Hanukkah is an excellent alternative Christmas. I’m sure Diwali will be a party once Hindu culture becomes more common in America. Juneteenth was a Texas holiday long before it became a national one. Columbus Day is fun mainly for seeing people get mad online. Presidents’ Day is…a day, I guess.

But OK, Thanksgiving. It has lots to recommend it. For one thing, *everyone* gets off work, which is not true for any other holiday except Christmas. It’s a great opportunity for most people to see their families. And since it’s on a Thursday, almost everyone gets at least four or five consecutive days off in a row (European friends, I assure you that this is a big deal in America). I also like pie,1 and Thanksgiving is a prime time for pie. Also, Thanksgiving is conveniently situated midway between Halloween and Christmas, making the last two months of the year feel like one big rolling holiday season.

For many years, though, I’ve felt like Thanksgiving could stand to have a major upgrade in our culture. Despite its advantages, the holiday as it stands has several big weaknesses.

First of all, it involves a lot of frantic rushing around. You fly or drive out to see your family on Wednesday, you eat a big dinner, you hang out for one or two more days, and then you fly right back for three more weeks of work before Christmas, with barely any time to relax. The air congestion is horrendous, and the roads aren’t much better. Contrast this with Christmas/New Year’s, which for many people is a week or more of vacation.

Unfortunately, I don’t think the timing of Thanksgiving is fixable. American culture being what it is, a second country-wide “vacation week” would be a big ask. And if we do get a second vacation week, it should really be in the spring, to balance out the relative lack of national holidays in that season.

Thanksgiving’s second big weakness — that not everyone has a family they can visit — has already been fixed, with the advent of Friendsgivings. This has also turned Thanksgiving into a much-needed “dinner-party holiday”. Americans already have lots of holidays where they go out and party and drink alcohol (or your equally attractive non-alcoholic beverage of choice). It’s nice to have one cozy, low-key holiday where you invite all your friends over, show off your cooking skills, and chill on the couch. Friendsgivings also spread out the Thanksgiving holiday season beyond simply the 5-day weekend.

But there are still some ways that I feel Thanksgiving could be significantly improved.

One is that other than the dinner, Thanksgiving is kind of thin on associated traditions. Halloween has costumes and spooky house decorations. Christmas has gift-giving and cheerful house decorations. The 4th of July and New Years have fireworks. Valentine’s Day has gift-giving. Thanksgiving just has…dinner. There’s nothing wrong with dinner, but I feel like we can do more.

One idea is to add **a tradition of gift-giving**. We have holidays where you give presents to your family and friends (Christmas/Hanukkah, birthdays), and a holiday where you give presents to your lover (Valentine’s). But what about a holiday when you give out little minor gifts to your acquaintances and associates — your coworkers, neighbors, and so on? Ideally, these would be little individually wrapped snacks or other food items, like the omiyage boxes in Japan:

Photo by Jorge from Brazil via [Wikimedia Commons](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Japanese_Omiyage_in_2014_%2813335201323%29.jpg)

In fact, I borrowed this whole idea from Japan. While Valentine’s Day is a purely romantic holiday in America, in Japan people [bring chocolates for coworkers and friends](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Giri_choco) — and there’s another holiday on March 14th called [White Day](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/White_Day) when people do the same.2

A tradition of broad-based giving of minor gifts on Thanksgiving would fit with the general theme of “giving thanks”, since it’s basically a way to give thanks for all of your social ties. And it would be a way to celebrate our broad social networks, which are both more economically and more psychologically important than we tend to appreciate. It would also lead to a burst of society-wide creativity, as stores competed to create ever-more-creative gift boxes.

A second new Thanksgiving tradition could be **house decorations**. Yes, it would be a pain in the butt to decorate your house for Halloween, Christmas, AND Thanksgiving, three months in a row. But there are some ambitious home-decorators out there. And there are probably lots of people who would like to do house decorations, but who don’t want to do the spooky Halloween theme, and for whom Christmas is too religious. Thanksgiving decorations could be a way to accommodate that group, and raise the percentage of homes in any given neighborhood that have decorations at the end of the year.

What would Thanksgiving decorations be? Fall colors and pumpkins and such are obvious, but I think we need something more. One idea is to do creative illumination, like the “illumination” you see in Japan around the wintertime.

…

items.body:
Continuing their series on how our brains find the right paths, Aatish Bhatia and Arkarup Banerjee show the learning process through “sparks” that stand in as simplified versions of brains [moving through a space of possible brains](https://aatishb.com/myriad/how-brains-learn/).

> It’s worth taking a moment to appreciate how surprising this is — given enough tries, the same learning process turned every novice into an expert light seeker.
> Of the myriad possible arrangements of this spark’s brain, only a tiny fraction generate the behavior that we want. There are far more ways to fail than to succeed.
> And yet, you’ve just witnessed a small miracle. The spark navigated this labyrinth of dead ends and rewired its brain to find the light, guided by nothing but reward and punishment.

**Tags:** [Aatish Bhatia](https://flowingdata.com/tag/aatish-bhatia/), [Arkarup Banerjee](https://flowingdata.com/tag/arkarup-banerjee/), [brain](https://flowingdata.com/tag/brain/), [learning](https://flowingdata.com/tag/learning/)

items.body:
# Börsen: An den Finanzmärkten verstärkt sich die Flucht aus Risikoanlagen

Wall Street in New York: Eine Trendwende nach oben ist nicht in Sicht. Foto: Bloomberg Zusammenfassung Nutzen Sie komprimierte Kernaussagen für maximale Effizienz in Ihrem News-Alltag – verfügbar im H+ Standard Abo. Jetzt für 1 € testen Frankfurt. Die Angst vor einem KI-Crash hat die US-Börsen weiter fest im Griff. Auch am Mittwoch sind die Märkte mit hohen Verlusten in den Handel gegangen. Die technologielastige Nasdaq fiel im frühen New Yorker Handel um 4,3 Prozent. Der Leitindex S&P 500 lag drei Prozent im Minus.

Besonders Technologiewerte gehörten erneut zu den großen Verlierern. Damit ist der positive Effekt vom Wochenbeginn verpufft, als die überraschende Rückkehr von Jensen Huang an die Spitze von Nvidia eine kräftige Erleichterungsrally auslöste.

Nun wird an der Wall Street intensiv über eine unbequeme Frage diskutiert: Was kann die Angst der Anleger jetzt stoppen?

items.body: IntroductionReduced executive functioning (EF) - including inhibitory control, cognitive flexibility, and working memory - has been frequently observed among adolescents and young adults living with HIV (AYALH), despite antiretroviral therapy (ART). These deficits may reflect HIV-associated alterations in brain structure and function. This review aimed to synthesize the available evidence of this relationship.MethodsFollowing the Preferred Reporting Items for Systematic reviews and Meta-Analyses (PRISMA) guidelines, we searched PsycINFO, PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science databases for relevant studies reporting EF outcomes and neural correlates (structural or functional).ResultsTwenty studies met the inclusion criteria. Significantly lower brain volumes and cortical thickness, lower fractional anisotropy, higher mean diffusivity, higher cerebral blood flow, and altered cerebral metabolites were observed among AYALH relative to matched controls. EF problems, particularly in working memory, were frequently reported. Overall, the observed neural alterations correlated with decreased EF among AYALH.ConclusionDespite ART use, HIV-associated neural alterations and executive function deficits still occur or persist among adolescents and young adults living with HIV. Preliminary evidence suggests that distinct HIV-associated neural alterations may be associated with EF problems in AYALH. Neuroimaging may offer insights into these cognitive difficulties, although more longitudinal and multimodal studies are needed.Systematic Review RegistrationThis review is registered in PROSPERO (https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/prospero/), registration number: CRD42025639283.

Amazon is on the hook to recall more than 400,000 hazardous products after losing its legal battle against the US Consumer Product Safety Commission (CPSC). The US District Court for the District of Maryland [ruled in favor](https://www.cpsc.gov/Newsroom/News-Releases/2027/Federal-Court-Rules-in-Favor-of-CPSC-in-Landmark-E-Commerce-Product-Safety-Case) of the CPSC, [which argued that Amazon is a distributor of goods](https://www.theverge.com/2024/7/30/24209953/amazon-notify-customers-recalled-items-cpsc), not a logistics provider, making it responsible for carrying out recalls of third-party products.

[Amazon sued the CPSC in March 2025](https://www.theverge.com/news/631435/amazon-cpsc-lawsuit-recall-third-party-products) after the agency ordered Amazon to recall over 400,000 "Fulfilled by Amazon" products that pose a "substantial product hazard," including faulty carbon monoxide detectors, hair dryers without electrocution protection, and child …

items.body:
## Improving on a timeless recipe

The bezier curve is a staple of CAD and computer graphics. Like Bic pens, the design is decades old and they're everywhere. You'll often find them as the default or only choice in various illustration and animation tools.

Conceived by [Paul de Casteljau](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Paul_de_Casteljau) in 1959, and refined by [Pierre Bézier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pierre_Bézier) in the 1960s at Renault, the enduring appeal of the bezier curve lies in its simplicity. While more sophisticated curves have been invented, and [new ones continue to be proposed](https://linebender.org/blog/hyperbezier/), these are limited to specific domains, like high-precision CAD or road design. In general use, the bezier stubbornly refuses to be dethroned, despite its shortcomings.

Hence bezier curves are a piece of legacy tech we appear to be stuck with. As a software engineer, my question then is: can we make beziers better without invalidating all the tech built on and with them?

The answer is yes.

[↗ wallup.net](https://wallup.net/renault-4cv-classic-cars-french-73/)

## Lerp-a-derp

Drawing a bezier curve is a surprisingly simple and linear process:

*Tip: All the diagrams in this post are fully interactive.*

Given a series of control points, we connect them with lines. We then run along those lines simultaneously, to produce new points, which can be connected again. This process is repeated until we are left with a single point, which lies on the curve.

This construction makes beziers far more regular than they might first appear.

The linear interpolations (aka *lerps* ) can be summarized into a single compact formula, e.g. for 4 control points $ \left(A, B, C, D\right) $:

$$ \gamma \left( t \right) = A \cdot \left(1 - t\right)^3 + B \cdot 3 \left(1 - t\right)^2 t + C \cdot 3 \left(1 - t\right) t^2 + D \cdot t^3 $$

The rule is simple: descending powers of $\left(1 - t\right)$, ascending powers of $t$, with coefficients taken from the n'th row of Pascal's triangle:

$$
\ {ccccccccccccc}
&&&&&& 1 \\
&&&&& 1 && 1 \\
&&&& 1 && 2 && 1 \\
&&& 1 && 3 && 3 && 1 \\
&& 1 && 4 && 6 && 4 && 1 \\
&1 && 5 && 10 && 10 && 5 && 1 \\
... &&&&&&... &&&&&&... \\
\ $$

For curves in 2D and 3D, the formula is applied to the individual X, Y or Z coordinates.

While beziers can be constructed for any number of control points, the common practice is to only use cubic beziers with 4 control points. This is because the curve is only guaranteed to cross through the first and last control point, which makes higher degree beziers more difficult to shape.

Larger curves are instead constructed by joining together multiple cubic bezier segments, with the tangents lined up to create a segmented curve that appears smooth:

This is the cubic bezier *spline*, as commonly understood. The precision "pen tool" in most drawing apps then consists of drawing and editing the control points, rather than drawing curves directly.

## A Lie Told Everywhere

Pen tools typically have a few different modes for the control points:

Intuitively these represent various degrees of smoothness. Symmetric tangents are offered as the smoothest option, with some qualities of smoothness being lost as you relax the constraints.

In reality this is **completely wrong**, and this is easy to demonstrate.

Bezier curves can be split exactly, by reading off the new control points from the interpolation diagram:

The left and right segments are 100% identical to the original curve, and always join up perfectly at the seam. Yet the tangents in the middle will be asymmetric except for one split near the middle. This can be confirmed using a *curvature comb* which represents the (inverse) radius of curvature at every point:

The curvature comb remains continuous, with no jumps.

This means that whether or not adjacent tangents are of equal length, i.e. symmetric, is completely irrelevant. Attempting to draw smooth and intuitive bezier curves this way is a fool's errand.

A simple way to improve this is to treat the tangents as relative rather than absolute. e.g. We can make them proportional to the distance between the start and end of each segment:

This spline is easier to edit, because as you move each curve point around, the adjacent segments naturally flex to get out of the way. There are far fewer cusps created this way. Editing the tangents remains the same.

However if we plot curvature again, we can tell this isn't a great solution:

Scaling tangents proportionally doesn't guarantee that curvature is preserved as you edit, nor does curvature remain continuous from one segment to the next.

This also shows that offering users a curvature comb visualization as a "helpful tool" is really quite *mean*: adjusting the curvature on one end will also affect the other side, requiring repeated adjustments back and forth until it's close enough.

## Handle Carefully

A much more effective strategy is to work with curvature directly.

While this is a difficult problem in general, it turns out there are some surprising relationships here, which we can observe directly:

Consider the curvature at the start of segment $A-B-C-D$. This is affected only by the positions of $A$, $B$ and $C$. Point $D$ can be moved freely if it's detached from $C$.

Furthermore, because the tangent $A-B$ is horizontal, only the vertical position of $C$ matters. This is a result of the underlying linear interpolations, which end up cancelling out a lot of terms in the formulas.

The curvature at $A$ is therefor only affected by the length of $A-B$, and the perpendicular distance from $C$ to $A-B$. The same applies to $D$ on the other side with $C-D$ and $B$.

…

items.body:
Auch in diesem Schuljahr veranstaltet die Föderation der Deutsch-Französischen Häuser den deutsch-französischen Geschichtswettbewerb EUSTORY-France. Der diesjährige Wettbewerb befasst sich mit dem Thema: « Klima- und Umweltschutz schreibt Geschichte. Engagement und Protest in Deutschland und Frankreich ». Er lädt Schüler*innen der 8. Klasse bis zum Abitur in Deutschland und Frankreich (4e bis zur Terminale) ein, sich mit dem vorgegebenen Thema auseinanderzusetzen und einen Beitrag zu verfassen – in Einzel- oder Gruppenarbeit oder idealerweise im deutsch-französischen Tandem.

**Klima- und Umweltschutz schreibt Geschichte. Engagement und Protest in Deutschland und Frankreich**

Menschen haben seit jeher ihre Umwelt beeinflusst. Aber beginnend mit der Industrialisierung im 18. Jh. ist das Ausmaß dieses Eingriffs ein anderes geworden: Maschinen, Fabriken und große Städte verändern nicht nur das Leben der Menschen – sondern auch die Natur. Die Folgen werden immer mehr spürbar. Vereinzelt werden Menschen laut, die fordern, dass sich etwas ändern muss. Sie machen auf Missstände aufmerksam, schließen sich mit Anderen zusammen, protestieren oder rütteln mit spektakulären Aktionen wach und schaffen es, Veränderungen herbeizuführen.

**Der Wettbewerb möchte es genauer wissen:**

Von ganz frühen Naturschutzinitiativen über erste Anti-Atomkraft-Proteste der 1970er Jahre und globale Klimadebatten seit den 1980er Jahren bis heute: Was hat Menschen in Deutschland und Frankreich zum Handeln gebracht? Was waren ihre Ängste und Hoffnungen? Welche Erzählungen und Konflikte prägten die Debatten innerhalb und außerhalb der Bewegungen? Und wer bestimmte mit – Menschen aus der Wissenschaft, der Politik oder der Zivilgesellschaft?

Welche Formen wählten sie für ihr Engagement? Was waren ihre Erfolge und Niederlagen? Wie ist es ihnen gelungen, in unseren Gesellschaften etwas zu verändern? Und wie kann aus der Idee Einzelner eine politische Entscheidung werden?

Der Wettbewerb lädt dazu ein, die Suche vor der Haustür zu beginnen, lokale Geschichte zu erforschen und in einen breiter gefassten, deutsch-französischen und europäischen Kontext zu setzen. Welche Rolle spielte internationale Vernetzung? Welche Gemeinsamkeiten und/oder Unterschiede gab es zwischen den deutschen und französischen Bewegungen?

Und genauso wichtig: Welche Menschen und Ereignisse aus der Vergangenheit machen heute Mut? Was lässt uns lernen für unsere Zukunft – und die der kommenden Generationen? Denn die Geschichte des Klima- und Umweltschutzes erzählt von Verantwortung, Engagement und Protest – und sie ist noch nicht zu Ende geschrieben.

Die besten Beiträge werden mit Preisen ausgezeichnet, die im Juli 2027 im Rahmen einer offiziellen Preisverleihung überreicht werden.

[Weitere Infos & Anmeldung](https://eustory.fr)

*Eine Meldung der EUSTORY-France.*

items.body:
Gloria Steinem was booked up. There had been luncheons and interviews scheduled for the fall; a high-profile conversation with Katie Couric at 92NY and a prominent place in The New Yorker Festival’s lineup. She left appearances unfulfilled, interviews unaired, an essay unpublished and a forthcoming book. In short: Gloria Steinem was, at 92, far from done.

That energy is palpable in that very book, her memoir [An Unexpected Life](https://bookshop.org/p/books/an-unexpected-life-notes-from-a-hope-a-holic-gloria-steinem/4b7ec63a4c7acf42/?aid=132!), published on September 22, in which she states that she planned to live to at least 100. Although she was “older than [she] ever imagined,” mortality didn’t really cross her mind much. Any why would it, when she was also “happier than [she] ever imagined” and her calendar was bursting at the seams? Part memoir, part manifesto, part consciousness raising group, *An Unexpected Life* is a collection of essays in which Steinem reflects on her life, lays out her worldview and looks towards the future. And just as she was in life, on the page she radiates a matter-of-fact conviction and an unflinching clarity—the result of more than sixty years spent organizing a movement.

Her story begins long before she would become the most prominent face of second-wave feminism (although Steinem would reject this label), with a bruised childhood in Toledo, Ohio. She spent stretches of her young life on the road, until her father left when she was ten years old, leaving her in a rat-infested home caring for her increasingly mentally ill mother. With a childhood spent longing for warm kitchens and cookie cutter family units, it is striking that Steinem would grow up to spend so much of her adult life traveling around the country, more often than not living out of a suitcase. But even more formative than her earliest years, perhaps, was the time spent in India in her early 20s, an experience that would become the very foundation of her feminism.

Although mortality was far from Steinem’s mind, it is apparent in these pages that she was hyperaware of her legacy. “At my age, in this still hierarchical time, people often ask me if I’m ‘passing the torch,’” she wrote in her 1983 book [Outrageous Acts and Everyday Rebellion s](https://bookshop.org/p/books/outrageous-acts-and-everyday-rebellions-third-edition-gloria-steinem/753219586e6d55f1/?aid=132!). “I explain that I’m keeping my torch, thank you very much—and I’m using it to light the torches of others.”

She is doing just that in *An Unexpected Life*, a text bursting with a kind of hopeful exhilaration about what could be. “Nothing is more exciting than making the invisible visible. It’s like finding the end in a ball of yarn,” she wrote. “Pull on it, and gradually the whole of patriarchy unravels.” At times, she gets as literal as bullet-point lists on how to best organize a feminist movement. There are glimmers of the—often cited—shortcomings of the women’s movement that she was at the helm of herself. “Insist on multiracial women who represent the movement,” is one such takeaway of Steinem’s. “Otherwise, people will have a distorted view.” There is an added poignancy to the essays upon her passing; a book that is as much about her life as it is a handbook for movement building. “Whatever my story might be to other people,” Steinem wrote, “I hope something has ripple effects that I myself may never see.”

One such ripple effect concerns her beloved home, an apartment in a brownstone building on the Upper East Side of Manhattan. “If time and ingenuity allow,” Steinem wrote in the book’s prologue, “I hope to acquire the other floors in this house and leave this whole building as a refuge for diverse women who need a place to stay or just to meet.”

Steinem first moved into her apartment in 1968, together with a roommate. Throughout the years, the apartment grew not only in square footage but in function. The single unit became an entire floor, which became three floors. Her living room had been a meeting place for over fifty years, where she hosted gatherings and talking circles up until this very year. She held meeting on topics ranging from women’s health to misinformation in the media—a meeting in that very living room had led to the founding of *Ms. Magazine* in 1971. On September 3, Gloria’s Foundation announced that her brownstone would continue to be a feminist sanctuary; a place for women to father and organize, to discuss and seek shelter.

Lingering in the background of these pages is Steinem’s time in India. The years spent there upon graduating from Smith College made such a deep and lasting impression on Steinem, it not only ignited her activism but it is where her ideology was rooted throughout her life. In her final essay, published in [The New Yorker](https://www.newyorker.com/culture/life-and-letters/gloria-steinems-final-essay?utm_mailing=tny_nl_6667_daily_090326_utg9beo9c3&utm_source=nl&utm_brand=tny&utm_campaign=aud-dev&utm_medium=email&utm_content=tny_nl_6667_daily_090326_utg9beo9c3&cndid=64331124&utm_term=6667) following her passing, she wrote that it was where she realized that “white people were a very small minority in the world. In India, I got accustomed to, and began to value, racial diversity.” The open, nonviolent M.O. of Ghandi and his followers captivated her, perhaps not in the last place because she learned that his peace movement was once inspired by India’s women’s movement. “I think culturally women are drawn to nonviolence,” Steinem wrote in her final essay. “Probably because we are the major victims of violence, we become the major movers of peace.”

There is an odd comfort in having Gloria Steinem insist that it really, truly, *believe her*, has been worse.

…

items.body:
**KARLSRUHE. Erneut geht die Bundesanwaltschaft gegen eine mutmaßliche rechtsextremistische Terrorgruppe vor, deren Mitglieder zum großen Teil noch im schulpflichtigen Alter sind. Wie der „Spiegel“ berichtet, wurden am Mittwoch drei Jugendliche im Alter von 14 und 15 Jahren festgenommen. Sie sollen sich über Chatgruppen in kürzester Zeit radikalisiert und schwerste Gewalttaten geplant haben. Bereits im vergangenen Jahr hatten Ermittlungen gegen eine andere rechtsextremistische Gruppierung mit überwiegend jungen Mitgliedern bundesweit für Aufsehen gesorgt.**

Die Polizei ermittelt (Symbolfoto). Foto: Shutterstock

Die Bundesanwaltschaft ermittelt[dem „Spiegel“ zufolge](https://www.spiegel.de/panorama/justiz/terror-18-bundesanwaltschaft-geht-gegen-mutmassliche-rechtsterroristen-vor-a-0f1adf41-8cf7-4306-934d-6d8d9186fa43) gegen insgesamt sechs Jugendliche und Heranwachsende im Alter von 14 bis 19 Jahren wegen des Verdachts der Mitgliedschaft in einer rechtsterroristischen Vereinigung. Die Gruppe soll sich aus einem rechtsextremistischen Chatgruppen-Netzwerk namens „Terror 18“ entwickelt haben. Die Zahl 18 steht in der Neonazi-Szene für die Initialen Adolf Hitlers.

Die Beschuldigten hätten sich „extrem schnell radikalisiert“, zitiert das Nachrichtenmagazin die Bundesanwaltschaft. Sie sollen Angriffe auf Geflüchtetenunterkünfte bis hin zu „gezielten Tötungen von Ausländern und politischen Gegnern“ geplant haben. Weitere Ermittlungen richten sich gegen vier Personen aus dem Umfeld der Gruppe. Auch bei einem Jungen in Brandenburg wurde dem Bericht zufolge eine Hausdurchsuchung vorgenommen. Gegen ihn wird allerdings nicht ermittelt: Er ist noch keine 14 Jahre alt und damit nicht strafmündig.

Bereits im Mai 2025 hatte die Bundesanwaltschaft fünf mutmaßliche Mitglieder der rechtsextremistischen Terrorgruppe „Letzte Verteidigungswelle“ festnehmen lassen. Auch sie waren erst zwischen 14 und 18 Jahre alt. Die Gruppierung wollte durch Gewalt gegen Migranten und politische Gegner die demokratische Ordnung destabilisieren.

Im August dieses Jahres verurteilte das Hanseatische Oberlandesgericht in Hamburg sieben Mitglieder und einen Unterstützer der Gruppe zu Freiheitsstrafen zwischen anderthalb und fünf Jahren – unter anderem wegen versuchten Mordes. Die Angeklagten waren zur Tatzeit zwischen 14 und 21 Jahre alt. Wie die Deutsche Presse-Agentur (dpa) im September berichtete, hat die Bundesanwaltschaft mittlerweile auch gegen zwei weitere Jugendliche aus dem Umfeld der Gruppe Anklage erhoben. *News4teachers / mit Material der dpa*

> [Rechtsterroristen werden immer jünger: Urteil gegen die „Letzte Verteidigungswelle“ zeigt, warum (auch) Schulen alarmiert sein müssen](https://www.news4teachers.de/2026/08/rechtsterroristen-werden-immer-juenger-urteil-gegen-die-letzte-verteidigungswelle-zeigt-warum-auch-schulen-alarmiert-sein-muessen/)

items.body:
## fabrizio giugiaro introduces his copper-bodied peralta D

Italian automotive designer Fabrizio Giugiaro and his studio GFG Style unveil the Peralta D, a one-off [supercar](https://www.designboom.com/tag/car-design/) with bodywork made entirely from hand-hammered [copper](https://www.designboom.com/tag/copper-architecture/). Presented at the Pastejé Automotive Invitational in Mexico in October 2026, the Maserati-based grand tourer revisits the angular automotive design language that the designer’s father, Giorgetto Giugiaro, helped establish in the 1960s and 1970s.

The car has the appearance of a solid piece of polished metal, even across its expansive windshield and roof. A specially treated mirrored glass canopy takes on the reddish tones of the copper below, and the distinction between the two materials nearly disappears when the car is viewed in profile.

The project follows GFG Style’s 2025 Peralta S, a sports car sculpted from mirror-polished aluminum and inspired by Giorgetto Giugiaro’s 1971 Maserati Boomerang. Both vehicles were commissioned by Mexican collector Carlos Peralta. While the earlier model was dedicated to his sons, the latest takes its name from his daughters, with the letter D also referring to donne, the Italian word for women.

Fabrizio Giugiaro’s Peralta D features a hand-hammered copper body | images courtesy GFG Style

## GFG style shapes the bodywork by hand

The warm color of the Peralta D comes directly from the metal itself. The [design team](https://www.gfgstyle.it/) at GFG Style works sheets of copper by hand to achieve the broad, uninterrupted surfaces of the body, whose low nose and sharply defined edges recall the wedge-shaped concept cars of half a century ago.

Beneath the copper skin, a carbon fiber structure supports the bodywork, while an aluminum chassis and mechanical components draw from the Maserati GranTurismo. The dark, geometric wheels reference designs from the 1970s and sit almost entirely within the contours of the body.

Much of the functional hardware disappears into the exterior. Narrow blades of light extend across the nose and tail, while diamond-patterned aluminum grilles conceal additional lighting elements within their geometry. Even the carbon fiber aerodynamic components are tucked into the body.

the entire glass canopy lifts upward and forward to open the cabin

## a moving glass canopy replaces conventional car doors

Perhaps the most unusual aspect of the Peralta D becomes apparent when its occupants step inside. In place of conventional car doors, [designer](https://www.giorgettofabriziogiugiaro.it/) Fabrizio Giugiaro develops a system in which the entire canopy lifts upward and forward in one motion. Smaller gullwing sections can open independently along either side.

Access to the second row of seats introduces another moving element to the architecture of the car. Two additional panels rise from the rear bodywork in a configuration that recalls the split engine cover of the 1967 De Tomaso Mangusta, designed by Giorgetto Giugiaro. Here, Fabrizio adapts his father’s idea to accommodate passengers.

With all of these elements raised, the seemingly solid copper volume opens up into a series of thin metallic planes. It is a particularly expressive evolution of the moving dome that distinguished the Peralta S, this time adapted to the proportions and practical demands of a four-seat grand tourer.

independently opening gullwing panels are integrated into the canopy

## copper extends into the interior of the supercar

Inside the Peralta D, the reddish metallic finish continues across the leather upholstery, with genuine copper thread sewn into the seams. Dark, perforated Alcantara interrupts the otherwise continuous material palette.

The dashboard is organized symmetrically around the center console. Opposite the driver’s instrument display, a second screen sits above a concealed vanity compartment with an illuminated mirror. Between the rear seats, a retractable refrigerator houses a champagne bottle alongside four copper drinking glasses.

More than fifty years after Giorgetto Giugiaro experimented with the geometric possibilities of the automobile through his Maserati Boomerang, the Peralta D explores that same design language through the malleability of a different metal. Its futuristic appearance owes much to the work of traditional metalworkers and the painstaking process of shaping each surface by hand.

the angular silhouette recalls the futuristic wedge cars of the 1970s

a thin red light traces the perimeter of the copper tail

metallic leather upholstery echoes the exterior bodywork

the symmetrical dashboard features dedicated displays for the driver and passenger

the four-seat grand tourer transforms its silhouette through its movable panels

items.body:
On a foggy September morning in 1877, Eugene Victor Debs adjusted his suit collar and set out for the Indiana State House. Just shy of twenty-two years old, he’d been a member of his labor union, the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen, for barely two and a half years. But today he would deliver the opening address to its national convention.

Horse-drawn wagons and carriages rolled through the downtown streets of Indianapolis, clacking on the cobblestones and kicking up gravel as paved stretches came to an end. Lavishly ornamented cast-iron buildings mingled with simple brick structures; steam whistles sounded from the railroad tracks bound for the teeming Union Depot, the first in the country to bring all train traffic to a central hub. City leaders were thinking longterm here. Meatpacking was the city’s other big industry, Kingan and Company’s mammoth plant one of the largest in the world, its state-of-the-art chilling system allowing year-round production in these days before refrigeration.

Theirs was grimy, dangerous work.

Indianapolis wasn’t Chicago or St. Louis, Midwestern metropolises with populations in the hundreds of thousands, but its 75,000 inhabitants painted a smaller-scale picture of a rapidly industrializing America. With all the corresponding possibilities and cruelties. The boom-and-bust of capitalism had gone bust four years before in the so-called Panic of 1873, an economic disaster nearly as severe as the Great Depression of the 1930s—and joblessness persisted in Indianapolis, as elsewhere. Workers terrified of being laid off grudgingly accepted wage cuts. Politicians responded to calls for a public jobs program with creative new punishments instead: fines for begging, a proposed workhouse “where all persons incapable of paying fines” would be forced to smash stones to pave more city streets.

Soon, Gene Debs would have seen the Indiana State House come into view. A white wooden fence edged the tree-lined lawn—the trunks like matchsticks, branches draped with green leaves holding on despite the imminent change in seasons. The dome of the state capitol rose above, a grand if crumbling structure of blue limestone and gray stuccoed columns patterned on the Greek Parthenon. Debs—amiable and outgoing, a bit over six feet tall, with a slim but solid build—entered the capitol and mounted the stairs to the House of Representatives’ chamber on the upper floor, which the Brotherhood of Locomotive Firemen was borrowing for the convention. He greeted his fellow delegates, who had exchanged their soot-stained work clothes for suits and ties.

Theirs was grimy, dangerous work. Firemen shoveled the coal that powered steam engines into the locomotive’s firebox, which was prone to explosion. Every month the firemen’s magazine carried grim news of widowed wives, orphaned children, maimed railroaders. Train derailments and collisions were ubiquitous. Railroad workers made up the bulk of workplace injuries in Gilded Age America: by one count 56 percent of the broken ribs, 50 percent of broken arms, 41 percent of broken legs, 71 percent of severed arms, and all of the amputated legs.

Nearly one in four trainmen could expect to die on the job if he worked for thirty years; only coal mining was as lethal. The work was well paid by the standards of the day, with veteran engineers often able to own their own home, but shifts were long and irregular, running anywhere from twelve to twenty-four hours, or longer. “It is no uncommon thing,” one railroader said, “for an engineer to go for nearly a week without sleep except in snatches on the road or waiting on a branch or engine house.” Workers lived close to the railyards, knowing that at a moment’s notice they could be gone for days or weeks. The imperatives of their employers, rather than their own individual wants or collective needs, governed workers’ lives.

Not that Debs begrudged the railroad companies. If the work was too dangerous or too demanding, the hours too long or the bosses too harsh, it was up to railroad workers to prove themselves worthy of more respect. If they could do so—if they could renounce strikes and hard-drinking and rebelliousness, if they could live out the brotherhood’s motto of “benevo-lence, sobriety, industry”—then the companies would treat them with the dignity they deserved and pay them a decent wage. He was sure of it.

The story of Eugene V. Debs’s life is the story of one man’s radicalization—and of the country he helped radicalize in turn.

That summer, as far as Debs was concerned, rail workers had done the opposite.

Exhausted by four dragging years of economic depression, railroaders had struck by the tens of thousands, from the East Coast to the Corn Belt, inspiring hundreds of thousands of other workers to join them on strike. It was the first walkout of its size in United States history. The government treated it as an insurrection. President Rutherford B. Hayes sent in federal troops and militias, who shot down protesters, which triggered violence and widespread destruction of railroad property—torched locomotives, smoldering roundhouses, train tracks turned into twisted hulks of metal. The question at the heart of the Great Upheaval, as it came to be called, was whether the nation’s industrial development would benefit the workers who stoked the engines and ran the cotton looms and mined the coal, or whether it would anoint a new class of economic barons who’d monopolize the country’s wealth and power. “It is wrong to call this a strike,” one newspaper announced. “It is a labor revolution.”

And that’s exactly what Eugene Debs—a fresh-faced twenty-one years old, idealistic and respectable—did not want. After all, those same railroad companies that workers struck against had granted the brotherhood’s delegates free transport to their national convention. What better sign of the rail lines’ goodwill? What stronger proof of the benefits of currying favor with employers?

items.body:
# PET/CT imaging provides new insights into type 1 diabetes progression

## PET/CT imaging provides new insights into type 1 diabetes progression

edited by Gaby Clark , reviewed by Andrew Zinin

Gaby Clark

Scientific Editor

Andrew Zinin

Chief Editor

This article has been reviewed according to Science X's editorial process and policies . Editors have highlighted the following attributes while ensuring the content's credibility:

fact-checked

peer-reviewed publication

trusted source

proofread

A novel molecular imaging approach that measures beta-cell mass in the pancreas can offer valuable insights into the progression of type 1 diabetes, according to new research published in the Journal of Nuclear Medicine . The study found that individuals who have had type 1 diabetes for less than seven years have higher total beta-cell mass and function, larger pancreatic volume and lower intrapancreatic fat compared to those who have had the disease for longer. This valuable information, paired with functional tests, has the potential to significantly improve clinical trials of new therapeutic interventions.

Globally, more than 9.5 million people live with type 1 diabetes. In this chronic disease, pancreatic beta cells are destroyed over time, leading to an insulin deficiency and thereby hyperglycemia.

"Not all beta cells will be destroyed in type 1 diabetes, but the exact timing and fate of beta-cell loss are still unknown," said Sevilay Tokgöz, Ph.D., a postdoctoral researcher at Radboud University Medical Center in Nijmegen, the Netherlands. "A better understanding of this process is required to develop therapeutic strategies to halt disease progression."

In the study, Tokgöz and colleagues measured total beta-cell mass using ⁶⁸Ga-NODAGA-exendin-4 PET/CT imaging, an approach that targets GLP-1 receptors that are highly expressed on beta cells. Data from 16 individuals with short-duration type 1 diabetes (less than seven years) and 10 with long-duration type 1 diabetes (more than seven years) were analyzed. Participants underwent ⁶⁸Ga-NODAGA-exendin-4 PET/CT and a mixed-meal tolerance test to determine total beta-cell mass and function, respectively. Intrapancreatic fat deposition and pancreatic volume were derived from CT.

Total beta-cell mass and function were higher in individuals with short-duration type 1 diabetes compared with those with long-duration type 1 diabetes. Larger pancreatic volume and lower intrapancreatic fat deposition were also observed in individuals with short-duration type 1 diabetes compared with the long-duration group. Together, these findings provide new insights into the relationship between beta-cell mass, function and disease duration.

"These findings are highly relevant in regard to the development of therapies aimed at restoring beta-cell function or preserving beta-cell mass," said Tokgöz. "They may aid in more precise estimates of treatment effects and improve the logistics of clinical trials, and in the future could identify individuals who may benefit from therapeutic interventions."

Publication details

Sevilay Tokgöz et al., β-Cell Mass and Function, Pancreatic Volume, and Fat Differences Between Short- and Long-Duration Type 1 Diabetes: A Detailed PET/CT Imaging Study, Journal of Nuclear Medicine (2026). DOI: 10.2967/jnumed.126.272915

items.body:
**ERFURT. Wie leicht können sich Bundesländer von angestellten Lehrkräften in der Probezeit trennen? Das Bundesarbeitsgericht hat die Kündigung eines Sportlehrers bestätigt, dem Schulleitungen unter anderem mangelnde Selbstbeherrschung und ein fehlendes Gespür für körperliche Distanz zu Schülerinnen und Schülern vorgeworfen hatten. Der Lehrer bestritt die Vorwürfe. Ob sie tatsächlich zutrafen, war für die Entscheidung der obersten Arbeitsrichter allerdings gar nicht ausschlaggebend.**

Das Bundesarbeitsgericht hat entschieden. Foto: Shutterstock / Tobias Arhelger

Der Fall betrifft einen Sportlehrer, der zum 1. Dezember 2023 in den Thüringer Schuldienst eingetreten war und an drei Regelschulen eingesetzt wurde. Für sein Arbeitsverhältnis galt der Tarifvertrag für den öffentlichen Dienst der Länder (TV-L). Bereits Anfang Februar 2024 äußerte sich eine Schulleiterin gegenüber dem Schulamt dahingehend, dass der Lehrer aus ihrer Sicht die Probezeit nicht bestanden habe. Der Pädagoge verfasste daraufhin eine Gegendarstellung. Die Schulleiterin sah sich durch diese allerdings in ihrer Einschätzung bestätigt, dass es dem Mann an Einsicht mangele.

Auch der Leiter einer weiteren Schule äußerte sich kritisch. Zwar bescheinigte er dem Sportlehrer fachliche Kompetenz und Erfahrung. Allerdings neige dieser dazu, die Beherrschung zu verlieren, wenn er sich angegriffen fühle. Der Schulleiter berichtete von Beschwerden und Problemen im Zusammenhang mit überhöhten Leistungsanforderungen, fehlenden Erkundigungen nach Vorerkrankungen von Schülerinnen und Schülern, überzogenen Unterrichtszeiten sowie unangemessenen Berührungen. Insbesondere die mangelnde Sensibilität des Lehrers für die körperlichen Grenzen anderer Menschen bereitete ihm Sorgen.

Auch aus der dritten Schule lagen nach Angaben des Landes Elternbeschwerden vor. In einem Fall ging es um die Verletzung einer Schülerin, die ärztlich behandelt werden musste. Dem Lehrer wurde vorgehalten, die Schwere der Verletzung bestritten und dem Kind Übertreibung unterstellt zu haben.

## Lehrer weist sämtliche Vorwürfe zurück – und klagt

Das Land kam zu dem Schluss, dass der Mann „für den Lehrerberuf als nicht geeignet erscheint“, wie aus dem jetzt vorliegenden Urteil des Bundesarbeitsgerichts hervorgeht. Am 13. März 2024 wurde der zuständige Bezirkspersonalrat über die beabsichtigte Kündigung informiert. Dem mehrseitigen Schreiben waren Stellungnahmen der Schulleitungen beigefügt – nicht allerdings die Gegendarstellung des Lehrers. Der Personalrat stimmte der Kündigung zu. Anfang April erhielt der Sportlehrer seine Kündigung zum Monatsende.

Dagegen zog er vor Gericht. Der Lehrer erklärte die gegen ihn erhobenen Tatsachenbehauptungen für falsch. Er argumentierte insbesondere, dass der Personalrat nicht ordnungsgemäß beteiligt worden sei. Das Land habe seine Kündigungsabsicht mit konkreten Vorfällen und angeblichen Pflichtverletzungen begründet, ohne dem Personalrat seine Sicht der Dinge zur Kenntnis zu geben.

Vor dem Arbeitsgericht hatte der Lehrer zunächst Erfolg. Das Thüringer Landesarbeitsgericht wies die Kündigungsschutzklage jedoch in zweiter Instanz ab. Das Bundesarbeitsgericht bestätigte diese Entscheidung mit einem Urteil vom 30. Juli 2026, dessen Begründung mittlerweile vorliegt (Az. 2 AZR 195/25).

## Ein subjektives Werturteil reicht in den ersten sechs Monaten aus

Entscheidend ist dabei, dass der allgemeine Kündigungsschutz nach dem Kündigungsschutzgesetz erst greift, wenn ein Arbeitsverhältnis länger als sechs Monate bestanden hat. Innerhalb dieser sogenannten Wartezeit muss ein Arbeitgeber eine ordentliche Kündigung noch nicht sozial rechtfertigen.

Das hat nach Auffassung des Bundesarbeitsgerichts auch Konsequenzen für die Beteiligung des Personalrats. Zwar ist dessen ordnungsgemäße Beteiligung Voraussetzung für eine wirksame Kündigung. Wie ausführlich der Arbeitgeber seine Entscheidung begründen muss, hängt jedoch davon ab, worauf er sie tatsächlich stützt.

Beruht die Kündigung auf einer subjektiven Einschätzung der persönlichen Eignung eines Beschäftigten, genügt es, diese Einschätzung dem Personalrat mitzuteilen. Der Arbeitgeber muss weder die einzelnen Beobachtungen offenlegen, die zu seinem Urteil geführt haben, noch dieses näher begründen.

Auch wenn der Arbeitgeber freiwillig konkrete Vorfälle schildert, um seine Einschätzung nachvollziehbar zu machen, ändern sich dadurch die rechtlichen Anforderungen nicht zwangsläufig. Hinsichtlich solcher zusätzlichen Angaben sei es „nicht entscheidend, ob diese objektiv zutreffend sind oder nicht“, stellt das Bundesarbeitsgericht fest.

Anders verhält es sich, wenn ein Arbeitgeber den Personalrat bewusst falsch informiert oder wenn tatsächlich konkrete Pflichtverletzungen und nicht eine subjektive Gesamtbewertung den Ausschlag für die Kündigung gegeben haben. In letzterem Fall muss der Arbeitgeber dem Personalrat die konkreten Kündigungsgründe mitteilen. Eine bewusst falsche oder unvollständige Unterrichtung kann die Kündigung unwirksam machen.

Im Fall des Thüringer Sportlehrers sah das Gericht dafür keine Anhaltspunkte. Die von den Schulleitungen geschilderten Vorfälle hätten aus Sicht des Landesarbeitsgerichts lediglich dazu gedient, die Gesamtbewertung der beruflichen Eignung nachvollziehbar zu machen. Diese Auslegung beanstandete das Bundesarbeitsgericht nicht.

## Personalrat hätte den Lehrer selbst befragen können

Auch die Tatsache, dass dem Bezirkspersonalrat die Gegendarstellung des Lehrers nicht vorgelegt worden war, machte die Kündigung nach Auffassung der Erfurter Richter nicht unwirksam. Aus einer ergänzenden Stellungnahme der Schulleiterin sei hervorgegangen, dass eine solche Gegendarstellung existierte. Der Personalrat habe deshalb erkennen können, dass die Vorwürfe gegen den Lehrer umstritten waren. Es hätte ihm freigestanden, den Betroffenen selbst zu befragen.

A large light well brings daylight deep into this private [home](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/houses/) that was designed by [Desai Chia Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/desai-chia-architecture/) for a tight site in a dense [Maryland](https://www.dezeen.com/tag/maryland/) neighbourhood.

The project takes its name from its location in Bethesda, a city located northwest of Washington DC.

The house is set within a suburban neighbourhood near the downtown district, where residential lots are about one-fifth of an acre (647 square metres). Because the houses here are close together, the architects needed to be very mindful of privacy concerns.

### Drawings and photographs

Previous

Next

### Drawings and photographs

Close

- Basement and first floor plans
- Second and third floor plans
- Roof plan

“The clients sought a house that would feel open and light-filled without sacrificing privacy,” said New York-based [Desai Chia Architecture](https://www.desaichia.com/).

“Its compact lot and the close proximity of neighbouring houses required a careful response balancing both openness and discretion."

The architects intended the house to “rethink suburban-urban hybrid living through a modern lens”.

Roughly rectangular in plan, it has three levels and a basement. Setbacks help break up the mass, particularly on the street-facing elevation.

The building appears “as a two-storey building from several vantage points,” the team said.

“The home is carefully scaled to blend with neighbouring houses, balancing a strong architectural identity with sensitivity to its suburban context,” the team said.

Facades are clad in grey fibre-cement panels made to last for a century. The material is known for protecting against fire, pests and extreme weather, according to the team.

“A durable, low-maintenance exterior with a strong architectural presence was a key client priority from the outset,” the architects said.

“Glass-fibre-reinforced concrete (GRFC) panels were selected to create a crisp, sculptural facade that captures texture and shifting light throughout the day.”

[Read: Desai Chia uses "camouflaging effect" for secluded Osprey House in New York](https://www.dezeen.com/2025/11/27/desai-chia-camouflaging-effect-osprey-house-new-york/)

A modern-style bay window adds dimension and visual interest to the front and back facades.

Within the home, public spaces are located on the ground level. The rear portion opens into a yard with a lap pool.

The upper levels contain bedrooms and two offices, and the top floor has a rooftop terrace. The basement holds a gym, ping-pong area and media room.

A limited number of windows helps ensure privacy. To provide natural illumination, the team created a three-storey light well, which is positioned along a central staircase and brings daylight deep into the dwelling.

“This vertical, faceted volume allows sunlight to cascade downward, distributing diffuse light from a small skylight across circulation spaces on multiple levels while minimising solar heat gain,” Desai Chia Architecture said.

The all-electric house has a geothermal heating and cooling system. To enable the homeowners to age in place, the house has a shaft where an ADA-compliant elevator could be added in the future.

The homeowners are physicians, one of whom can walk to his practice in downtown Bethesda.

“When needed, the dedicated home offices allow both physicians to work from home in spaces with calming natural light,” the studio said.

“Its location – easily walkable to downtown amenities and robust public transit – supports a connected pattern of work and family life.”

Other homes in Maryland include a [restored carriage house by Colleen Healey Architecture](https://www.dezeen.com/2022/06/09/colleen-healey-red-maple-house-maryland/) that features colourful facade panels and a [family home by Ziger Snead](https://www.dezeen.com/2018/08/27/slate-house-ziger-snead-architects-replaces-fire-ravaged-home-maryland/) clad in stone shingles, charred wood and weathering steel.

**Architect of record:** Thomson & Cooke Architects

items.body:
In 1994, as a refugee from New York City advertising (an accidental career resulting from a failed attempt to convert my biology degree into artistic fame in the big city), I returned to my home state of Vermont and dove headlong into wildlife art, crisscrossing the U.S. for six years on the national art show circuit. I didn’t write anything but birthday cards to my daughters.

Right in the middle of a show out west in the winter of 2000/2001, it hit me: I’d become as much a teamster as an artist, and I felt cut off from what inspired me to paint. I ditched my late summer schedule and planned an August/September, 330-mile “source-to-salt” canoe trip on the Missinaibi River, which flows north to James Bay (I bought my first canoe with my paper route money when I was 11). The trip wasn’t to be an escapist adventure, but work: a painting trip and a chance to reconnect with my Muse, as a classicist would say.

It also introduced writing into my creative repertoire. Realizing that hardly anyone would notice if I disappeared into the wilderness for a month, I contacted an art magazine that liked the artist-on-a-canoe-trip angle, and a canoeing magazine that liked the canoeist-on-an-art-trip angle. I wasn’t sure what I would write, but I figured something would come to mind on the river.

I’d assumed I’d have to go alone with an artist’s itinerary, but at an art show opening in June, John Pitcher, a pre-eminent U.S. wildlife artist, asked to join me. On the river, John and I became fast friends and discussed future trips, but in Mattice, Ontario, after 130 miles, he had to return, and I continued solo.

As soon as Mattice disappeared behind a bend, the enormity of what I was doing settled in. I was alone, facing 200 miles of wild river through roadless wilderness. On the one hand, I was keenly aware that without anyone to help, even a minor mishap could cascade into tragedy. On the other, the river held my undivided attention.

The wild expanses I have experienced aren’t alien places, but reminders that the wild is where we all come from.

That first night alone, I camped at the Kettle Falls portage, and in a substantial blow to my self-image as an adventurer, I was hit with an acute attack of loneliness. I focused on setting camp and starting dinner, but I couldn’t shake the intense melancholy. Then the westering sun lit the river’s east bank with an evening glow. Hoping for another distraction, I set to painting while my dinner boiled. I had to work fast to catch the light, but before long (and to my pleasant surprise), the painting started to come alive. A surge of euphoria welled up out of nowhere and washed the loneliness away in a tidal wave so intense that, for a few moments, I wondered if I was OK. The weirdest part was a heartwarming sense of connection, not just to my surroundings, but to people—not anyone in particular, but everyone. I was never lonely on the river again.

That evening, as I dutifully recorded the day’s events in the journal the magazines had asked me to keep, I discovered that my new assignment was more than just a travelogue. The small painting that had precipitated one of the most intense emotional reactions of my life could, ironically, do nothing to describe or explain the internal transformation I’d undergone. But writing could.

*The Way North – Kettle Falls, Missinaibi River*. Acrylic field painting, September 4, 2001.

Over the next week, I made friends with Canada Jays and sandpipers, talked to rocks and various pieces of my gear, all of whom were generally supportive. On the other hand, an oblivious bull moose nearly killed me by accident, and a large bear looked like he was contemplating doing it on purpose.

But the river and forest offered only indifference. There was sound: birds, wind, the current along my hull or surging through rapids, but no noise and nothing I did seemed to matter. The ageless enormity of the planet pressed in, a wild Earth utterly unconcerned with humans, and as I thought back on the dizzying diversity of life that “Mother Earth” has birthed, provided for, and let pass away through the eons, I realized she is an impassive parent. That felt like an implied warning and crystalized how foolish it is to take the world for granted. I also knew then that painting wouldn’t be enough. I needed to write about it.

That point was underscored when I returned home and learned, to my surprise, that the wild rivers I had run in the Northwoods were all part of the world’s greatest remaining wilderness and largest terrestrial biome: the boreal forest. While this global forest’s southern reaches are within an easy drive of billions of people, much of it remains vast, remote, and rarely seen by anyone but the scattered indigenous peoples who have lived there for millennia. Yet writing about it matters because the boreal forest matters. As Earth’s largest and most intact land biome, it provides environmental services that help keep this planet habitable, second only to the oceans.

Painting is my first love, but writing grew from a journaling sideline into an equal partner in decades of work with fellow artists, scientists, conservation organizations, and indigenous communities to bring attention to the boreal forest.

items.body:
SAARBRÜCKEN. **Jahrelang haben die Kultusministerien händeringend nach Lehrkräften gesucht. Nun zeichnet sich aufgrund der gesunkenen Geburtenzahlen eine demografische Wende ab – und damit eine neue bildungspolitische Auseinandersetzung: Was passiert mit den frei werdenden personellen Ressourcen, wenn die Schülerzahlen zurückgehen? Der Verband Reale Bildung (VRB)** **im Saarland warnt bereits vor einem Abbau von Lehrerstellen. Denn der pädagogische Aufwand pro Kind steige erheblich. Ohnehin ist der Lehrkräftemangel längst nicht überwunden, wie aktuelle Prognosen zeigen.**

Winter Wonderland. Karikatur: News4teachers

Der VRB Saarland fordert eine grundlegende Neuberechnung der Lehrerstellen. Eine Personalplanung, die sich überwiegend an Schülerzahlen orientiere, werde den veränderten Anforderungen des Schulalltags nicht mehr gerecht, heißt es in einer aktuellen Mitteilung des Verbandes. Immer mehr Schülerinnen und Schüler benötigten zusätzliche Unterstützung, weil ihnen grundlegende motorische, sprachliche und soziale Fähigkeiten fehlten. Was Schule früher vielfach habe voraussetzen können, müsse sie heute zunehmend selbst vermitteln und einüben.

Hinzu kämen wachsende Anforderungen durch individuelle Förderung, Förderplanung, Dokumentation, Elternarbeit und die Begleitung einer zunehmend heterogenen Schülerschaft. Besonders an Gemeinschafts- und Förderschulen steige dadurch der pädagogische Aufwand erheblich.

„Lehrkräfte unterrichten längst nicht mehr nur. Sie müssen vielfach erst die Voraussetzungen für erfolgreiches Lernen schaffen – und gleichzeitig unveränderte Bildungsziele innerhalb der vorgegebenen Zeit erreichen. Das ist mit den vorhandenen personellen Ressourcen immer weniger zu leisten“, erklärt Karen Claassen, Vorsitzende des VRB Saarland. Zusätzliche Belastungen entstünden durch krankheitsbedingte Ausfälle, die von den ohnehin stark beanspruchten Kolleginnen und Kollegen aufgefangen werden müssten.

## Die demografische Wende erreicht die Schulen früher als erwartet

Hintergrund des Vorstoßes ist eine Entwicklung, die sich bundesweit abzeichnet. Die Bildungsministerkonferenz hat im September ihre aktualisierte Schülerzahlprognose vorgelegt. Demnach machen sich die seit 2021 deutlich gesunkenen Geburtenzahlen früher und stärker in den Schulen bemerkbar als bislang angenommen. Im Jahr 2025 wurden in Deutschland nach Angaben des Statistischen Bundesamtes 654.241 Kinder geboren – so wenige wie in keinem Jahr seit 1946.

Die Zahl der Schülerinnen und Schüler an allgemeinbildenden und beruflichen Schulen wird der Modellrechnung zufolge zunächst noch von rund 11,27 Millionen im Jahr 2025 auf rund 11,54 Millionen im Jahr 2029 steigen. Anschließend geht sie zurück. Für das Jahr 2040 werden nur noch rund 10,58 Millionen Schülerinnen und Schüler erwartet – knapp 700.000 weniger als 2025. Noch in der Prognose des vergangenen Jahres hatten die Kultusminister den Höchststand der Schülerzahlen erst für 2032 erwartet.

Allerdings verläuft die Entwicklung regional sehr unterschiedlich. Während in den westdeutschen Flächenländern bis 2040 ein Rückgang um 3,6 Prozent gegenüber 2025 erwartet wird, sind es in den ostdeutschen Flächenländern rund 21 Prozent.

Auch die Schulformen sind unterschiedlich betroffen. Während für die Primarstufe bis 2040 ein Rückgang um 14,8 Prozent prognostiziert wird, steigen die Schülerzahlen in der Sekundarstufe I zunächst bis 2031 noch um 8,3 Prozent. In der Sekundarstufe II wird der Höchststand sogar erst 2035 erwartet.

## Trotz sinkender Schülerzahlen: Bis 2035 könnten 87.000 Lehrkräfte fehlen

Dass sich der Lehrkräftemangel mit dem demografischen Wandel keineswegs erledigt, zeigt eine Ende Oktober veröffentlichte Untersuchung des Forschungsinstituts für Bildungs- und Sozialökonomie (FiBS). Der Bildungsforscher Dieter Dohmen hat seine bisherigen Berechnungen zum Lehrkräftebedarf auf Grundlage der tatsächlichen Schülerzahlen bis einschließlich des Schuljahres 2025/26 aktualisiert.

Das Ergebnis: Zwischen 2026 und 2035 könnten an den allgemeinbildenden Schulen bundesweit rund 87.000 grundständig ausgebildete Lehrkräfte fehlen – selbst dann, wenn sich das zahlenmäßige Verhältnis von Schülerinnen und Schülern zu Lehrkräften gegenüber heute nicht verbessert.

Dohmen macht insbesondere auf den hohen Ersatzbedarf für Lehrkräfte aufmerksam, die den Schuldienst dauerhaft verlassen. Seit dem Schuljahr 2015/16 lag deren Anteil am Lehrkräftebestand jährlich zwischen fünf und 6,8 Prozent. Der von den Kultusministern errechnete Einstellungsbedarf entspreche dagegen lediglich einer Ersatzrate von 3,8 Prozent, gemessen an der vom FiBS berechneten Entwicklung des Lehrkräftebestands.

Für den Zeitraum von 2026 bis 2035 ergibt sich aus der FiBS-Modellrechnung ein Einstellungsbedarf von rund 357.000 Lehrkräften allein an den allgemeinbildenden Schulen. Dem stehen nach den Berechnungen der Länder lediglich rund 270.000 Absolventinnen und Absolventen des Vorbereitungsdienstes gegenüber.

Besonders brisant: Rund 82.000 fehlende Lehrkräfte entfallen laut Dohmen auf die nichtgymnasialen Schulformen der Sekundarstufe I – also gerade auf jene Schulen, an denen der VRB einen steigenden pädagogischen Aufwand beklagt. Für die Grundschulen hingegen errechnet der Bildungsforscher einen möglichen Überschuss von rund 11.000 Lehrkräften.

## Rechnungshof warnt vor Personalmangel und wachsenden sprachlichen Defiziten

Ausgerechnet im Saarland hatte erst im August der Landesrechnungshof in einem mehr als 150 Seiten umfassenden Sonderbericht zur Gewinnung von Lehrkräften erheblichen Handlungsbedarf festgestellt. Bereits heute bestehen demnach Personalengpässe unter anderem in der Sonderpädagogik, in beruflichen Fachrichtungen sowie in den mathematisch-naturwissenschaftlichen Fächern.

items.title: The Hidden Spiegeltent in Chicago, Illinois
items.subtitle: These round wooden dance halls, lined with mirrors and stained glass, went from fair to fair.

The building opened in 1926. Rapp & Rapp designed it, with the Oriental Theatre movie palace on the lower floors. The theater is now the James M. Nederlander Theatre. items.body:
Spiegeltents were made to travel. These round wooden dance halls, lined with mirrors and stained glass, went from fair to fair. They went up fast and came down fast. The one on Randolph Street is not going anywhere. It was built indoors, on the 14th floor of a Loop building.

The building opened in 1926. Rapp & Rapp designed it, with the Oriental Theatre movie palace on the lower floors. The theater is now the James M. Nederlander Theatre. The whole building stands on the site of the Iroquois Theatre, where a fire in 1903 became one of the deadliest in American history.

High above the theater, the architects put a large hall for Masonic meetings. It sat empty for decades. Later it was turned into offices, and a dropped ceiling hid the room completely. When the building was converted into the Cambria Hotel, workers took that ceiling down and found the old hall again, steel bow trusses and all.

In 2019 the tent came over from Belgium in pieces, about 4,000 of them. Belgian tent builders put it together inside the hall, the traditional way, with no nails. It is about 72 feet across. From the hall, it looks like a small circus parked under factory trusses. Inside, there is carved wood, stained glass, velvet and mirrors everywhere. The mirrors are not just for looks. They let guests see around the posts that hold up the roof.

Since October 2026, the tent has been the home of Kermess by Circensia, which kept it right at the center of the room.

items.feedText: Bundestagspräsidentin Julia Klöckner im Parlament. (dpa / picture alliance / Andreas Gora) Klöckner sagte dem Internet-Portal "The Pioneer", sie habe die Parlamentsverwaltung gebeten, zu überprüfen, wie man sanktionieren könne. Die Linken-Politikerinnen Becker und Mazzi hatten sich bei einer Bundestags-Veranstaltung mit dem früheren Chef des israelischen Geheimdienstes Mossad, Barnea, kurzzeitig vor die Tür eines Sitzungssaals gesetzt.
items.body:
# Bundestagspräsidentin - Klöckner will Sanktionen nach Blockade durch Linke-Politikerinnen im Bundestag

Bundestagspräsidentin Julia Klöckner im Parlament. (dpa / picture alliance / Andreas Gora) Klöckner sagte dem Internet-Portal "The Pioneer", sie habe die Parlamentsverwaltung gebeten, zu überprüfen, wie man sanktionieren könne. Die CDU-Politikerin Klöckner nannte die Aktion einen "Tiefpunkt", der nicht folgenlos bleiben dürfe. Sie sei da keine Schiedsrichterin der Meinungen, sondern des Umgangs. Zuvor hatte Klöckner bereits angekündigt, den Vorfall im Ältestenrat des Bundestags zu erörtern. Die Linken-Politikerinnen Becker und Mazzi hatten sich bei einer Bundestags-Veranstaltung mit dem früheren Chef des israelischen Geheimdienstes Mossad, Barnea, kurzzeitig vor die Tür eines Sitzungssaals gesetzt. Barnea wird eine maßgebliche Rolle bei dem Pager-Angriff auf die Terror-Miliz Hisbollah im September 2024 im Libanon inne gehabt zu haben. Damals waren gleichzeitig tausende tragbare Funkempfänger und Walkie-Talkies explodiert. Dutzende Menschen wurden getötet und Tausende verletzt. Diese Nachricht wurde am 26.11.2026 im Programm Deutschlandfunk gesendet.

## Art Basel Announces New Highlights To Look Forward to at 2026 Miami Beach

[↗ Primärquelle: mymodernmet.com](https://mymodernmet.com/art-basel-miami-beach-2026-highlights/)

Art Basel Miami Beach, General Impressions, Courtesy of Art Basel

[Art Basel Miami Beach](https://mymodernmet.com/art-basel-miami-beach-2025-recap/) is preparing to bring the international art world together for another year. The fair has announced additional details for its 2026 edition, including major gallery presentations, digital art projects, artist conversations, and public installations throughout South Florida. With 272 exhibitors from more than 40 countries and territories, the event will offer a wide-ranging look at contemporary art and the ideas shaping it.

The newly announced gallery presentations span several generations and mediums. Brazilian artist Rosana Paulino will present her first bronze sculpture, *Crisálida* (2025–26), with Mendes Wood DM. Other highlights include a new painting by Shara Hughes at David Kordansky Gallery and monumental bronze sculpture by Wangechi Mutu at Gladstone. A joint presentation by Ortuzar and Crèvecœur will feature paintings by Ernie Barnes, coinciding with an exhibition of his work at ICA Miami. Miami-based Spinello Projects will also make its debut in the Galleries sector, showcasing artists from the Latin American and Caribbean diaspora.

Digital art will have an expanded presence through Zero 10: Generation, the initiative’s largest edition to date. Curated by Karen Archey and Eli Scheinman, it brings together 21 exhibitors across 19 projects. The presentations explore generative art, artificial intelligence, and emerging technologies. The program also looks to the history of digital experimentation, with a presentation on early computer art in Latin America and a new collaboration with Google Arts & Culture.

The fair’s Conversations program will explore the connections between art and other cultural fields, including sports and technology. Across four days, artists, curators, and public figures will discuss topics ranging from creative practice to identity and representation.

A dedicated Art & Sports series features NBA champion Kevin Love, soccer star Crystal Dunn, and Brooklyn Nets and New York Liberty co-owner Clara Wu Tsai. The program also includes a panel with the NFL examining portraiture and legacy in professional football.

Beyond the convention center, public art and museum exhibitions will extend the experience across Greater Miami. In Collins Park, *Between Tides*, a collaboration with Public Art Fund, transforms six ping-pong tables into playable sculptural installations designed by artists.

The Art Basel Awards will also return for a second year, recognizing achievements across the contemporary art world. The winners will be announced at a ceremony at Miami Beach’s New World Center.

Art Basel Miami Beach takes place Dec. 4–6, at the Miami Beach Convention Center. VIP preview days are scheduled for December 2–3.

items.body:
Does a real video show Prince Harry shoving wife Meghan Markle, while holding their daughter, Lilibet, outside what appears to be Buckingham Palace in London? No, that's not true: The video shows visual signs of AI generation, and the girl being held is too young to be Lilibet, who is 5 years old. Lead Stories found no matching reports from established news outlets.

The claim appeared in [a post](https://x.com/mbaadol/status/2125265002592628978) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125235414/https://x.com/mbaadol/status/2125265002592628978) ) by the @MbaAdol account on X on Nov. 24, 2026. It read:

> BOOM 💥 MASSIVE ROYAL STUNNER - LESS THAN 15 MINUTES AGO HARRY WAS PHOTOGRAPHED FRANTICALLY TAKING PRINCESS LILIBET TO THE CAR AFTER REPORTEDLY DISCOVERING WHAT MEGHAN HAD DONE TO THEIR LITTLE GIRL.
> Uwahala Everywhere

This is what a screenshot of the video in the post looked like at the time of writing:

*(Image source: post by @MbaAdol on X.)*

The post is embedded below:

> BOOM 💥 MASSIVE ROYAL STUNNER - LESS THAN 15 MINUTES AGO HARRY WAS PHOTOGRAPHED FRANTICALLY TAKING PRINCESS LILIBET TO THE CAR AFTER REPORTEDLY DISCOVERING WHAT MEGHAN HAD DONE TO THEIR LITTLE GIRL. Uwahala Everywhere https://t.co/ShJH76t2AJ
> -- Hon Dim (@MbaAdol) [November 24, 2026](https://x.com/MbaAdol/status/2125265002592628978?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

#### AI indicators

The scene in the fabricated video appears to be set outside Buckingham Palace in central London in a very public place. Several visual glitches reveal that the video is AI-generated.

First, the man pushes the woman, but his arm bends oddly as he reaches out. He then gets into the vehicle while holding the child, whose body appears to float against his chest as she shifts from one side to the other, with nothing visibly supporting her. Finally, as the woman pushes the car door shut, its edge visibly bends against her hands before springing back flat against the side of the vehicle. Her hand also appears to blend into the window frame. Throughout the clip, both people move in unnatural ways.

Also, the girl in the video appears younger and smaller than Lilibet did several months earlier. [A post](https://www.instagram.com/p/DZKE3Hpm46M/?hl=en&img_index=1) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125235528/https://www.instagram.com/p/DZKE3Hpm46M/?hl=en&img_index=1) ) by Meghan Markle (@meghan) on Instagram on June 4, 2026, shows Lilibet appearing bigger and taller:

*(Image source: post by @meghan on Instagram.)*

#### News searches

Lead Stories searched [Google News](https://news.google.com/search?q=%22Harry%2C%22%20%22Meghan%2C%22%20%22shoving%2C%22%20and%20%22Lilibet.%22&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125235719/https://news.google.com/search?q=%22Harry%2C%22%20%22Meghan%2C%22%20%22shoving%2C%22%20and%20%22Lilibet.%22&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen) ) and [Yahoo News](https://news.search.yahoo.com/search;_ylt=A2RRbgqsYgdrBwMA64DQtDMD;_-?fr=uh3_news_web&.tsrc=uh3_news_web&fr2=sb-top&p=%22Harry%2C%22+%22Meghan%2C%22+%22shoving%2C%22+and+%22Lilibet.%22) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125223710/https://news.search.yahoo.com/search;_ylt=A2RRbgqsYgdrBwMA64DQtDMD;_-?fr=uh3_news_web&.tsrc=uh3_news_web&fr2=sb-top&p=%22Harry%2C%22+%22Meghan%2C%22+%22shoving%2C%22+and+%22Lilibet.%22) ) and found no matching reports about the claim from established news outlets using the search terms: "Harry," "Meghan," "shoving" and "Lilibet."
