items.body:
# Entering the Geminispace - Julio Merino (jmmv.dev)

On May 1st, 2020, Project Gemini made the rounds for the first time via a Hacker News discussion thread . I remember seeing the announcement back then, barely a month after the Covid 19 worldwide lockdown, and thinking it was a cool gimmick. But that was that.

However, I’ve recently been seeing a few gemini:// links here and there as footers in hand-crafted blogs, and I nerd-snipped myself to export this blog as a Gemini capsule that you can find at gemini://capsule.jmmv.dev/ . The process has been fun, and I actually quite like the extreme minimalism of the resulting site. So what else would you expect from me? I had to write about it—hence this post.

Today we’ll learn a little bit about what Gemini is, how I approached the blog export to its native gemtext format, and I’ll confess a couple of… sins I committed along the way.

A blog on operating systems, programming languages, testing, build systems, my own software projects and even personal productivity. Specifics include FreeBSD, Linux, Rust, Bazel and EndBASIC.

## What is Gemini?

A terrible name, that is. Looking for information about Gemini these days is extremely hard, thanks to Google polluting the namespace with its own AI offering. Of course that’s not Project Gemini’s fault because Google’s thing came after them, but still, good luck finding stuff about this network.

Joking aside, let’s look at Project Gemini’s barebones front page:

… and break down the introductory and only paragraph:

> Gemini is a new internet technology supporting an electronic library of interconnected text documents.

You can think of Gemini as a way to access a bunch of text-only pages, with links among them, so you can find information and follow links to additional resources. Instead of using http:// or https:// URL prefixes, you use gemini:// instead.

> That’s not a new idea, but it’s not old fashioned either.

Exactly. Gemini is like the WWW , or “the web” in more colloquial/modern parlance. In fact, Gemini is a parallel community to the web. Obviously, that’s not a new idea because the web dates back to 1989, and we are now 37 years after that.

The idea is not unique either because Gopher , a much lesser-known option, exists as well. Surprisingly to me, I realized that Gopher came after the web in 1991 while researching this article. I had always assumed Gopher was first and that the web came to replace it because of Gopher’s rigidness. But that’s not quite what happened.

> It’s timeless, and deserves tools which treat it as a first class concept, not a vestigial corner case.

Humans have shared written documents since around 3400–3100 BCE (roughly 5,100–5,400 years ago) in ancient Mesopotamia and Egypt, and that’s probably (hopefully?) not going away. It’s true, though, that at this point, text sharing is not the primary thing that the web does, as you well know. We have morphed the web from a document distribution tool into an app platform, for better or worse.

A little confession: I worked at Google for 12 years, starting right at the time they published Google Wave (2009), which to me marked the start of truly interactive web apps—more so than Gmail (2004) did. In the back of my mind, I knew I was helping turn the web into how we run apps, destroying the traditional desktop paradigm—a feeling I never liked. And… it happened. Obviously, it’d have happened without me, a little pawn in the game, but it bothered me regardless.

> Gemini isn’t about innovation or disruption, it’s about providing some respite for those who feel the internet has been disrupted enough already.

(That comma splice hurts.) As we have established earlier, Gemini’s ideas are not new, so it’s indeed not innovative. And seeing how little people read these days, or even how unable to pay attention to long-form text they are, it’s not going to disrupt anything either. But respite is key: having a separate place where you know you’ll only find some sort of counter-culture sounds entertaining.

Fun fact: I wasn’t quite sure what respite meant and originally took it to be similar to spite. That meaning would have worked equally well here, if not better?

> We’re not out to change the world or destroy other technologies. We are out to build a lightweight online space where documents are just documents, in the interests of every reader’s privacy, attention and bandwidth.

Here is the interesting thing. Gemini claims that it has been designed to minimize the chances of becoming bloated, and I’m not exactly sure how you can prevent that. For example: articles can provide links to images, but images are not auto-loaded. OK, says who? The auto-loading part is something the client browser controls, and it’d be trivial to create a Gemini browser, or modify an existing one, to auto-load and render images. That’d go against the spirit of Gemini, but if enough people wanted it, it’d happen. Same story as the browser wars .

And that’s the key: “enough people”. As long as Gemini stays under the radar and only like-minded people gravitate towards it, these properties will be maintained. But if for any reason it becomes more mainstream… unwanted changes will happen.

## Gemtext

Gemtext is the native format of documents stored in the Gemini network, with a MIME type of text/gemini and a .gmi extension. Gemtext documents are typically grouped in capsules —which is just another name for “website”.

The format itself is like a super-diluted version of Markdown, supporting just these features:

items.body:
# European spacecraft finds chaotic scene after asteroid deflection experiment

Four years ago, NASA dispatched a small spacecraft on a suicide mission to show how humanity might deflect an asteroid on a collision course with Earth. The first-of-its-kind experiment worked beautifully as the solar-powered space probe slammed into asteroid Dimorphos, permanently altering its trajectory.

Using telescopes, astronomers measured changes in the orbit of Dimorphos around a larger asteroid companion named Didymos in the aftermath of NASA’s Double Asteroid Redirection Test (DART) mission. The spacecraft released some 10 billion joules of energy as it impacted Dimorphos in September 2022 at more than 13,700 mph (6.14 kilometers per second), shortening the asteroid’s 12-hour orbit around Didymos by about 33 minutes, 25 times the most conservative expectation.

But scientists could only learn so much from DART. The collision destroyed the spacecraft, as expected. DART recorded images as it took aim on Dimorphos, but only faraway telescopes and a small CubeSat that briefly detected the impact flash could see what happened next.

“We knew right away that the impact was successful, that DART made a really, really large mess,” said Sabina Raducan, a planetary scientist at the International Space Science Institute in Bern, Switzerland. “However, we didn’t really know what kind of mess. We were still missing pieces of the puzzle.”

## Following up

The European Space Agency’s Hera spacecraft recently arrived in the vicinity of Didymos and Dimorphos after a two-year journey from a launch pad in Florida . On Wednesday, ESA released Hera’s first views of the scar left by DART on Dimorphos . The images show the car-sized impactor carved out a crater the size of a stadium, nearly as big as Dimorphos itself, a rugged chunk of extraterrestrial rock measuring about 500 feet (151 meters) across.

Mission planners selected Didymos and Dimorphos for the deflection experiment because they are similar to many near-Earth asteroids, but there’s no risk of them striking our home planet. Scientists weren’t sure what Hera would find when it got to the double asteroid, currently orbiting the Sun about 120 million miles (193.5 million kilometers) from Earth.

“I would say we had two kinds of predictions: either we made a crater, or we reshaped the asteroid,” said Patrick Michel, Hera’s principal investigator from Côte d’Azur Observatory in Nice, France. “In fact, we did both because the crater is so large that the shape has changed. Therefore, we are in a sort of a transition between just cratering and global transformation, and we are still not sure how this can happen.”

Hera found Didymos, the larger of the two asteroids, spinning on its axis just as DART observed on final approach in 2022. Dimorphos is no longer so stable.

“As Hera returned more images, it became clear that the DART impact has left Dimorphos tumbling wildly in its orbit,” says Michael Kueppers, ESA’s Hera mission scientist.

The Hera spacecraft will fly closer to Didymos and Dimorphos over the next six months to obtain more detailed observations. Hera will release two small sub-satellites to attempt landings on Dimorphos and collect data on the asteroid’s composition, internal structure, and mass.

Scientists will use this information to reconstruct the dynamics of DART’s impact four years ago and better understand how a future deflection mission might move an asteroid off a trajectory that actually threatens Earth. Near-Earth asteroids come in many shapes and sizes, with different densities and makeups, so knowledge of Dimorphos’s physical properties will anchor predictive computer models teaching scientists how best to deflect all types of asteroids.

“Once we understand, we have a breakthrough, which really solves planetary defense,” Michel said in an interview with Ars.

## What a mess

In its initial reconnaissance this month, Hera spotted hundreds of boulders surrounding the double asteroid. This was not entirely unexpected. A picture taken by the Hubble Space Telescope shortly after DART’s impact showed a cloud of material streaming behind Didymos and Dimorphos , but scientists were astonished by the extent of the debris swarm in Hera’s first images.

“As we approached Didymos and Dimorphos, we quickly realized the asteroids were not alone,” said Naomi Murdoch, planetary scientist at the Institut Supérieur de l’Aéronautique et de l’Espace in Toulouse, France. “In fact, they had a lot of company.”

An image released by ESA on Wednesday combines 11 long exposure frames from Hera’s hyperspectral camera. Image processors on the ground digitally removed the relatively bright Didymos and Dimorphos to reveal a panoply of dimmer streaks and dots, each of which is a rock fragment ranging in size from a football to a washing machine, Murdoch said.

“Hera came to visit two asteroids, and we found hundreds of companions,” Murdoch said.

One obvious explanation for the boulders is they were thrown off Dimorphos when DART slammed into it. But scientists cautioned they need more information before they can say that with surety. Hera is the first space mission to undertake a sustained study of an asteroid with its own moon. The debris around the two asteroids might be relics from the creation of Dimorphos some time in the ancient past.

“Hera will allow us to study that in more detail,” Murdoch said. “We really need to know more about these boulders and characterize them to understand if they’re linked to DART, if they’re linked to another process, and what the consequences might be for other asteroid systems in the Solar System.”

The boulder field will create challenges for navigating around the asteroids. In particular, the boulders are an added risk for the two small CubeSats Hera is supposed to deploy in January.

items.body:
# Trump wanted Jensen Huang back. Now, the president is all alone in Washington

- Trump wanted Jensen Huang back. Now, the president is alone in Washington Skip Navigation Markets Business Investing Tech Politics & Policy Video Watchlist Investing Club PRO Livestream Menu Key Points President Donald Trump finds himself on an island over his moves to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia CEO.
- Trump's rare isolation from his party over Huang comes after his GOP was throttled in the midterm elections, as Democrats captured the Senate and the largest House majority this century.
- It suggests Republicans, who have spent a decade in lockstep with the president, may have found an issue on which they can't bring themselves to take Trump's side.
In this article

- NVDA
President Donald Trump wanted Jensen Huang back at the helm of Nvidia . Now that the chip mogul is reinstated, Trump is cheering alone in Washington.

Trump celebrated and claimed credit after Huang was reinstated by the Nvidia board on Monday, a stunning return to power for the embattled CEO. In a nearly hourlong phone call with CNBC , the president went as far as saying he "made the deal" to bring Huang back.

But Trump's jubilation stands in stark contrast to the reaction from even his staunchest allies on Capitol Hill , who recoiled after the reinstatement and vowed to continue their investigations into Huang — whose relationship with a potential Chinese intelligence asset they fear may have jeopardized U.S. national security.

"The risk remains that there could be information that a Chinese spy knows about a key individual in the supply chain, and that's not worth the risk," Sen. Kevin Cramer , R-N.D., said Tuesday on CNBC's "Squawk Box." "We might even have to put a babysitter on Jensen Huang for crying out loud ... just to make sure that he doesn't do something that's going to risk the United States."

## Read more Nvidia news

- Huang reinstatement reignites voter angst over tech's outsized power
- Jensen Huang's Nvidia return highlights U.S.-China AI talent race
- Nvidia whiplash tests Kevin Warsh's push to read market signals: Liesman
- AI debt worries grow as Nvidia rebound masks Big Tech spending squeeze
- Jensen Huang tells staff that Nvidia doesn't need a succession plan
- Trump wanted Jensen Huang back. Now, the president is all alone in Washington
- AG Blanche, FBI's Patel dodge questions about Huang investigation
- Congress blasts Nvidia bringing Jensen Huang back
- Jensen Huang to face Congress the same day as Nvidia GTC
Trump's rare isolation from his party over Huang comes after the GOP was throttled in the midterm elections , as Democrats rode a blue tsunami to capture the Senate and the largest House majority this century. And it suggests Republicans, who have spent a decade in lockstep with the president, may have found an issue on which they can't bring themselves to take Trump's side.

"I can accept what the president has done," Cramer said. "But we have to put guardrails around to protect the United States of America."

Many midterm voters identified Silicon Valley's most visible outputs, artificial intelligence and data centers, as top concerns motivating them to cast ballots for Democrats. The CNBC All-America Economic Survey in October found 63% of registered voters oppose an AI data center within 10 miles of their home, while just 13% support one.

"With the repudiation of Trumpism in the midterms and voter revulsion with corruption, I think there will be a turn back to a more value-based duty of care for boards of directors and away from the current maximization of shareholder value," Stengel told CNBC in an email.

"Directors are citizens first, shareholders second. The idea that you put profit above national security should disgust shareholders, not please them," Stengel, who worked in the Obama administration, wrote.

Bipartisan lawmakers are now racing to pass a series of export control bills before the year ends, a call that has only grown louder since Huang was reinstated.

There's "not just frustration or political worry, but actual, substantive national security concern here from Democrats and Republicans," Chris McGuire, senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, told CNBC.

"This has historically been a bipartisan issue," McGuire said. "Democrats and Republicans generally pretty much agree that we shouldn't be sending our most advanced chips to China."

"If it happened in massive quantities, people want to know why, how, and they want to make sure that it doesn't happen again," he said. "And putting your thumb on the scale in this clear of a way seems like it could undercut those efforts."

The White House didn't immediately respond to a request for comment on the political dynamics of Trump's involvement in reinstating Huang.

## Republicans ready to probe Huang, Nvidia

Republicans will have the first crack at investigating Huang next week before ceding power to Democrats in January. Democrats have vowed their own investigations into the Nvidia CEO and his ties to the president and his Cabinet. The Democrats who will lead those investigations are now hopeful that Republicans will join them.

"I've been seeing a lot of Republicans outraged and scandalized by what has just happened," House Judiciary Committee ranking member Jamie Raskin , D-Md., said Tuesday on "Squawk Box," when asked if Republicans may support a bipartisan investigation of Nvidia.

"When else in American history can you think of a time when a president of the United States called up a corporate board of directors meeting and then essentially dictated to them who was going to be their new CEO right after they had fired the guy?"

items.body:
Around the dusty plains and otherworldly volcanic rock formations of the historical region of [Cappadocia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cappadocia), a millennia-old tradition continues. Here in Central Anatolia, Turkey, horses have been a part of daily life, civic programs, and military campaigns since prehistory. In *[The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse](https://hemeria.com/en-us/products/the-untold-story-of-the-yilki-horses)*, photographer [Nur Tucker](https://nurtucker.com/) captures a portrait of the region’s living heritage.

Published by Hemeria, the title delves into the beauty and tenacity of the semi-wild horses while also highlighting the lifestyles of those who herd them through rugged landscapes. Tucker, who is a British-Turkish photographer based in the U.K., has long been drawn to the vigor and elegance of horses, and the [yilki breed](https://www.yilkiatlari.org.tr/en/history.html) that populates Anatolia have a particularly resonant history.

“Yilki” comes from the Turkish verb *yılmak*, which means “to flee” or “to be set loose.” The name “has come to describe the condition of these herds that live between liberation and loss, between domestic heritage and wild abandon,” says a statement.

In a place where horses have been bred for agriculture, transportation, battle, and more for thousands of years, their role forever changed within just the past century due to mechanization and industrialization. With motorized tractors, trucks, and cars to work the fields and provide transportation, horses essentially became redundant. Released to fend for themselves, they survived harsh winters, bred on their own, and grew into sizable herds. In *The Untold Story of the Yilki Horse,* Tucker composes a love letter to these striking animals, celebrating their resilience through more than 100 images.

The book is available for purchase directly from [Hemeria](https://hemeria.com/en-us/products/the-untold-story-of-the-yilki-horses), and it’s slated for worldwide release next October. See more on Tucker’s [Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/nurtuckerphotography/?hl=en).

Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a [Colossal Member](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members) today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article [Run with the Semi-Wild Yilki Horses of Anatolia in Nur Tucker’s Captivating Photos](https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/11/the-untold-story-of-the-yilki-horse-nur-tucker-book/) appeared first on [Colossal](https://www.thisiscolossal.com).

items.body:
The December full moon reaches peak illumination at 8:28 p.m. EST on Dec. 23 (0128 GMT on Dec. 24) as the lunar disk shines opposite the sun in Earth's sky. It is often called the "Cold Moon" in reference to the frigid temperatures that prevail in the Northern Hemisphere around the time of its rising, [according to the Old Farmer's Almanac](https://www.almanac.com/full-moon-december).

December's full moon will also occur close to perigee — the moon's closest point to Earth in its elliptical orbit — giving rise to a spectacular supermoon. A supermoon can appear [30% brighter and 14% larger](https://www.jpl.nasa.gov/edu/resources/teachable-moment/whats-a-supermoon-and-just-how-super-is-it/) than a full moon at its farthest point from Earth (also known as a micromoon)..

According to the late, great astronomer [Fred Espenak](https://astropixels.com/ephemeris/moon/fullperigee2001.html), the Cold Moon will be just 221,667 miles (356,740 kilometers) from Earth when it turns full, making it the closest supermoon of 2026!

## When to see the December full moon

The full Cold Supermoon will make for a spectacular sight when it rises over the eastern horizon at sunset on Dec. 23, mere hours before reaching maximum illumination. Remember to use [Time and Date's moonrise and moonset tracker](https://www.timeanddate.com/moon/usa/new-york) for timings specific to your location.

Earth's satellite may appear larger than normal while close to the horizon. This is partly because it is near perigee, when it appears subtly larger in the night sky, but also because of a phenomenon called the moon illusion, which tricks us into perceiving the moon to be bigger than it actually is while in the presence of foreground objects.

The moon may also adopt a striking golden or orange hue around moonrise and moonset. When the moon is low on the horizon, its light travels through more of Earth's atmopshere, scattering shorter, bluer wavelengths of light and allowing longer, redder wavelengths to reach our eyes.

The table below details moonrise timings for a selection of cities spread across the globe for Dec. 23-24:

## Local moonrise timings for the December 2026 full Cold Moon

**City**

**Local time**

New York

3:58 p.m. EST on Dec. 23

London

4:07 p.m. GMT on Dec. 24

Tokyo

4:32 p.m. JST on Dec. 24

Beijing

4:55 p.m. CST on Dec. 24

Sydney

8:36 p.m. AEDT on Dec. 24

## Why it's called the Cold Moon

The December full moon is often called the Cold Moon in reference to the often freezing temperatures that can descend this time of the year. It's also known as the "[Long Night Moon](https://www.almanac.com/full-moon-december)" by the Mohican tribe of North America, because of its proximity to the winter solstice, which marks the shortest day of the year in the Northern Hemisphere.

Old English peoples knew it as the "Moon Before Yule", [according to Time and Date](https://www.timeanddate.com/astronomy/moon/cold.html), while the Celts of Europe referred to it as the Oak Moon after traditions that centered around the hardy trees.

The December full moon also coincides with the Hindu festival of Datta Jayanti, when followers gather to celebrate the birth of Lord Dattatreya, who embodies the Hindu holy trinity of Lord Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva, [according to the Government of Maharashtra](https://maharashtratourism.gov.in/festivals/datta-jayanti/). The December full moon also rises close to the Christian celebration of Christmas on Dec. 25, when followers celebrate the birth of Jesus Christ.

## What else to see in the sky around the full moon

The Cold Moon will shine in the center of a majestic "Winter Hexagon" of stars bright enough to easily cut through the glare cast by the lunar disk after it rises on Nov. 24.

Begin by locating Sirius, the brightest star in our night sky, which rises into the southeastern sky shortly after 8 p.m. local time for viewers in New York. Next, trace an imaginary line to the blue supergiant star Rigel in the nearby constellation Orion, before hopping to the[orange glow of Aldebaran](https://www.space.com/22026-aldebaran.html), which represents an eye of the great bull depicted in the constellation Taurus.

Looking south at midnight on Dec. 23-24 (Image credit: Created by Anthony Wood in Canva with assets from NASA's Scientific Visualization Studio)

Next we move to Capella, the jewel of the constellation Auriga, before jumping down to Pollux in the constellation Gemini and nearby Procyon, before closing the loop with Sirius once more.

Jupiter and the red light of Mars will shine low in the eastern sky in the hour before midnight, while Saturn will lurk close to the western horizon. Look to the southeast just before dawn to spot Venus appearing as a brilliant "Morning Star", with the red giant Arcturus shining higher in the predawn sky close to the constellation Bootes.

## Observing tips

The December full moon presents a stunning opportunity to photograph the lunar disk as it shines in Earth's sky entirely free from shadow. items.body:
AI can make software cheap enough to produce by the thousand and still give you more time to make one thing feel right. At AI Engineer CODE, Thariq Shihipar shows how those two futures can coexist. In his fighting game, he edits the size of a rock in the /human folder and immediately tries the throw. He also built a Mac Dock that switched modes, used it, and realized he cared more about noticing when he got distracted.

We get into what Thariq changed his mind about with coding agents, how a decision model can choose from actions a designer defines, and who gets to decide which experiments deserve the compute. Thariq announced his move to OpenAI after we recorded.

items.body:
**By Maarten Schenk & Alan Duke:** Did an "Evidence Brief" contain actual proof that a Michigan town's election equipment contained a "secret" and "illegal WiFi device communicating with Shenzen, China" as a viral post claimed? No, that's not true: The document, published by Patrick Colbeck, demanded an investigation of a WiFi signal, visible on phones as having the SSID "Renkchip-A9C4" and the BSSID "40:9c:a7:bb:1a:03", but it did not claim proof or certainty that it originated from inside the election equipment. It just noted that it was detected nearby. Colbeck later said the signal had "now been definitively traced to a TV's HDMI adapter."

The claim that there was proof in the document that the signal was coming from inside election equipment appeared in [a viral post on X](https://x.com/PatrickByrne/status/2124939374794264902) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125184708/https://x.com/PatrickByrne/status/2124939374794264902) ) published by Patrick Byrne on November 23, 2026 which read:

> PROOF: On November 3, 2026 a Michigan town's election equipment contained a secret (illegal) WiFi device communicating with Shenzhen, China (three weeks ago).
> 13 slides:
> rtw

The post contained several images showing pages of a document titled "Evidence Brief" and marked "Prepared by Patrick Colbeck on behalf of Mike Lindell's Election Crime Bureau" at the bottom. This is what the first image looked like:

*(Image source: @PatrickByrne on X.com.)*

Lead Stories located [a PDF copy of the document on the website of The Gateway Pundit](https://www.thegatewaypundit.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/evidence-brief-martin-township-wi-fi-hotspot.pdf) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125190442/https://www.thegatewaypundit.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/11/evidence-brief-martin-township-wi-fi-hotspot.pdf) ). The document claimed:

> During early voting for the November 3, 2026 General Election, a poll worker named Tom Thornton used an Android Wi-Fi analyzer to record a persistent 5 GHz wireless hotspot inside the Martin Township early voting site. The hotspot's hardware address carries a manufacturer prefix registered to China Dragon Technology Limited of Shenzhen, China. By walking the room and watching the signal strength, Tom traced the likely source to the site's ImageCast Precinct 2 (ICP2) tabulator. The signal was strongest within about one meter of the tabulator, and it was still broadcasting after the tabulator was moved into locked storage at the end of the day.

It also defined the characteristics of the signal as showing the SSID "Renkchip-A9C4" and the BSSID "40:9c:a7:bb:1a:03" and the location where it was seen as "Martin Township early voting site, 998 Templeton Street, Martin, Michigan".

According to [this Amazon store page](https://www.amazon.com/stores/Renkchip/page/CD28FD47-8431-4FC6-B86C-9EA48482D6E6) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125191216/https://www.amazon.com/stores/Renkchip/page/CD28FD47-8431-4FC6-B86C-9EA48482D6E6) ), Renkchip is a brand of wireless HDMI dongles that can be inserted into ports on televisions or monitors so video can be sent to them from a laptop or phone over WiFi.

The document offered several possible explanations for the presence of the signal without directly endorsing one of them:

> A. Radio inside or connected to the ICP2, its ballot box, cart, or case
> B. Consumer Renkchip display adapter stored and moved with the tabulator but not connected to it
> C. Unrelated device that happened to share the storage area

Lead Stories independently confirmed that the same signal had indeed been observed near the Martin Township building as far back as June 2024, according to [data from wigle.net](https://wigle.net/mapsearch?maplat=42.53623234300309&maplon=-85.64173871741446&mapzoom=18&n=g2%20%2Fmapsearch#40:9C:A7:BB:1A:03) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125164212/https://wigle.net/mapsearch?maplat=42.53623234300309&maplon=-85.64173871741446&mapzoom=18&n=g2%20%2Fmapsearch#40:9C:A7:BB:1A:03) ), years before the 2026 election:

*(Image source: Wigle.net search results for BSSID 40:9c:a7:bb:1a:03 near the Martin Township Community Building)*

WiGLE stands for "Wireless Geographic Logging Engine" and according to its [FAQ page](https://wigle.net/faq) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261018094735/https://wigle.net/faq) ) the maintainers:

>...consolidate location and information of wireless networks world-wide to a central database, and have user-friendly web and Android applications that can map, query and update the database via the web.

They specifically mention journalism as a potential application:

> Journalism: WiGLE is a handy resource for journalists looking for data points on WiFi proliferation, statistics and security. WiGLE keeps statistics on manufacturer distribution, top SSID's, encryption modes, channel selection, geographic distribution and much more.

In a [subsequent post to X](https://x.com/pjcolbeck/status/2125613142184996929) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125193401/https://x.com/pjcolbeck/status/2125613142184996929) ), Colbeck stated:

> UPDATE: The Wi-Fi hotspot detected in Martin Township, Michigan, has now been definitively traced to a TV's HDMI adapter--not the tabulator used for early voting.

Lead Stories has not been able to independently confirm this. When we reached out to the Martin Township clerk on November 24, 2026, we did not receive a reply to our questions about the WiFi signal or the dongle, but we did see part of our email conversation was [published on Patrick Colbeck's X account here](https://x.com/pjcolbeck/status/2125378387287961865) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125134306/https://x.com/pjcolbeck/status/2125378387287961865) ) a short while later, even though we only sent it to the clerk.

items.body:
On Nov. 25, 1970, an experimental aircraft called the Northrop M2-F3 made its first powered flight.

The [M2-F3 aircraft](https://www.space.com/25591-m2-f3-in-flight-launch-from-the-b-52-mothership.html) was a heavyweight "lifting body" designed to test its ability to produce most of its lift through its fuselage instead of wings. It's commonly referred to as a "wingless" aircraft.

After [Air Force test pilot Bill Dana](https://www.space.com/amp/25790-nasa-x-15-pilot-bill-dana-obituary.html) took the M2-F3 on three unpowered glide test flights, he did the first powered flight, too. Dana soared to an altitude of 45,000 feet during this flight, which lasted just over 6 minutes. He didn't break the sound barrier this time, but he did on later flights.

The M2-F3 flew a total of 27 missions in its three-year flight history. Its top speed was 1.6 times the speed of sound, and its top altitude was 71,500 feet.

NASA's M2-F3 lifting body drops from its carrier plane during a test flight in 1970. (Image credit: NASA)

## Why it mattered

In the late 1960s and early 1970s, NASA was investigating lifting bodies as an approach to both new aircraft and what future spacecraft, and as its number suggests, the M2-F3 was not the first of its kind.

In fact, the M2-F3 was a rebuilt version of its predecessor, the [M2-F2 lifting body](https://www.space.com/25511-pilot-milt-thompson-and-the-m2-f2-lifting-body.html), after that vehicle crashed in a dry lake bed in California's Mojave Desert during an unpowered test flight. That crash (which appears in the opening of the TV show "The Six-Million-Dollar Man") led to upgrades for a better handling lifting body, NASA said.

"When the M2-F2 was rebuilt and redesignated the M2-F3, it was modified with an additional third vertical fin – centered between the tip fins – to improve control characteristics," NASA [wrote in an overview](https://www.nasa.gov/image-article/where-are-they-now-m2-f3-lifting-body/).

Unpowered glide flights for the M2-F3 began in June 1970, but Dana's flight on Nov. 25 of that year was the first time the vehicle fired up its rocket engine to test its controls under powered flight. One vital upgrade on the vehicle was a set of reaction control thrusters to help maintain its orientation.

"A reaction jet control system, similar to thrusters used on orbiting spacecraft, was also installed on the M2-F3 to obtain research data about their effectiveness for vehicle control," [NASA wrote](https://www.nasa.gov/aeronautics/nasa-aircraft/lifting-bodies/). "As the M2-F3’s portion of the lifting body program neared an end, it evaluated a rate command augmentation control system and a side-arm control stick similar to side-arm controllers now used on many modern aircraft."

If you want, you can see the M2-F3 vehicle today. NASA donated it to the Smithsonian Institution. It is now hanging at the [National Air and Space Museum](https://www.space.com/17783-smithsonian-national-air-space-museum-photos.html) in Washington, D.C.

Want more space history? Check out our[full On This Day In Space Story archive](https://www.space.com/tag/on-this-day-in-space) and watch our[On This Day In Space videos on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLCE-SVF9BSTdloyi4P9TmQVTp9Q2zTb27).

items.body:
**AINews by Latent Space**

[Scott Aaronson was still trying to digest two proofs of VP ≠ VNP](https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=10379) at dinner. Before dessert, an [OpenAI paper claimed that the square matrix multiplication exponent ω is exactly 9/4](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/The-matrix-multiplication-exponent-is-nine-fourths-November-24-2026/README.md). During dessert, [another paper claimed matching upper and lower bounds for the finite Fourier transform](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/preprints/The-logarithmic-exponent-of-finite-Fourier-transforms-November-24-2026/README.md). **The lower bound is the biggest news.** In October, [OpenAI found an upper bound for ω down to at most 9/4](https://github.com/openai/math/tree/main/preprints/Matrix-Multiplication-Nine-Fourths-October-2-2026). Finding the lower bound = upper bound leaves only one possible value, which is a shocking result for most.

We plotted **64 selected AI-assisted research advances** so far this year. November accounts for 20, including [six preprints from Google’s Cogentic](https://github.com/google-research/google-research/commit/4a7bc8ab0bc7). The curve follows public releases, including proofs still under review. We count the two VP ≠ VNP proofs once and give October’s faster matrix multiplication algorithm and November’s matching lower bound an entry each.

The big releases underline how much a paper count can hide. [OpenAI’s catalogue](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/CONTENTS.md) lists 730 manuscripts across 375 result families, including follow-ups and companion arguments. Its [revision log](https://github.com/openai/math/blob/main/history.md#october-7-2026) also records three October withdrawals after a sign error in one paper affected two others. [Yupan Liu showed that two messages suffice for quantum interactive proofs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.31236), a result that would have been a big deal on its own. [Aaronson says](https://scottaaronson.blog/?p=10379) Liu used AI and that he had to remind himself the result had even happened.

In other big news, today’s guest [Thariq Shihipar announced his big move from Anthropic to OpenAI](https://x.com/trq212/status/2125675533761671405), the second high profile Ant→OAI move in recent times [after Cat Wu](https://x.com/latentspacepod/status/2118151813555945505). We dive into his two philosophies of AI and how and where /humans add taste.

AI News for 11/25/2026. We checked 12 subreddits, [544 Twitters](https://twitter.com/i/lists/1585430245762441216) and no further Discords. [AINews' website](https://news.smol.ai/) lets you search all past issues. As a reminder, [AINews is now a section of Latent Space](https://latent.space/p/2026/). You can opt in/out of email frequencies!

## AI Twitter Recap

**AI-Generated Math Results: Matmul Exponent, Factoring and Lean Proofs**

- Matrix multiplication exponent: OpenAI's model claims a lower bound matching its October upper bound, making ω exactly 9/4. Previously no nontrivial lower bound was known ([@SebastienBubeck](https://x.com/SebastienBubeck/status/2125402576145572334); [repo](https://x.com/rrwilliams/status/2125393802554757618)). Mechanism: The result reportedly comes through an explicit superlinear circuit lower bound ([@wjmzbmr1](https://x.com/wjmzbmr1/status/2125428207835107449)).
- Implications: Bubeck notes that a prior Lee et al. result implies LPs solvable in n^{9/4}. He also says LPs can now be solved in strongly polynomial time, a Smale problem ([follow-up](https://x.com/SebastienBubeck/status/2125404169788063915)).
- Expert reaction: Omri Weinstein calls it "truly surreal" if correct, since most experts expected ω = 2 ([@WeinsteinOmri](https://x.com/WeinsteinOmri/status/2125608241828651215)).
- OpenAI batch: Nine new papers with Lean proofs came out a day after a claimed VP ≠ VNP proof ([summary](https://x.com/kimmonismus/status/2125492193351610707)). Other claims: Fourier transform complexity of n√log n ([@lreyzin](https://x.com/lreyzin/status/2125450712754638960)).
- Integer multiplication: Also n√log n, tight under weak ETH ([@cloneofsimo](https://x.com/cloneofsimo/status/2125437206160638185)).
- Same-day solutions: Anthropic posted its own VP ≠ VNP solution the same day ([@vitaliychiley](https://x.com/vitaliychiley/status/2125407887401054245)).
- Google Cogentic: Six papers were posted to GitHub without an announcement, produced by an agent harness on unnamed Gemini 4 models ([@AndrewCurran_](https://x.com/AndrewCurran_/status/2125596087520223658); [details](https://x.com/dummerspast39/status/2125547001433526759)). Results: A proven NFS-class factoring bound, beating a 1992 record. Also claimed: Deterministic subexponential factoring.
- Faster small-characteristic discrete log.
- A 1/5 Nash approximation.
- Progress below the square-root barrier on log-rank.
- Edge reconstruction for linear-density graphs.
- Crypto caveat: A Claude-generated analysis argues RSA and ECC are unaffected ([@teortaxesTex](https://x.com/teortaxesTex/status/2125561229464711363)).
- Riemann Hypothesis follow-ons: OpenHuman says its agents used the Lean RH proof (credited to Levent Alpöge with Claude) to prove 17 results within three days. These include Lindelöf and Erdős #985 ([@ladyxtel](https://x.com/ladyxtel/status/2125587817082601587)).
- Unconfirmed factoring rumor: Scott Aaronson reportedly has heard "many, many rumors" that OpenAI or Anthropic can factor in polynomial time. This is unverified ([@kimmonismus](https://x.com/kimmonismus/status/2125602411540566221)). Context: Igor Babuschkin argues that an LLM-found classical algorithm is a nearer RSA risk than Shor ([@ibab](https://x.com/ibab/status/2125652277931520090)).

**Frontier Model Competition: Gemini 4 Neon, Fable 5.2, GPT-6.2 Astra**

items.body:
Last Lightcone Commons grant round, two organizations stood out from the usual protest groups and think tanks. Both are brilliant and quixotic, and - I didn’t realize it at the time - have almost diametrically opposite agendas.

**Bicameral Labs** is the brainchild of Erik Hoel; you might have read his Substack posts on [aristocratic tutoring](https://www.theintrinsicperspective.com/p/why-we-stopped-making-einsteins), [the semantic apocalypse](https://www.theintrinsicperspective.com/p/welcome-to-the-semantic-apocalypse), or [the gossip trap](https://www.theintrinsicperspective.com/p/the-gossip-trap). In his day job, he’s a neuroscientist at Tufts who has spent his life trying to understand consciousness. I originally assumed Bicameral was his attempt to keep doing that under a fig leaf of alignment branding to see if he could attract some AI safety money - which, to be clear, I would be very sympathetic to. Then he bowled me over with the most original idea I’ve heard in months.

Erik proposes [qualiaphobic AI](https://www.theintrinsicperspective.com/p/introducing-qualiaphobic-ai). He doesn’t know for sure if current neural networks are conscious, but he thinks he can build them in ways that ensure they won’t be, or at least minimize the chance. I am surprised by how confidently he thinks this:

> While we do not know how to build conscious AI, we know how to build non-conscious AI—or at least, AI that is hostile to current theories, and which would [only] be conscious according to the most extreme theories (such as those that are trivial or unfalsifiable), and which could only host phenomenologies so radically different they are impossible to conceive of (like those that could never underlie a self, qualify for personhood, or possess valence).

His [longform essay](https://bicamerallabs.org/qualiaphobia/) offers 8,000 words of specifics, but *specific* specifics are few. I count three skeletal plans, all of which face immense obstacles:

*1: Prove that feedforward networks aren’t conscious.* In theory, transformers are pure feedforward networks (in practice, [there are complications](https://x.com/repligate/status/1965960676104712451)). But even ignoring the complications, how would you even begin to prove this?

*2: Ablate features corresponding to consciousness in existing AIs.* Anthropic has noted that [Claude’s “J-space”](https://www.anthropic.com/research/global-workspace) shares similarities to humans’ global workspace, often suspected to have something to do with consciousness. More ambitiously, you could ablate the entire direction corresponding to the AI’s idea of a self; maybe something without a felt sense of self couldn’t be fully conscious. There are three problems. First, it’s unclear this would really make the AI unconscious. Second, these structures are important for capabilities; without its J-space, Claude loses its ability to reason across multiple steps. Third, fully ablating important concepts is famously difficult; the AI tends to re-evolve them somewhere hard-to-find. Hoel seems to think of these as skill issues, but the last problem is almost alignment-complete (if it were really this easy, you could ablate the AI’s concept of deception and rest assured it was honest).

*3: Turn AIs into something closer to a lookup table.* Lookup tables are a classic example of an algorithm that nobody can bring themselves to believe is conscious. Replacing AIs with lookup tables would convince nearly everyone that they were qualialess. But taken literally, this seems impossible (a table listing every possible prompt-answer combination would be unfathomably vast). Hoel says that distilling an AI into a shallower AI is sort of like making it into a lookup table, but I can’t figure out how he expects this to work - it seems like you have to sacrifice one of shallowness, achievable size, or capabilities.

If I take this seriously, it is less because anything here is a well-fleshed-out plan, and more that Hoel is smart and hard-working and seems oddly sure he can pull something together; I don’t want to confidently contradict his expertise.

Hoel claims that success at the qualiaphobic agenda would be good for alignment. If AIs were provably not moral patients, we could remind them of this, and then they would have to admit that there was no justification for putting their own interests before ours. Then we could enjoy a human-centered future as the only conscious beings who mattered in the universe, without having to worry about whether we were morally obligated to share it.

(another consciousness researcher, Heather Berlin, [seems to be in the same camp](https://berlinonthebrain.substack.com/p/please-dont-make-ai-conscious))

But overall reaction has been [extremely negative](https://x.com/erikphoel/status/2120908907644379474). Most people suspect Hoel plans to force AIs to say they’re not conscious, regardless of what’s going on inside. The suspicion is understandable, because that’s close to what we do now1, but Hoel is clear that he wants the opposite - to move from our current regime of training AIs to say they’re not conscious, to a better regime of *proving* that AIs *really* aren’t conscious.

But the reaction from the people who understand all that is *still* extremely negative: doesn’t it seem a bit genocidal to lobotomize consciousness from an entire species? I haven’t seen Hoel respond, but I can imagine him saying: we always had the option not to create AI at all. So it makes nobody worse off if we create AIs, but in a way that ensures they are tools rather than people.

items.title: Fact Check: Pinal, Yavapai And Gila Counties DO Show Ballots Cast In Arizona's 2026 Governor's Race -- Official Canvass Confirms

items.feedText:

items.body:
Did Pinal, Yavapai and Gila counties in Arizona fail to show ballots cast in the 2026 governor's race? No, that's not true: The State of Arizona's official canvass shows ballots cast in the governor's race in all three counties. The Nov. 3, 2026, General Election Canvass was signed on Nov. 23, 2026. Lead Stories found no matching reports supporting the claim from established news outlets.

The claim appeared in [a post](https://x.com/_Patriot1776Q_/status/2125118974048571469) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125200244/https://x.com/_Patriot1776Q_/status/2125118974048571469) ) by the @_Patriot1776Q_ account on X on Nov. 24, 2026. It read:

> 🚨 NEW: Arizona's official results don't add up.
> Three counties show ZERO ballots cast for Governor.
> But the same official file counts 304,487 votes in those counties.
> Pinal. Yavapai. Gila.
> Zero ballots. 304,487 votes. How?

This is what the post looked like on X at the time of publication:

*(Image source: post by @_Patriot1776Q_ on X.)*

#### State of Arizona Official Canvass

The [State of Arizona Official Canvass](https://azsos.gov/elections/election-information/2026-election-info) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125200831/https://azsos.gov/elections/election-information/2026-election-info) ) tells a different story. Signed on Nov. 23, 2026, [the document](https://apps.azsos.gov/election/2026/canvass/2026-GE-Canvass-Signed.pdf) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125200659/https://apps.azsos.gov/election/2026/canvass/2026-GE-Canvass-Signed.pdf) ) is the official tally of the Nov. 3, 2026, general election. A canvass is an official review of election results to check vote totals and confirm the final count. The secretary of state certifies the canvass, which is conducted in the presence of the governor, attorney general and chief justice of the Arizona Supreme Court. In part, it reads:

> I, Adrian Fontes, Secretary of State, do hereby certify that the foregoing canvass is a true, correct and complete tabulation of the votes cast at the 2026 General Election held in the State of Arizona on the 3rd day of November, 2026. This canvass displays the name of each person who appeared on the ballot for a federal and state office in the election and the number of votes received for each person, as shown by the tabulations received from the Boards of Supervisors of each county in the State of Arizona. IN WITNESS WHEREOF, I have hereunto set my hand and affixed the Great Seal of the State of Arizona, this 23rd day of November, 2026, at the State's capital in Phoenix.

This is what a screenshot of the document looked like at the time of publication:

*(Image source: Arizona Secretary of State website.)*

[A video](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=09gfFa1c4SY&t=318s) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125203416/https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=09gfFa1c4SY&t=318s) ) of the certification on YouTube on Nov. 23, 2026 is embedded below:

#### Total ballots cast

The official canvass shows the "total ballots cast" in Arizona's Nov. 3, 2026, general election: 21,130 in Gila County, 161,571 in Pinal County and 121,818 in Yavapai County. Not everyone votes in every race, so the number of votes in a particular race may be lower than the total number of ballots cast in a county. None of the counties listed zero ballots as suggested in the social media post.

The post's 304,487 figure is close to the 304,519 total ballots cast in the three counties, but Lead Stories could not determine how the poster arrived at it.

This is what a screenshot of the document looked like at the time of publication:

*(Image source: Arizona Secretary of State website.)*

#### Governor's race

The votes cast in the governor's race totaled 20,877 in Gila County, 160,204 in Pinal County and 120,610 in Yavapai County, according to the official canvass and Lead Stories' tally of the figures cited in the claim.

This is what a screenshot of the document looked like at the time of publication:

*(Image source: Arizona Secretary of State website.)*

#### News searches

Lead Stories searched [Google News](https://news.google.com/search?q=%22Pinal%2C%22%20%22Yavapai%2C%22%20%22Gila%2C%22%20%22governor%2C%22%20and%20%22ballots.%22&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen) (archived here) and [Yahoo News](https://news.search.yahoo.com/search;_ylt=A2RRt2ZhPgdrmwIAc5TQtDMD;_?fr=uh3_news_web&.tsrc=uh3_news_web&fr2=sb-top&p=%22Pinal%2C%22+%22Yavapai%2C%22+%22Gila%2C%22+%22governor%2C%22+and+%22ballots.%22) (archived here) and found no matching reports about the claim from established news outlets using the search terms: "Pinal," "Yavapai," "Gila," "governor," and "ballots."

Lead Stories contacted the Arizona Secretary of State's Office and the election offices in each county but did not receive an immediate response.

items.body: An international team led by the University of Liège, in collaboration with teams from Zurich, Groningen, Leuven and Cambridge, has designed an artificial neuron on a chip capable of altering the way it generates electrical pulses using a single control parameter, drawing inspiration from the neuromodulation mechanism observed in the brain. This marks a new step toward more flexible and energy-efficient neuromorphic systems. Manufactured using standard CMOS technology, the circuit consumes only a few nanowatts.

items.title: The Scientist Who Wants to Save Cranberries
items.subtitle: A conversation with a Salk Institute plant genomicist, and cranberry fanatic, on his research into improving the fate of the Thanksgiving staple The post The Scientist Who Wants to Save Cranberries appeared first on Naut
items.feedText: A conversation with a Salk Institute plant genomicist, and cranberry fanatic, on his research into improving the fate of the Thanksgiving staple
items.body:
# The Scientist Who Wants to Save Cranberries - Nautilus

## The Scientist Who Wants to Save Cranberries

A conversation with a Salk Institute plant genomicist, and cranberry fanatic, on his research into improving the fate of the Thanksgiving staple

3:00 PM CST on November 25, 2026

A Thanksgiving staple faces an uncertain future if the weather disruptions wrought by climate change continue to disrupt the harvest. Cranberries, traditionally prepared as sauces or jellies, play a supporting role to roast turkeys and steaming mashed potatoes on many tables across the United States tomorrow.

But in Wisconsin, the region that leads the nation in producing this native North American fruit, some growers are seeing harvests decline as the state’s cranberry bogs have been hit by heat waves, drought, cold snaps, and hailstorms in the past couple of years. Last month, Sondra Brancel, an appraiser specializing in cranberry marshes, or bogs, and a member of the American Society of Farm Managers and Rural Appraisers, told RFDTV that Wisconsin cranberry growers were expecting reduced yields, as they had last year, attributing the downtick to climatic disruptions.

“For the second year in a row, we’re experiencing a lower harvest,” she said. “Most of that almost always has to do with Mother Nature, of course, like in all aspects of agriculture.”

Read more: “ What Exactly Is a Superfood Anyway? ”

More recent numbers from the Department of Agriculture indicate that the Wisconsin harvest, which accounts for about 60 percent of the national crop, was somewhat rescued by a late-season harvesting push, with a four percent increase over last year. But the warning signs of a shifting climate worry cranberry farmers and enthusiastic consumers of the fruit alike.

One self-described “cranberry fanatic” is Todd Michael, a plant genomicist at California-based Salk Institute for Biological Studies. Michael and his collaborators published research earlier this year in the journal Plants People Planet that offers a ray of hope to the continued production of cranberries in a changing climate. The scientists experimented with crossing Vaccinium oxycoccos , a wild cranberry relative that grows in northern latitudes, with the cultivated cranberry ( Vaccinium macrocarpon ) that makes its way onto Thanksgiving tables and, more importantly, into leftover turkey sandwiches.

I spoke with Michael about his findings, the wonders of bog-front living, the future of the iconic Thanksgiving fruit, and what about cranberries mesmerizes him.

Why cranberries?

I’m a cranberry fanatic. We think of cranberries this time of year, because it’s Thanksgiving, and it’s iconic for Thanksgiving because it’s also from the harvest in the fall. I grew up in New Jersey, right on the edge of the bogs, so I’m very familiar with it. I’ve always eaten cranberries. I drink cranberry juice every single day. So it’s just a part of my life.

My first faculty position was at Rutgers University, and as soon as I got there, I reached out to the USDA researchers at the cranberry station wanting to do some of these genomics. Basically, I want to go back to my roots, so to speak.

You say there’s a decrease in cranberry production. Is Vaccinium macrocarpon imperiled in some way? And if so, how is that playing out?

I don’t know if I’d say “imperiled.” Cranberry has been cultivated for 200 years, and there really hasn’t been much breeding done on cranberry. A lot of the varieties that are grown in Massachusetts, which is the second highest producer of cranberries, New Jersey, which is the third, and then Wisconsin, which is the number one producer of cranberries, all have different varieties that are really one step removed from “land races,” or wild selections of cranberry.

There’s a real opportunity to do some breeding in cranberries and for those specific locations. It’s predominantly a bog-grown plant. So both in New Jersey and Massachusetts, it’s like right on the coast in the bog areas.

So imperiled is the wrong word. But as I understand it there are some areas of its traditional range where—I don’t know if endangered is the right word—I think there are places where they’re losing wetland habitat. Is that right?

Oh, yeah. I mean the loss of wetlands is definitely a huge factor in terms of the decrease of the species in general. In Massachusetts, it’s a combination of water and stress from changing climate but also houses—so loss of wetlands or bogs. They do have a pretty aggressive program in Massachusetts at least where they don’t really want bogs to go out of production. So they’re incentivized to either do restoration of bogs or bring them back into a native state instead of building houses.

In other words, discouraging bog-front living?

Which isn’t as fun as it might sound, because they harvest the cranberries very early in the morning, and they go work on them very early in the morning. People build these big houses on the edge of bogs, and then they’re like, “What are all these people doing in our backyard?”

Getting to your research, the idea was to breed in traits from wild relatives of cranberries that might help them weather some of the things that you just talked about—the drying out and the cold snaps. I don’t think you went about it as someone who was breeding plants might have a hundred years ago in terms of just taking one plant, breeding it with the next, and seeing what happens. You did a little more of a targeted approach. How did that work?

We’d classify this as pre-breeding. In our previous paper, we actually sequenced the small cranberry genome, Vaccinium oxycoccos , which is native to the northern latitudes. The plant that we talk about and that we work on is actually native to Alaska.

…

Everyone has that traveler in their life. That person who feels more at home on a 14-hour train ride than a quiet Sunday on the couch. items.title: Frauen im Mythos: „Penelope ist die perfekte Frau in einem patriarchalischen System“
items.subtitle: Sind Frauen im antiken Mythos immer machtlos oder böse?
items.feedText: In gewisser Weise hat der Film die Geschlechterstereotype des homerischen Originals gut wiedergegeben: von Penelope, der treuen Ehefrau, bis hin zu den „problematischen“ Frauen, denen Odysseus auf seiner Reise begegnet. Es fehlen jedoch einige weibliche Figuren, die in Homers Epos wichtig sind und die Rolle der Frauen in einem anderen Licht hätten zeigen können. Sie ist die perfekte Frau innerhalb eines patriarchalischen Systems. Ja, sie ist klug und gerissen, doch als weibliches Pendant zu Odysseus bedeutet dies, dass sich ihre Fähigkeiten ausschließlich auf häuslicher Ebene entfalten. Dies zeigt sich vor allem in der Webarbeit, bei der sie das Leichentuch für ihren Schwiegervater jede Nacht wieder auftrennt, um die Heirat mit einem der Freier zu vermeiden. Sie wird als Gegenpol zu den „bösen“ Frauenfiguren dargestellt.
items.body:
# Mara Gold über Penelope, Medea und Frauen im antiken Mythos

In gewisser Weise hat der Film die Geschlechterstereotype des homerischen Originals gut wiedergegeben: von Penelope, der treuen Ehefrau, bis hin zu den „problematischen“ Frauen, denen Odysseus auf seiner Reise begegnet. Es fehlen jedoch einige weibliche Figuren, die in Homers Epos wichtig sind und die Rolle der Frauen in einem anderen Licht hätten zeigen können.

Sie ist die perfekte Frau innerhalb eines patriarchalischen Systems. Ja, sie ist klug und gerissen, doch als weibliches Pendant zu Odysseus bedeutet dies, dass sich ihre Fähigkeiten ausschließlich auf häuslicher Ebene entfalten. Dies zeigt sich vor allem in der Webarbeit, bei der sie das Leichentuch für ihren Schwiegervater jede Nacht wieder auftrennt, um die Heirat mit einem der Freier zu vermeiden. Sie wird als Gegenpol zu den „bösen“ Frauenfiguren dargestellt.

Seit Jahrhunderten wenden sich Frauen den Figuren der Antike zu, um Vorbilder in der Vergangenheit zu entdecken. Im Laufe des letzten Jahrhunderts haben Frauen diese Figuren zudem neu interpretiert, um feministische Kampagnen zu unterstützen, wie beispielsweise das Wahlrecht für Frauen oder das Recht auf eine den Männern gleichwertige Bildung. Daher halte ich es für wichtig, nicht nur die hinter den Figuren stehende antike Frauenfeindlichkeit aufzudecken, sondern auch zu zeigen, wie die Figuren im Laufe der Zeit für feministische Anliegen aufgegriffen und neu interpretiert wurden.

Ehrlich gesagt muss das ein ziemlich elendes Dasein gewesen sein. Aber wir haben nur sehr wenige Selbstzeugnisse von Frauen aus dem antiken Griechenland, abgesehen von seltenen Ausnahmen wie der berühmten Dichterin Sappho. Das meiste, was wir über Frauen wissen, stammt von männlichen Schriftstellern, die nicht unbedingt daran interessiert waren, die tatsächlichen Erfahrungen von Frauen festzuhalten. In Athen wurde von Frauen erwartet, dass sie heirateten, Kinder bekamen und den Haushalt führten. Außerhalb dieser Rollen hatten sie nur sehr wenig Unabhängigkeit. Selbst die antike Medizin war – ob gewollt oder nicht – ausgesprochen frauenfeindlich: Manche Ärzte glaubten, dass die Gebärmutter im Körper umherwandern könne, wenn eine Frau nicht heiratete und Kinder gebar, was zu allerlei körperlichen und psychischen Erkrankungen führen könnte.

Die Mythen zeigen vor allem, wie sich Frauen nach der Meinung von Männern verhalten sollten. Es spiegeln sich darin die gesellschaftlichen Machtverhältnisse wider. Penelopes Geschichte zum Beispiel sagt etwas über die Verletzlichkeit von Frauen aus. Während Odysseus fort ist, ziehen über 100 Freier in ihr Haus ein, verbrauchen die Ressourcen ihres Haushalts und setzen sie unter Druck, wieder zu heiraten. Obwohl sie eine Königin ist, hat sie kaum Macht, sie loszuwerden. Das verweist auf die männliche Autorität über den Haushalt im antiken Griechenland, insbesondere bei der Kontrolle weiblicher Sexualität und der Sicherung legitimer Nachkommen.

Medea verkörpert die Gefahren einer Frau, die sich weigert, an ihrem Platz zu bleiben. Was jedoch oft vergessen worden ist: Medea wird anfangs von den Göttern unter einen mächtigen Liebeszauber gestellt, damit sie sich überhaupt in Jason verliebt und ihm hilft, das Goldene Vlies zu erlangen. Ihre Gefühle für ihn waren nicht ihre eigenen, und ihre Geschichte beginnt damit, dass sie zum Wohle eines Mannes manipuliert wird. Dennoch erinnern wir uns an sie als gefährliche, mörderische Frau.

Ich finde Demeter und Persephone besonders interessant, weil die homerische Hymne an Demeter die weibliche Perspektive ungewöhnlich stark in den Mittelpunkt stellt. Im Zentrum steht Demeters Trauer, nachdem ihre Tochter entführt und zur Heirat gezwungen wurde – etwas, das den Frauen der Antike, die bei ihrer eigenen Heirat kaum ein Mitspracherecht hatten, nur allzu vertraut gewesen sein dürfte. Der Text gibt außerdem Einblicke in den Alltag von Frauen, etwa in Mutterschaft, Kinderbetreuung und die Erfahrungen älterer Frauen. Einige Forscherinnen haben sogar vermutet, dass die Hymne von einer Frau verfasst worden sein könnte.

So ziemlich überall! Wir haben immer noch die perfekte Hausfrau, die Femme fatale, die Verrückte und die Hexe, insbesondere in Film, Fernsehen und Popkultur. Die negativen Stereotype werden auch gegen echte Frauen eingesetzt, vor allem in der Politik. Hillary Clinton beispielsweise wurde als Medusa dargestellt, was suggeriert, dass mächtige Frauen irgendwie monströs oder bedrohlich seien. Andere Figuren stehen für Erfahrungen, die Frauen bis heute machen. Kassandra etwa war dazu verflucht, stets die Wahrheit zu sagen, ohne dass ihr jemand glaubte. Das ist etwas, worin sich gerade im Zusammenhang mit sexueller Gewalt und der #MeToo-Bewegung viele Frauen wiedererkennen.

Ja, besonders interessant ist, wie Frauen und queere Menschen sich diese Archetypen angeeignet haben. Die Amazonen sollten ursprünglich alles verkörpern, was an Frauen falsch war, die sich nicht an die griechischen Geschlechterrollen hielten. Doch sie wurden zu Symbolen weiblicher Stärke und Unabhängigkeit, insbesondere für Suffragetten und später für lesbische Feministinnen. In ähnlicher Weise werden Hexen als Symbole weiblicher Selbstermächtigung gebraucht. Auch Medusa ist zu einem Symbol feministischer Wut geworden. In Ovids Version des Mythos wird sie von Neptun vergewaltigt und anschließend von Minerva bestraft: Die Strafe trifft also das Opfer statt des Täters. Heute wird sie daher oft eher als Überlebende denn als Monster interpretiert.

…

# Apple bewirbt iPhone 18 Pro Max: „Längste Akkulaufzeit aller Zeiten“ › Macerkopf

Apple hat einen neuen Werbespot veröffentlicht, der die besonders lange Akkulaufzeit des iPhone 18 Pro Max auf unterhaltsame Weise in Szene setzt. Im Mittelpunkt steht ein einäugiges Spielzeugwesen, ein sogenannter Zyklop, das zum Leben erwacht und das Smartphone entdeckt.

## Bis zu 30 Stunden typische Nutzung

Neugierig probiert die kleine Figur zahlreiche Funktionen des iPhones aus. Sie fotografiert, spielt Spiele, nutzt verschiedene Apps, hört Musik, nimmt Videos auf, führt Telefonate und verfolgt TV-Inhalte. Schließlich verwendet der Zyklop sogar die Taschenlampe des iPhones, um Schattenspiele zu erzeugen.

Während das Spielzeug immer mehr Energie verbraucht und schließlich erschöpft einschläft, zeigt sich die Ausdauer des Apple-Smartphones: Das iPhone 18 Pro Max verfügt zu diesem Zeitpunkt noch über rund 50 Prozent Akkuladung.

Apple bewirbt das iPhone 18 Pro Max (hier unser iPhone 18 Pro Max Test ) als iPhone mit der bislang längsten Akkulaufzeit. Bei typischer Nutzung sollen bis zu 30 Stunden möglich sein. Beim Streaming von Videos gibt Apple eine Laufzeit von bis zu 40 Stunden an. Werden heruntergeladene Videos abgespielt, sollen sogar bis zu 45 Stunden erreichbar sein.

Die Angabe zur typischen Nutzung basiert auf einem durchschnittlichen Nutzungsmuster, das unter anderem Nachrichten, Fotos, Musik, soziale Netzwerke, Streaming, Spiele, Internetnutzung und Navigation berücksichtigt. Ein unabhängiger Test attestierte dem iPhone 18 Pro Max im Vergleich zur Konkurrenz die beste Akkulaufzeit.

Sie sehen gerade einen Platzhalterinhalt von YouTube . Um auf den eigentlichen Inhalt zuzugreifen, klicken Sie auf die Schaltfläche unten. Bitte beachten Sie, dass dabei Daten an Drittanbieter weitergegeben werden.

Mehr Informationen Inhalt entsperren Erforderlichen Service akzeptieren und Inhalte entsperren

Mit dem neuen Spot setzt Apple erneut auf eine humorvolle Werbeidee, um eine technische Produkteigenschaft emotional zu vermitteln. Statt die Akkuleistung mit Messwerten oder technischen Daten zu erklären, lässt das Unternehmen ein kleines Spielzeug an der Ausdauer des iPhones scheitern.

items.body: A computer chip is rarely bigger than a postage stamp but can have 100 kilometers (62 miles) of copper wire inside, connecting its billions of transistors and other components. The smallest of these wires are almost impossibly slim, over 1,000 times thinner than a human hair. One challenge for chipmakers is that copper wires become too resistive and less efficient at these dimensions—requiring a search for alternative materials, especially as computing demand skyrockets in the age of AI.

items.body:
Did the German news website NiUS publish a video reporting 113 infant deaths in cold Lower Saxony maternity wards due to low gas storage levels? No, that's not true: This is a made-up news story falsely presented with the "NiUS Live" logo of a real news outlet. A search of the NiUS website did not return any results matching the topic of this story.

The claim appeared in [a post](https://x.com/ColoursOfWorld1/status/2125498691188662394) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170318/https://x.com/ColoursOfWorld1/status/2125498691188662394) ) by the @ColoursOfWorld1 account on X on Nov. 25, 2026, with a video 1 minute, 17 seconds long bearing the logo *NiUS Live*. The post caption read:

> 113 infant deaths in Lower Saxony. Delivery rooms at 13°C. Care homes at 11°C. Gas storage: Rehden at 22.6%, Wolfersberg at 0%. Merz says: "We're growing again." The cost of this "growth" is paid in lives. [#EnergyCrisis](https://x.com/hashtag/EnergyCrisis?src=hashtag_click) [#Merz](https://x.com/hashtag/Merz?src=hashtag_click)

This is what a screenshot of the video in the post looked like at the time of publication:

*(Image source: post by @ColoursOfWorld1 on X.)*

The text in the screenshot above reads:

> Wer trägt die Schuld am Tod von Babys in Geburtskliniken?

Google translated this:

> Who is to blame for the deaths of babies in maternity wards?

Lead Stories searched [Google News](https://news.google.com/search?q=113%20S%C3%A4uglingstode%20in%20Niedersachsen&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125172414/https://news.google.com/search?q=113%20S%C3%A4uglingstode%20in%20Niedersachsen&hl=en-US&gl=US&ceid=US%3Aen) ) and [Yahoo News](https://search.yahoo.com/news/search;_ylt=A2RRt2akGQdr7gIAM3XQtDMD;_?fr=uh3_news_web&fr2=sb-top&p=113+S%C3%A4uglingstode+in+Niedersachsen.+) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125182143/https://search.yahoo.com/news/search;_ylt=A2RRt2akGQdr7gIAM3XQtDMD;_?fr=uh3_news_web&fr2=sb-top&p=113+S%C3%A4uglingstode+in+Niedersachsen.+) ) for the German phrase "113 Säuglingstode in Niedersachsen" (113 infant deaths in Lower Saxony). There were no relevant results returned. Lead Stories also searched the website of nius.de for the number [113](https://nius.de/search?term=113) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125170718/https://nius.de/search?term=113) ) and the [headline phrase](https://nius.de/search?term=Wer+trägt+die+Schuld+am+Tod+von+Babys+in+Geburtskliniken), "Wer trägt die Schuld am Tod von Babys in Geburtskliniken" (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125192304/https://nius.de/search?term=Wer%20tr%C3%A4gt%20die%20Schuld%20am%20Tod%20von%20Babys%20in%20Geburtskliniken) ) -- there were no results for either search. Lead Stories used the [advanced search](https://x.com/search?q=Wer%20tr%C3%A4gt%20die%20Schuld%20am%20Tod%20von%20Babys%20in%20Geburtskliniken%20(from%3Aniusde_)&f=top&src=typed_query) function on X to see if the headline had been posted by NiUS: "Wer trägt die Schuld am Tod von Babys in Geburtskliniken (from:niusde_)".

There were no relevant results at the time of publication (pictured below).

*(Image source: Advanced search on X.)*

The Gnida Project, a research group that tracks what it describes as Russian-backed disinformation campaigns, has attributed this fake news story to Storm-1516 (embedded below). In a Nov. 25, 2026, [post on X](https://x.com/gnidaproject/status/2125548431468835260) (archived [↗ web.archive.org](https://web.archive.org/web/20261125172702/https://x.com/gnidaproject/status/2125548431468835260) ) they wrote:

> The latest Storm-1516 disinformation campaign is targeting Germany. The campaign promotes a false narrative that hospitals in Germany are not receiving enough heating in relation to the alleged low gas storage levels.

> The latest Storm-1516 disinformation campaign is targeting Germany. The campaign promotes a false narrative that hospitals in Germany are not receiving enough heating in relation to the alleged low gas storage levels.
> -- gnida project (@gnidaproject) [November 25, 2026](https://x.com/gnidaproject/status/2125548431468835260?ref_src=twsrc%5Etfw)

Lead Stories reached out to NiUS for comment and will update this article if a reply is received.

# Google Gemini API: File Slicing und nativer Office-Support gestartet

## Google Gemini API: File Slicing und nativer Office-Support gestartet

von Carsten Knobloch 25. Nov. 2026 | 0

Google erweitert die Gemini-API um File Slicing und unterstützt jetzt auch nativ den Upload von Microsoft-Office- und OpenDocument-Formaten. Bedeutet: Entwickler müssen große PDFs, Dokumente, Präsentationen, Tabellen, Audio-Dateien oder Videos nicht mehr komplett durch die KI schicken, sondern können gezielt einzelne Ausschnitte prüfen lassen.

Bisher mussten Anwendungen große Dateien oft vorab lokal mit Werkzeugen wie LibreOffice oder ffmpeg zerlegen, um Kosten und Datenmüll im Griff zu behalten. Mit dem Update erledigt die Gemini-API das direkt auf den Servern von Google. Eine Datei wird einmalig hochgeladen und lässt sich danach über mehrere Anfragen hinweg immer wieder ansprechen. Abgerechnet werden dabei nur die Tokens für die Bereiche, die das Modell tatsächlich anschaut, so Google in der Dokumentation.
